## Issue batch B22 — Remove Silences' notes name the clip (`silence2_proof.py` 4, 8c, 8d and 8e, `silence2_probe.py` 17; #107)

`SilenceDetector.Outcome` answered by MEDIA only, so with one file behind two
clips neither the sheet nor `detect_silence` could say which clip the mix made
quiet or which fell back to the level test, and the sheet hedged ("…, unless
the mix already turns it down far enough to be quiet."). This section
supersedes the road map 4 sections' hedge wording above: those rows now read
the per-clip sentences below.

**The toll first.** `Span`, `Scope`, `Mode`, `Settings` and `Outcome` moved
verbatim into `app/Sources/SilenceDetector+Vocabulary.swift` (586 → 435 and
163 lines), gated alone: `make typecheck` 0 errors, 4 warnings, tsc clean;
`inventory.py --check` 5/5.

**The change.** `Outcome.answers` is one `VoiceAnswer` per scoped voice
(clip, media, span, judged by level, waiting on the cache its quiet test reads
after the floor, proposed by its OWN overlap test). `detect_silence` gains
`judged_by_level_clips` (always) and `proposed_by_mix_clips` (when non-empty);
its note names clips by id ("Clip 3 is proposed only where the mix already
turns it down far enough to be quiet. Clips 3, 4 hold no voice and were judged
by level."). The sheet names them by label, "<clip name> at <timecode>"
("toneA.m4a at 00:00:00:00 holds no voice and is judged by level.";
"…, except where the mix already turns {labelA} down far enough to be
quiet.", where the probe checks the label but does not print it).

**Rows.**

- `silence2_proof.py` 4 (voice then tone): a new row, `judged_by_level_clips`
  is the tone clip alone. 4 (waveform withheld, tone): the two note rows end
  "Clip {clip} holds no voice and was judged by level." and "Clip {clip} is
  proposed only where …". 8c ducked: "Clip {clip} holds spans that ARE
  proposed here: the mix turns it down …". 8d (c): its last sentence is
  "Clip {tone clip} holds no voice and was judged by level." B21's swap
  mutant's anchor (`\(proposedHere.count)`) is untouched (`grep -c` 1) and the
  mixed ending it swaps is byte-identical; the swap mutant was not re-run.
- `silence2_proof.py` 8e (new, `twoclips_part`): `tone.wav` laid at 0 (a) and
  12 s (b), nothing selected, caches landed, a ducked to 0.001, the waveform
  removed, one `detect_silence`. (a) CONTROL both clips in scope, the media a
  waveform waiter judged by level, no voice waiter; (b) CONTROL a span inside
  a, none overlapping b; (c) `judged_by_level_clips == [a, b]`; (d)
  `proposed_by_mix_clips == [a]`; (e) the whole note.
- `silence2_probe.py` 17 (`ducked`): a second clip of `tone.wav` at 12 s, the
  clip at 0 ducked; the two hedge rows are replaced by rows requiring the
  waveform sentence naming the ducked clip's label, "2 clips hold no voice and
  are judged by level: {labelA}, {labelB}.", no "unless the mix", and "What is
  proposed inside {labelA} is quiet in the MIX …" with both caches gone. 17's
  "stays plain" row now requires the plain sentence and no "except where the
  mix". `main` catches ffmpeg's decode failure: 12d then SKIPs, naming "ffmpeg
  could not decode clean.wav on this host" and the error, where the probe used
  to die at its first line on this host.

**Mutant M1** (rule R's words): in a `tree_copy` copy
(`work/b22/m1`), the anchor line
`let inside = spans.contains { $0.start < voice.end && voice.segment.start < $0.end }`
(count 1) replaced by `let inside = proposed.contains(voice.segment.media)` —
membership in the set `proposedMedia` is built from — then the copy's
`make app`, its own instance, and the tree's `silence2_proof.py`.

## Issue batch B23 — the canvas editor lays text out as the render does, the inspector's name fields (`text_break_proof.py`, `text_break_probe.swift`, `name_field_proof.py`, `name_field_probe.swift`, `graphics_inspector_proof.py --mutant name-height`; #117 #171)

Both probes are compiled AS `main.swift` over `app/Sources` minus the app's
`main.swift` on `harness/build.sh`'s swiftc line, `-D REELCUT_DEV_TOOLS`
included; a probe that will not build is a scored FAILURE, a probe that dies
scores every row it did not write as FAIL, and each calls only what HEAD
`2e78a25` already had. `--baseline <commit>` builds the same probe over
`git archive <commit> app/Sources` and follows rule R (1 caught, 0 survived,
2 not performed; a failed control or an unwritten row is not performed).

- **`text_break_proof.py` (#117, spec §11 K-3)** — the app's own editor
  window over one-clip packages in `SourceSans3-SemiBold` (left, fixed width,
  except E9). A line START is the UTF-16 offset a line begins at: the
  editor's from `textLayoutManager` (TextKit 2; reading `layoutManager` would
  switch the view to TextKit 1), the render's from `LayerRenderers.layout(for:)`.
  E0 the font (control); E1 plain, ≥ 3 lines and equal starts (controls); E2
  `tracking` 24; E3 E2 after " and more" by key events, against the applied
  render; E4 E2 after the window shrinks to 75 % (the canvas scale moving
  > 5 %, control); E5 `line_spacing` 1.8, starts (control) and each line
  pitch within 1 pt of the render's × scale; E6 size 12 at video scale 0.6
  (4.71 pt in view, control), the frame the box + 2 px (control), starts;
  E7 `case: upper` holds `content` before and after "ab" (control); E8 E2
  emptied by Delete over the select-all (control), "Wrap" typed (control),
  the storage's font size and kern at index 0 the render's × scale, starts;
  E9 auto-sized, centred, one line at `tracking` 24, one line in the render
  (control) and the editor, and after " again" (the render a control). E6's
  width is 260 px on purpose: the editor's frame is aligned to backing
  pixels (#36's rule), so its wrap width can stand up to ~1 px wider than the
  render's; at 240 px a line with its next word measured 240.04 px and the
  editor kept the word. E6 is at video scale 0.6 because at scale 1 the view
  size (7.84 pt) was too near the old 8 pt clamp to break differently.
- **`name_field_proof.py` (#171, spec §11 SH-3)** — the probe, once per look
  (`NSApp.appearance` set first), over an `InspectorNameField` "HHHH" at
  170 × `DS.controlHeight`, a header-configured one (12 semibold, 20 pt) and
  an `OptionFieldControl`, captured by `cacheDisplay` over an opaque host
  (PNGs in `work/name-field/probe/`). N1 border and interior pixels equal the
  number field's within 2; N2 the cap ink's centre within 1 pt of the
  field's; N3 + 20 pt moves the ink 10 ± 0.5; N4 N3 for the header field; N5
  N2 and N3 with the field editor attached, on the first glyph's columns;
  N6 the ink 7–11 pt from the left edge; N7 one height constraint of its own
  (Auto Layout's `NSContentSizeLayoutConstraint` left out), `DS.controlHeight`;
  N8 (control) the layout dump finds no problem with "Director of
  Photography"; N9 it finds a wider name `truncated`. N8 and N9 read the field
  not editable, because an editable `NSTextField` reports no intrinsic width
  (measured -1); N9 is not a control, because the unfixed field's cell
  wrapped. Then the harness (1440 × 1500, the tree's build) renders a text
  clip with one marker: H1/H2 the Document tab, H3/H4 the Clip tab with the
  clip selected, light and dark, twice each, byte-identical (kept in
  `work/name-field/`).
- **`graphics_inspector_proof.py --mutant name-height`** supersedes B8's

**The fix.** #117: `LayerRenderers.textAttributes(_:scale:)` is split out of
`attributedString` (every value at scale 1 is today's), and
`PreviewCanvasView+TextEditFrame`'s `fitTextEditor` styles the editor from it
at `video.scale × canvasScale` before sizing it (`styleTextEditor`: the
editor's ink, no stroke, the storage rewritten only when its font, kern or
paragraph style differ, never over marked text or an empty storage). A pure
move of `refitTextEditor`, `editorFont` and `alignment` out of the frozen
`PreviewCanvasView.swift` came first, gated alone. #171: `InspectorNameField`
moved out of `InspectorPane.swift` (a pure move, gated alone) into
`InspectorNameField.swift`, then drawn by `InspectorNameFieldCell`; it pins
its own `DS.controlHeight`, so `stringRow` and `markerRow` stopped re-pinning.

(`-D REELCUT_DEV_TOOLS`), with `Compositor.metal` built beside it, and calls

it. Gestures go through `beginGesture` / `continueGesture` / `endGesture`;

rows (F0 D0 D1 M1 M2 M3 X0 X1 T1 G1 C1 C2 L1, then the harness photos H1/H2
on a plain run) are in the runner's docstring. A travel of dv view points is

per pixel), tolerance 0.01 px. `--baseline <commit>` builds the same probe
over `git archive <commit> app/Sources`, and `--mutant` edits a copy. Both

the inspector. Every inspector claim is measured over the inspector's pixels
only, and two new rows require "one vs none" and "two vs one" to change
the preview (the outlines, #85).

against the stand-in (`--rehearse`) or the real API (`--live --cap D`),

forwarded POST's parsed body and reply bytes kept in memory, never on disk).

the shipped threshold stays 300 000. The fixture burns ids to 71 first

bounds; K (live) the key in no file. A refused POST fails its turn's rows

## Issue batch B29 — media caches and relink: a silent file's stale caches, the sheet's refused sentences, the pass sleeper (`remaining_proof.py` 1i, `cache_pass_probe.py` W1, `relink_sheet_probe.py`; #180 items 1–3, #178 items 6–7)

- **#180.1** — a pass for a media with no audio (a relink to a silent
  file) withdraws the old file's peaks and speech `.bin` and markers while
  the pass is current, and posts the change (`peaks` with no `replaced`,
  `speech` with it). `remaining_proof.py` 1i asserts the withdrawal over MCP
  again (the section above).
- **#180.2** — the missing-media sheet's Relink alerts each refused
  relink's sentence, in order, after its one grouped commit and the cache
  pass (spec §11 #63, amended). The Media tab's Relink… keeps the fold's
  beep and CI-10 strip.
- **#178.6** — `awaitPass` cancels its 30 s sleeper once the bounded wait
  returns, and returns it.

`relink_sheet_probe.py [--sources DIR] [--mutant NAME] [--only IDS]` builds
`relink_sheet_probe.swift` over `--sources` (`cache_pass_probe.py`'s swiftc
line) and runs it once, killed at a 120 s wall, over copies of
`media/toneA.m4a`, `toneB.m4a` and `A.mov` under
`work/relink-sheet/<tree|mutant-NAME>/`. The fixture is an untitled
`ProjectDocument` with three video media whose `path` names no file and
whose `bookmark` is nil, in a window whose content is a bare host view
controller. Exits follow rule R, as `cache_pass_probe.py`'s.

| Row | Passes when |
|---|---|
| B0 | the probe builds |
| C1 | CONTROL, run first: `relinkMedia` with no flag (the Media tab's door) of the first media to toneA posts exactly one `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with that relink's own refusal sentence, and no sheet attaches within 3 s |
| S0 | CONTROL: `missingMedia` is 3 (the detail prints each `mediaURL(for:)`) |
| S1 | after `chose` toneA, toneB and A.mov and a `performClick` on the sheet's Relink, the third media's path is the A.mov copy's within 20 s and the other two are unchanged; after the alerts the undo action is "Relink Media", and one undo restores the third's path and leaves `canUndo` false |
| S2 | an alert sheet attaches holding the first media's sentence; after `endSheet` a second holding the second's; after that none within 2 s |
| S3 | when the first alert attached, the project already held the third media's new path |
| S4 | after S1's undo, a second sheet chooses a garbage `.png` (ImageIO refuses it; no ffmpeg question) for the first media, toneA for the second and A.mov for the third: an alert holding "Could not read unreadable.png.", held until the commit lands and 0.5 s more, then after `endSheet` a second holding the second media's sentence, none after that within 2 s, and the third media relinked |

`cache_pass_probe.py`'s **W1**: a previous pass that ends in 0.3 s, waited
for bounded through `MediaImporter.awaitPass`; the wait returns within 5 s,
a sleeper is answered, and it ends within 2 s of the return.

| `--mutant` | Edit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `relink_sheet_probe.py --mutant sheet-silent` | `applyClicked` calls `document.relinkMedia(choices)` | S2 FAIL ("alert 1 false … texts []"), caught, exit 1 |
| `relink_sheet_probe.py --mutant unreadable-at-once` | the sheet's unreadable file `present(error)`ed at once instead of held for the chain | S4 FAIL ("alerts 1 … alert 2 holds media 3's sentence false"), caught, exit 1 |
| `cache_pass_probe.py --mutant no-cancel-sleeper` | `sleeper?.cancel()` → `_ = sleeper` | W1 FAIL ("a sleeper answered: true; it ended never after the return"), caught, exit 1 |
| by hand: the two no-audio arms of `peaks` and `speech` put back to their HEAD lines, the app built in a `tree_copy` copy and launched on 4852 | `guard media.hasAudio, media.duration > 0 else { return true }` / `… else { return }` | `remaining_proof.py 4852`: 77/80, exit 1 — 1i's peaks pair GONE, speech pair GONE, and all four ABSENT ("across 1 samples … peaks.bin: None → (…)") |

**Measured while building it**: `present(_:)` called once per refusal,
back to back, shows ONE alert. AppKit builds the second error alert and
never attaches it while the first is up, nor after the first ends
(`relink_sheet_probe.py` on that tree: 5/6, S2 "alert 2 false"). So each
next alert is asked for from the last one's `didPresent` callback
(`presentRelinkRefusals` in `ProjectDocument+Import.swift`). The sheet's
unreadable-file errors go through the same chain, ahead of the refusals: one
presented at once was still up when the chain asked for its first alert, and
that alert was dropped (the `unreadable-at-once` mutant). An S4 that ended
the first alert at once scored that mutant as SURVIVED, since the alert was
gone before the commit, so S4 holds it as a person would.

## Issue batch B30 — a held scope change that fails or empties (`scope_playhead_probe.py` S13–S15 and `all_at`'s `at_least`, `e2_proof.py` §4 (b)'s message; #185 items 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6)

- **The fix** (`Playback.swift`, `Playback+Scope.swift`;
  `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` "### Playback" has the long form). A held
  scope change whose rebuild FAILED left the outgoing item on the player under
  the new container's time; one whose new plan was EMPTY dropped the item but
  left `restoring` set with the time never heard. Both now drop the item and
  call `Playback.endHoldWithoutItem()`, which clears `holding`, `isSeeking`,
  `restoring` and `pendingSeek` and reports the kept time once through
  `startSeek`'s no-item branch. The failure arm also clears `built` and
  `builtPlanJSON`, so the next update rebuilds. Outside a hold both arms are
  unchanged. #185 item 3 (`set_scope` answering before the player lands) is
  left as it is.
- **The move, gated alone first**: `seekAfterRebuild(to:)` to
  `Playback+Scope.swift`, with the eight members it writes widened from
  `private` (`make typecheck`: 0 errors, 4 warnings, tsc clean). `wc -l
  app/Sources/Playback.swift`: 595 → 581 after the move, 590 at the end;
  `Playback+Scope.swift` 35.
- **The seam** — `Playback.rebuildHop`'s block now takes an error: `nil` is the
  build's own result, an error is delivered to `finishRebuild` as the build's
  failure. `scope_playhead_probe.swift` holds it as `Hold.block`; `release(_:)`
  runs it with `nil`, `failHeld(_:)` with `ProbeFault()`. `playback.onError` is
  replaced by a recorder (`rebuildErrors`) that never forwards: the editor's
  `NSApp.presentError` is app-modal and would stall the probe. The probe no
  longer builds over `work/b21/prefix-sources/`; the pre-fix reference is now
  `work/b30/prefix-sources/` (the tree with the seam and the rows, without the
  fix).
- **`all_at(log, t, at_least=0)`** (#185 item 4): an empty log used to pass
  every "every tick t" row. S1, S2, S3, S5, S6 and S7 now require at least one
  report (S6's `len(...) > 0` folded in); S10 and S11 keep 0, because a restore
  resting on the tick last reported is silent by design. `kept_at(s, t)`: the
  document's playhead, the timeline's and `Playback.currentTime` all `t`, for a
  row with no item on the player.
- **Rows** (after S12, in this order): **S13 [B]** timeline 3 s, held, enter
  N, the held build FAILS → no item, `builtPlanJSON` nil, `restoring` false,
  one error recorded, scope 1, kept at 1 s, log non-empty and every tick 1 s.
  **S14 [B]** then, inside N, an opacity edit on N's clips → an item again, the
  built plan N's, scope 1, rests at 1 s, every tick 1 s. **S15 [B]** timeline 3
  s, held, enter N, N's clips deleted with the block still held (N's plan
  empties), the held block run (a stale generation, discarded) → no item,
  `restoring` false, scope 1, kept at 1 s, log non-empty and every tick 1 s.
- **`e2_proof.py`** (#185 item 5): `clockwise_text(top_x, left_y)` is §4 row
  (b)'s message, each clause "is" or "is NOT" as measured; the row's predicate
  is unchanged.
- **`Playback+Meter.swift`'s header** (#185 item 6) names `meterInterval`.

## Issue batch B31 — graphics residue: the props-cap pin, the texture-side pin, G11's settle (`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs`, `graphics_proof.py` G11; #183 items 1–4)

- **`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs`** — `one_max_props_in_the_engine_and_the_core`
  compares the engine's now-exported `graphic::MAX_PROPS` with the core's
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS`; `the_app_texture_side_holds_the_largest_graphic` reads
  `app/Sources/LayerRenderers.swift`'s `static let maxTextureSide = <integer>`
  line at run time and holds it at or above `graphic::MAX_SIDE` (a G-8 error
  card is drawn through `bitmap(_:)` at the graphic's own size).
- **`graphics_proof.py`** — G11's 0.5 s settle is gone: after the 17 writes,
  `m00.js` is rewritten in place and `await_revisions` (the new shared helper,
  polling `get_graphic` every 0.2 s) waits up to 5 s for its revision, which
  proves a pass ran after every write event from the setup; then 0.3 s (one
  `GraphicStore.coalesceInterval` and margin) for the pass the settle's own
  write may leave pending. The control's poll uses the same helper.
  `store-uncapped` still fails G11.

  overlap (`.grows`, `.shrinks`), both overlaps read off the snapshots (spec
  §11 D4-6). `changeLine` prints `clip <id> gains a <s> s <kind>`, `clip
  <id>'s <kind> grows to <s> s` or `clip <id>'s <kind> shrinks to <s> s`. A
  transition at the same overlap before and after is not named.

## Include Reelcut windows — the recorder panel's checkbox and `record_screen`'s `include_reelcut_windows` (`recording_probe.py` section 14, 1f, 5d, 7c; `recording_proof.py` sections 0 and 1; spec §11 recording.md)

The rows are `recording_probe.py`'s (a probe compiled from `app/Sources`
over `harness/build.sh`'s swiftc line; its docstring holds each row in
full), and three are `recording_proof.py`'s.

- **Section 14 `exclusion`** — its own process, the six older
  `ReelcutRecording…` keys pinned and the seventh,
  `ReelcutRecordingIncludeReelcutWindows`, not pinned and removed from
  `UserDefaults.standard` before and after the rows. **X1**:
  `RecordingExclusion.make` over four cases — off with a bundle → that
  bundle, no window; off with no bundle → nothing; on with the panel's
  window 42 → no bundle, window 42; on with no panel window (the tool's
  door) → nothing. **X2**: the shared panel with the key absent → the
  checkbox off and the choice false; titled "Include Reelcut windows", its
  target the panel, its action `controlChanged:`, in the panel's window; on
  and `controlChanged` → the key true and the choice true; off with no
  action, then `restoreChoices()` → on. **X3**: disabled at
  `.countdown(3)` and `.recording`, enabled at `.idle`. **X4**, structural
  over the comment-stripped sources: `presentPicker` sets
  `excludedBundleIDs` / `excludedWindowIDs` from `recordingExclusion(` and
  never names `Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier`; `startRecording` passes
  `excluding:`, built from `choice.includeReelcutWindows` above the
  `shareableContent` closure; `recordScreen` reads
  `"include_reelcut_windows"` above `screenRecordingGranted` and passes it to
  `RecordingExclusion.make(` (with `panelWindowID: nil`) and to
  `RecordingChoice(`; `filter`'s display arm holds `excludingApplications:`
  and `excludingWindows:`.
- **1f, 5d, 7c** — `RecordingChoice()`'s `includeReelcutWindows` is false;
  the panel's row reads false and its title; `out["keys"]` lists seven, the
  harness pins all seven by value (`"ReelcutRecordingIncludeReelcutWindows":
  false`, a literal) and `screens.py`'s `PINS` carries it for P2;
  `record_screen` declares `include_reelcut_windows`. Every probe mode that
  pins the six keys pins the seventh false.
- **`recording_proof.py`** — `include_reelcut_windows` is declared
  `boolean` (eleven arguments plus `project`), `{"seconds": 2,
  "include_reelcut_windows": "yes"}` → `include_reelcut_windows must be true
  or false.`, and the ORDER row with `"display": 99` added answers the same
  sentence.
- What no script reads is the PICTURE: a granted-tier pixel measurement of
  Reelcut's windows in a recording is out of scope, and REC-11 in
  `docs/manual-checks.md` is the person's check.

## Issue #127 — parallel graphic export (`graphics_prefetch_proof.py`)

An `ExportWriter` export rasterizes its graphics ahead on worker threads
(`app/Sources/GraphicPrefetch.swift`, spec §11 G-26); the compositor stays
the one writer and uses a worker's raster only on a pool miss whose texture
key matches its own. The proof launches two owned instances one after the
other, each on a scratch socket (OFF with `-ReelcutGraphicPrefetchOff YES`, ON without),
logs under `work/graphics-prefetch/`, every child under
`graphics_spike/bounded.py`. Its fixture, made over MCP and saved: a 30 fps
canvas; `heavy` (moving gradient, `feGaussianBlur`, an `<image>` of the
imported `red.png`, bundled-font text) on two overlapping clips with
different props; `static`; `stepped` (`Math.floor(frame / 2)`); each 4 s,
over a 5 s shape clip. Movies are `prores_422`, compared with
`video_configuration_proof.py`'s `same_movie`.

- **S0** CONTROL: two OFF exports masked-equal. **S1** the ON export
  masked-equal to S0's. **S2** ON's `[reelcut] graphic prefetch: …` line:
  hits > 0 and ≥ 95% of hits + mismatched + missed. **S3** no such line in
  OFF's log. **S4** ON, `throw10` beside a heavy clip: `export` errors naming
  "throw10" and "frame 10", no file, the session's line within 10 s.
- **S5** `graphics_prefetch_probe.swift` (built like
  `graphics_proof.build_pin_probe` into `work/graphics-prefetch-probe`), off
  then on, `prores_422` at 25 fps from tick 140 000: both succeed with `fps`
  [25, 1] and `start` 144 000, the movies masked-equal, ON's stderr line at
  ≥ 95% hits. The frame-rate override has no MCP argument, so this is the
  one row through `ExportWriter.videoComposition`'s variant.
- **S6** MEASURED: OFF and ON wall seconds. **Z1** no `Reelcut: ` in any log.
- `--mutant worker-frame-plus-one` (the worker asks `svg` for `frame + 1`)
  must fail S2; `--mutant unguarded` (that plus `take`'s texture-key
  comparison removed) must fail S1. Exit 0 caught, 1 survived, 2 control
  not performed.
- `--bench PACKAGE [--preset h264]` exports a COPY under `work/` OFF then ON
  and prints the load average before each, both walls, ON's line and the

## Issue batch B39 — the harness playhead (`harness_playhead_proof.py` P0–P3, S0, S1 and `--mutant`, `e2_chrome.py` (b), `clip_inspector4_probe.swift` R7, `phase5_chrome.py` §3b; #198)

- **The fix** (`harness/main.swift`): straight after the 12-turn settle,
  under `if playheadSeconds != 0`, the harness calls
  `controller.setPlayhead(Ticks(playheadSeconds * 600_000))` and then
  `Harness.applySelectAction(selectActionSpec, to: document, refreshing:
  controller)`. Playback's first `report(0)` had written
  `document.playhead = 0` during the settle (B32, #188 item 5), so every
  render asked for at a non-zero playhead was taken at 0. The new
  `Harness.applySelectAction` (inside `#if !HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD`) maps
  the index through `ActionBands.ordered`, calls `document.selectAction`
  and then `controller?.viewStateDidChange()`. It never calls the editor's
  `selectAction(_:)`, because that moves the playhead to the action's end.
  The early site now calls it with `refreshing: nil`. `setPlayhead` stays
  outside the `#if`, because both reference trees (`65d43ae^`, `a4c476f^`)
  have it. A caller at playhead 0 runs exactly the code it ran before. The
  header's `selectAction` paragraph is reworded in its own seven lines, so
  `pinDefaults` is still at `:291`.
- **`harness_playhead_proof.py`** builds one fixture, `hp.reelcut`: a grey
  6 s card with action A (id 3, 0.5–1.5 s, opacity 0.5) and action B (id 4,
  2.0–3.5 s, x 100). It makes five renders (dark, 1440 × 862, size 1, Clip),
  as (select, playhead, action): `zero` (−1, 0), `two-a` and `two-b` (−1, 2),
  `inside` (0, 3, "0") and `outside` (0, 5, "0"). The rows:
  - P0 (control): `two-a` and `two-b` are byte-identical.
  - P1: `zero` and `two-a` differ.
  - P2: below y 598 every changed pixel is within 6 pt of x 132 or x 216,
    and each of those columns holds at least one.
  - P3: the toolbar (y < 44) holds changed pixels.
  - S0 (control): in `outside`, A's lane sample (193, 653) differs from B's
    (277, 653).
  - S1: `inside`'s two samples equal `outside`'s.

  The mutants (rule R: 1 caught, 0 survived, 2 not performed) each strip one
  anchor line from a copy, `work/harness-playhead/mutant-<name>/main.swift`,
  which is compiled last on `build.sh`'s swiftc line. `no-late-playhead`
  strips the `setPlayhead` line and must fail P1, P2 and P3. `no-reselect`
  strips the late `applySelectAction` line and must fail S1.
- **The three strengthened rows.** Each was made to FAIL on HEAD before the
  fix, and each passes after it. Each site is judged by whether its row's
  CLAIM held at 0 s:
  - **`e2_chrome.py` (b)**, "…with the playhead inside an ACTION it writes
    the clip's BASE motion". `PROBE_SOURCE`'s `editor()` now calls
    `controller.setPlayhead(playhead)` after its spin. (b)'s answer carries
    `playhead`, and the row requires `TICKS // 2`. On HEAD it printed
    `playhead 0`. **Its claim was unaffected**: the `action` and
    `zero-action` fixtures' only action spans [0, 1 s), so 0 s was inside an
    action as well. The playhead term is a regression guard on the playhead
    holding. It does not mean the row passed vacuously before. `zeroAction`
    (0.5 s) goes through the same `editor()` and is unaffected for the same
    reason.
  - **`clip_inspector4_probe.swift` R7** (affected). `setPlayhead(at(1.0))`
    and `spin(0.3)` now run after the editor opens. `held = document.playhead`
    is read before `addActionAtPlayheadCommand()`, and the first R7 check
    requires `held == at(1.0)`. On HEAD it FAILED with `playhead 0`. The
    refusal it heard then was `action 3 on clip 2 already runs from 300000
    to 900000 ticks, and two actions on one clip may not overlap`. That was
    a new action at 0 s overlapping action 3, not Add Action inside action
    1's span: `chrome`'s first action starts at 0.5 s, so 0 s is outside
    every span.
  - **`phase5_chrome.py` §3b's first check** (affected). It now scores
    `moved`, the pixels outside the bar that differ between `now-a` and
    `now-shifted` (one build). Before, it compared `was-a`, from another
    build, which differs everywhere whether or not the playhead moved. On
    HEAD it FAILED with `0 px outside the bar against now-a`, while the
    `was-a` diff still printed 299136 px outside the bar. After the fix it
    is 1146 px. The `was-a` diff, its print and the second check are
    unchanged.
- **The survey.**

## Issue batch B42 — proof-runner and recorder residue (`makefile_env_proof.py`'s sweep and `--no-sweep`, five runners' call-time defaults, the `--baseline` label, `recording_probe.py` F8–F10 and three mutants, `recording_proof.py`'s PCM sentence; #191, #193)

- **`makefile_env_proof.py`'s sweep (#191 item 1).** `bounded.run` kills
  the copy's `make app` process group at `--wall`, but what `xcodebuild`'s
  build service starts (`swift-frontend` among them) is in other groups.
  After `make app` returns, `sweep(root, since)` SIGKILLs every process
  whose cwd or command line lies under the copy. It rescans every second
  until two scans in a row find none or 30 s pass. `copy_processes` takes
  one `ps -A -ww -o pid=,ppid=,etime=,command=` scan and `lsof`'s cwds. It
  never selects by name. It spares this process and its whole `ppid` chain,
  and any process whose `etime` exceeds the time since `make app` began
  plus 2 s. The new row is "no process whose cwd or command line lies
  under the copy outlives its `make app`". `--no-sweep` scores that row on
  one scan taken before any kill.
- **Call-time defaults (#191 item 2).** `build_probe(sources=None,
  probe_dir=None)` in `playback_audio_proof.py`,
  `video_configuration_proof.py` (new global `PROBE_DIR`) and
  `export_cancel_proof.py` (new global `SOURCES`), B28's shape.
  `mixed_audio_probe.make_media(directory=None)` and
  `capture_spike/inventory.py`'s `grep_sites`, `line_of`, `_file_lines`,
  `enclosing_func`, `resolve` and `check` (`sources=None` / `root=None`)
  read `WORK` / `SOURCES` / `ROOT` when called. Explicit callers are
  unchanged.
- **The `--baseline` label (#191 item 3).** `name_field_proof.py` and
  `text_break_proof.py` print `baseline <commit>: the control could not be
  performed — <why>`, not `mutant baseline: …`.
- **The recorder (#193).** `ScreenRecorder.finishingDidBeginNotification`
  is posted by `beginFinishing` once the state is `.finishing`, just before
  `stopCapture`. `RecordingToolChrome.show` observes it and calls
  `freeze()`, so File ▸ Stop Recording over a tool's paused recording keeps
  the item's pause glyph and frozen time (manual check REC-8 step 7).
  `beginCountdown()` clears a stale `resumeProblem`. `recording_proof.py`'s
  PCM row names ffmpeg's cause through `pcm_failure(silent, loud)`.

The age rule's slack is 2 s on top of `ps`'s whole-second `etime`, and the
proof's own work before `make app` takes about 0.2 s. So a process started
less than about 3 s before the proof runs is not spared by age. A sleeper
started 2 s before was killed (PIDs 49595 and 50375 in that run's kill
list), while the shell still survived through the ancestor rule.


## Issue batch B44 — `close_project`, held-path refusals, the caption name rule (`close_project_proof.py`, `remaining_probe.py` 1e and 1f, `assistant_lane_proof.py --mutant close-ask-first`; #40, #43)

- **`close_project {discard?}` (#40, spec §11 #40).** File ▸ Close over MCP
  (`AgentServer+Project.swift`'s `closeProject`, on main): a window with a
  sheet attached is refused first, then unsaved changes unless `discard:
  true`; it closes through `ProjectDocument.close()` and writes nothing.
  `new_project {path}` and `save_project {path}` refuse a path another open
  document holds (`documentHolding`, `refuseHeldPath`), `new_project` before
  it creates anything; a save to the document's own file stays a plain save
  (#138). The assistant never sees the tool (AI-7, amended): a `.withheld`
  row in `AssistantToolTable.swift`.
- **The caption name rule (#43, spec §11 #43).** `export_captions` writes
  `AgentServer.captionDestinationURL(path, format:)`, which replaces only
  `CaptionExporter.knownExtensions` — the panel's rule — so `chart.png` is
  `chart.png.srt` both ways. The other tools keep `replaceableExtensions`.
- **Counts.** 86 product tools (`op_argument_proof.py`), twenty-seven
  app-state tools (`phase9_proof.py`, `recording_proof.py`,
  `recording_probe.py`'s `APP_STATE_TOOLS`).

`close_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]` needs a fresh Release instance.
T1 parity log; K1 schema; C1 sixty `new_project` → `close_project` cycles;
C2 every closed path refused by `get_project`, no editor window left,
`open_project` with no `already_open`; C3 threads after C1 under before plus
64; D1 the unsaved refusal's exact sentence; D2 `discard: true` and the disk;
H1 the sheet refusal (`perform_menu_item ["File", "Export…"]`, then
`cancel_sheet`); S3 (control, run first) a save to A's own path; S1 and S2
the held-path sentence for `save_project` (two spellings) and `new_project`;
E1 `export_captions {path: …/chart.png}`. D1 and D2 run behind an autosave
guard that retries a marker at a fresh `at` when `get_project` already reads
`unsaved_changes: false`, printing `<ID> retry <n>: autosave landed`.

## Issue batch B51 — one alert queue per document, the composer's menu-tool undo (relink_sheet_probe.py A1–A5, menu_undo_probe.py; #195, #184 item 2)

- **#195** — every `ProjectDocument.present(_:)` goes through one
  per-document queue (`ProjectDocument+Alerts.swift`, `DocumentAlertQueue`):
  one alert sheet at a time, each asked for a main-queue turn after the last
  one's `didPresent` or the window's last `didEndSheetNotification`, and
  only while no sheet is attached; with no window, app-modal at once. B29's
  `presentRelinkRefusals` chain is gone: both relink doors `present` an
  unreadable file at once, and the commit `present`s each refusal in order.
  Item 4 (the `RelinkRefusalsLeft` leak on close) falls out — nothing is
  retained through `contextInfo` any more; no row.
- **#184 item 2** — `UIMenu.perform` opens no eager document undo group
  when the target's own `undoManager` is not the document's: the Assistant
  composer, and every field editor, which answers its own
  `NSCellUndoManager` (M1). Such a target's text undo lands on its own
  manager, so a document group round its Cut or Paste could only be empty
  and clear redo; a target whose manager IS the document's is unchanged
  (`v2_menu.py` U1–U3). That covers the vetoed field too (V1). On a
  `ProjectDocument` such a target's action still runs in
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered`, so a document edit committed during it (a
  `controlTextDidChange` commit) is one step and leaves no implicit group
  open (F1, added by the review's finding 1).

`relink_sheet_probe.py` gains five rows after S4 (its wall is now 240 s). An
"alert" is an attached sheet that is not a relink sheet, A4's bare sheet or
A5's blocker, and has not been seen already.

| Row | Passes when |
|---|---|
| A1 | (#195.1) `importMedia` of two garbage `.png`s: an alert holding "Could not read unreadable-1.png." within 20 s, held until the completion has run and 0.5 s more; after `endSheet` one holding "…unreadable-2.png." within 10 s; none more within 2 s |

## Issue batch B52a — the ×1000 speed spike (`speed_spike/`; #190 part 1)

**A historical measurement, not a check: never run it for an ordinary
change.** It builds two hour-long movies (~18 GB) and a full run takes about
95 minutes. It runs only with `--remeasure` (otherwise it exits 2, not
performed), and only to re-measure the speed or audio ceilings: #212, or a
change to `SPEED_MAX` / `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`. A change to speed code is checked
by B52b's `speed_limits_probe.py` below. The numbers here are from 2026-10-01
and were taken without `--remeasure`, which was added afterwards.

### What ran

`speed_spike/speed_spike.py` (the runner) and `speed_spike/speed_probe.swift`
(an in-process instrument compiled as `main.swift` over every other
`app/Sources` file, `-O -whole-module-optimization`, with `Fonts`,
`Blank.mp4` and a `default.metallib` beside it). The probe CALLS the app's
`ReelProject.applying`, `MediaImporter.waitForProbe`, `CompositionBuilder`
(`build`, `fill`, `audioParameters`), `Playback.previewComposition`,
`LevelMeterTrack.mix`, `ReelExport.settings` and `Exporter`; it mirrors only
`Playback`'s private player and item lines (`Playback.swift:138-139`,
`:432-444`, plus `player.volume = 0` and an `AVPlayerItemVideoOutput`) and
`ExporterLoudness`'s private float mix output and its reader range. It links a
SCRATCH core: B0 copied `core/` and `graphic/` to
`work/speed_spike/tree/` and `diff -ru` printed exactly one changed line,
`-pub(crate) const SPEED_MAX: f64 = 10.0;` / `+… = 1000.0;`. No product file
changed; no app instance was launched and no MCP call was made.

**The source is a looped real recording, not an hour recorded for the
spike.** Recording the owner's screen for an hour captures whatever the owner
is doing, unasked. So `loop` is the recorder's own bitstream — `Screen
Recording 2026-09-24 at 11.33.28.mov` (118.230 s), the longest `.mov` in
`~/Movies/Reelcut Recordings/` — looped with `-stream_loop 30 … -c copy -t
3600` and muxed with its own microphone file, `… (Microphone).m4a`, also
`-c copy`. A dense 118 s recording looped is also the harder decode test than
an idle screen, which the recorder writes as sparse VFR. `loopv` is the same
file's video stream alone (`-map 0:v:0 -c copy`), so a video failure can be
told from an audio one. The owner's files were only read.

| Row | Printed |
|---|---|
| H0 | Mac14,6 · Apple M2 Max · macOS 26.5.1 · load { 6.90 9.64 16.48 } · other MacOS/Reelcut PIDs 1 |
| S.loop | 3600.110 s · hevc/hvc1 2560x1440 · r 60000/1001 avg 10432100/360011 · 104321 packets, 1766 keyframes · 8901965257 bytes · audio aac 48000 Hz 1 ch 3600.000000 s |
| S.loopv | the same video facts · 8840368552 bytes · audio none |
| B0 | exactly the SPEED_MAX line; cargo rc 0 (49 s on the first build) |
| B1 | metallib + probe built in 100 s (-O -wmo) |

**The host was shared.** Other sessions loaded the machine throughout; the
1-minute load printed beside the timed rows ran from 5.16 to 68.38. Every
timed row prints its own load; the timings below are this host's under that
load, not a quiet machine's.

The timeline is built through the ops: `set_canvas` to the first media's
probed size and rate — 2560x1440 @ [28977, 1000], the recorder's VFR average
— `add_media`, then per pass `add_clip` at the cursor and `set_speed`. ×1 and
×10 are CONTROLS, trimmed to 30 s; at ×120 one pass (the hour once) and at
×1000 nine passes (nine hours of source in 32.301 s).

### Audio: the time-pitch limit

Each A row puts one segment of r × 2 s of source into 2 s through the app's
`fill` and `audioParameters`, reads it through a float mix output, and counts
only the frames inside [0, 2 s) (the mix output hands back whole buffers:
98304 read for 96000 at ×2). `works` = completed, frames within ±1 %, RMS
within 6 dB of the same fixture and algorithm at ×1, and (sine,
spectral/time_domain) frequency within ±5 % of ×1. `speed_spike.py`,
`full.log`:

| Rates | spectral (keep pitch) | time_domain | off (varispeed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ×1–×24 | 96000 frames; speech RMS -19.11 → -21.87 dB; sine 1000.0 → 986.0 Hz | 96000 frames | 96000 frames |
| ×31, ×32 | **the reader never returns: expired at the 300 s bound**, both fixtures | 96000 frames; sine 966.0 / 979.2 Hz | 96000 frames |
| ×33, ×40, ×48, ×64, ×120, ×1000 | reader completed, **0 frames** | completed, 0 frames | completed, 0 frames |

| Row | L |
|---|---|
| L.speech.spectral | 24 (first failure ×31: reader expired) |
| L.speech.time_domain | 32 (first failure ×33: frames 0) |
| L.speech.off | 32 (first failure ×33: frames 0) |
| L.sine.spectral | 24 (first failure ×31: reader expired) |
| L.sine.time_domain | 32 (first failure ×33: frames 0) |
| L.sine.off | CONTROL (Nyquist: varispeed puts the 1 kHz tone at 1000·r Hz, 24 kHz at ×24) 16 (first failure ×24: RMS -38.76 vs r=1 -24.09) |

A.noise.spectral.1 (CONTROL): 96000 frames, RMS -21.44 dB, flatness 0.1067.
Speech under varispeed stays at RMS -19.48 to -19.62 dB through ×32 while its
flatness rises from 0.0254 to 0.6518 — sound, increasingly noise-like.
`grep -n "1/32"` in the MacOSX26.2 SDK's `AVAudioProcessingSettings.h`
printed lines 37, 41 and 45, "Variable rate from 1/32 to 32." for all three
algorithms: confirmed, except that spectral stops at ×24 here, not ×32 — at
×31 and ×32 it does not fail, it HANGS.

**The product path** (X rows: `speech_2100` at ×r, keep pitch `k` or not
`v`, trimmed to 2 s, exported `audio_m4a`):

| Row | Outcome |
|---|---|
| X.k.1 / X.v.1 (CONTROL) | success in 0.5 / 0.4 s, file 2.048 s, RMS -19.11 dB |
| X.k.32 | **deadline in 540.0 s** — the keep-pitch export hangs |
| X.v.32 | success in 0.4 s, file 2.048 s, RMS -20.31 dB, flatness 0.1989 |
| X.k.33, X.k.120, X.k.1000, X.v.33, X.v.120, X.v.1000 | failure in 0.3–0.7 s: "The operation could not be completed" |

So above ×32 a clip's audio makes an audio-only export FAIL and a movie
export silently LOSE its audio track (E120.loop), and at ×31–×32 with keep
pitch the export never finishes.

"with audio … copes" export lines read the video only: E120.loop's file has

### Back to the owner

**STOP: the preview cannot cope at ×1000.** On the video-only hour, P1000
delivered 14 of 936 frames, the clock held for 30.285 s (31.780 s with the
microphone track), and 32.301 s of timeline took 62.592 s of wall time to
reach its end. #190 says that goes back to the owner rather than an agent
choosing a smaller ceiling, so this batch proposes none. At ×120 the preview
copes (841 of 869 frames, a 3.445 s stall) and the export copes (157.0 s for
30 s, no black). The ×1000 export was not measured to the end in the final
run; the earlier complete run took 1624.5 s with audio and 1480.5 s without
for 32.301 s of timeline.

Whatever ceiling the owner chooses, the audio measurements stand on their
own and B52b needs them: no time-pitch algorithm produces anything above
×32 (`L.speech.time_domain` and `L.speech.off` = 32), spectral — what keep
pitch sets — stops at ×24 and HANGS at ×31 and ×32 (`L.speech.spectral` =
24), and the product's exports already show it: keep pitch at ×32 never
finishes, any audio above ×32 fails an audio-only export and silently drops a
movie's audio track. A ceiling above ×24 therefore needs B52b's audio rule —
above the measured `L.speech.<mode>` for the clip's pitch mode (×24 with keep
pitch, ×32 without) the clip's audio leaves the composition plan — before the
ceiling moves.

## Issue batch B52b — the ×1000 speed build (`speed_limits_probe`; #190 part 2)

Run `speed_limits_probe.py` (about 3 minutes, small generated sources) only
when a change touches the speed range or the audio ceiling, how `evaluate.rs`
assigns or places audio, `CompositionBuilder`'s audio parameters, or the
export's loudness pass. It never needs the B52a spike's hour-long movies.

### What it proves

A clip's speed runs ×0.1–×1000, and above ×12, in both pitch modes, the plan
leaves the clip's audio out (spec §11 #190). `speed_limits_probe.py` (the
runner) and `speed_limits_probe.swift` (compiled as `main.swift` over every
other `app/Sources` file on `speed_spike.py`'s `build_probe` line) call the
app's own `ReelSpeed.limits`, `SpeedSheetController`'s statics,
`VideoPane.silentAudioNote`, `ReelProject.applying`, `ReelExport.settings`
and `Exporter`. No app instance and no MCP call. Every child runs through
`graphics_spike/bounded.py`; every export has a 120 s deadline (runner bound
180 s) and must FINISH. The fixtures are generated: `tone_180.mov` and
`tone_600.mov`, 320x180 testsrc2 with a 200 Hz sine. "Sound" is an RMS
≥ −40 dB; "nothing" is an audio stream that ends by 2.05 s or a peak
≤ −80 dB after it.

**Why ×12, not B52a's ×24/×32.** The h264 export's loudness pass
("Measuring loudness…") never finished, in the probe's export mode:

| Shape (on `tone_180.mov`) | ×12 | ×14 | ×15 | ×16 | ×20 | ×24 | ×32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| keep pitch, the clip alone | 2.8 s | 3.4 s | stall | stall (also 600 s, and trimmed to 2 s) | stall | stall | — |
| varispeed, the clip alone | 2.4 s | — | — | 3.8 s (600 s: 7.7 s) | stall | stall | stall |
| after a 2 s ×1 clip, keep pitch | 2.9 s | — | — | 2.8 s | — | 3.3 s | — |
| after a 2 s ×1 clip, varispeed | 2.5 s | — | — | 2.7 s | — | 2.3 s | stall (5 of 5) |

"Stall" is a 45–120 s deadline with the export still measuring loudness. B52a's
own binary stalls the same way at ×24 alone in both modes. The owner chose
×12, a margin below both stalls; B52a's mixer limits are background only.

## Issue batch B53 — the paused playhead's late reports and the clip tag refreshed in place (`playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1/twice·2, `clip_inspector5_probe` D2 and `clip_inspector_probe` S1 trails, `clip_inspector7_proof.py` T4 and `--mutant tag-frozen`; #204, #209)

- **What was measured first (step 1, the tree at `c39efca`).** D2's "selected after the
  drop" row and S1's "a moveClip that slides a span…" row now carry a report trail
  in their detail: the editor's `playback.onTimeChanged` is wrapped, and every tick
  it carries is logged as `<t> seeking <isSeeking> player <player tick>`, then
  forwarded. One build of each proof (37/37, 39/39), then each probe binary rerun 8
  times off it:
  - **D2 failed 6 of 8** (runs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8), every one with the same trail:
    `selected 4, playhead 2.5000 s; reports: 1.5000 s seeking true player 1.5000 s;
    2.5000 s seeking true player 2.5000 s`. While the seek to 2.5 s was in flight
    the observer delivered 1.5 s (the action's end before the drag, a superseded
    seek), the document took it, and the entry rule then walked 1.5 s → 2.5 s
    into action 4. The two passing runs had an empty trail.
  - **S1 failed 1 of 8** (run 3): `clip time under the playhead -600000, selected
    nil; reports: 2.5000 s seeking true player 2.5000 s; 0.0000 s seeking false
    player 0.0000 s`. The other seven heard 2.5 s once or twice. The trail cannot
    say whether that 0 came from the observer or from a seek's landing.
- **The forced order (step 2).** `playhead_echo_probe.swift`'s `twice` scenario asks
  `setPlayhead(2 s)` then `setPlayhead(0.5 s)` from 1 s in ONE run-loop turn.
  `twice·1` [B] (at least one report, every one 0.5 s) FAILED 3 of 3 on the
  unfixed tree with the log `[1200000, 300000]`; `twice·2` (a CONTROL: the
  document, the timeline and the player rest at 0.5 s) passed 3 of 3. The pure
  move (step 3, `onMain` to `Playback+Step.swift`) scored the same: 21/22,
  `twice·1` alone failing with `[1200000, 300000]`.
- **The fix** (`Playback.swift`, 590 → 579 lines after the move, 587 after the
  fix): while `player.rate == 0`, `timeAdvanced` hears a tick only when it equals
  `currentTime` (where the player is or is seeking to) and differs from
  `reported`; while playing nothing changed. `seekFinished` ends every seek the same
  way: `restoring = false`, and the rest is reported once when it differs from
  `reported`, an asked seek as well as a restore.
- **Runs after the fix:**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `make typecheck` (after the move, and after the fix) | exit 0, 0 errors, the 4 baseline warnings, tsc clean |
| `make app` | BUILD SUCCEEDED |
| `playhead_echo_probe.py` | 23/23; `twice·1` log `[300000]`; `pause·1` ok |
| `playhead_echo_probe.py --sources work/b53/head/app/Sources` (HEAD) | 21/22 before `pause·1` was added; `twice·1` FAILS, `[1200000, 300000]` |
| `playhead_echo_probe.py`, the guard hand-tightened to `if player.rate == 0 { return }` (restored after) | 21/23; `pause·1` FAILS (document 1010036, player 1022677), `short·1` FAILS |
| `scope_playhead_probe.py` | 16/16 |
| `harness_playhead_proof.py` | 6/6 |
| `clip_inspector5_proof.py` | 37/37 |
| `clip_inspector_proof.py` | 39/39 |
| `clip_inspector5_probe` × 8 | 0 failing rows in all 8; D2's trail empty (2) or `2.5000 s seeking true player 2.5000 s` (6) |
| `clip_inspector_probe` × 8 | 0 failing rows in all 8; S1's trail empty (1) or `2.5000 s seeking true player 2.5000 s` (7) |
| `clip_inspector7_proof.py` | 16/16, T4 included |
| `--mutant tag-frozen` / `tag-hidden` / `tag-always` | MUTANT PASS: T4 / T1, T4 / T2, T4 |

  The echo probe, HEAD against the fix (every other row passes on both):

| Row | HEAD | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `twice·1` [B] | FAIL `[1200000, 300000]` | ok `[300000]` |
| `pause·1` | (added after this run) | ok |
| the other 21 | ok | ok |

- **`pause·1`** (a CONTROL, added at review): after play·1, `pause()` and a 0.5 s
  spin, rate 0, the document, the timeline and the player tick agree and the
  log's last report is the player tick. It covers the one paused transition no
  seek follows, a user's pause mid-play: the paused guard must not drop the
  pause's own callback. It has teeth: with the guard hand-tightened to
  `if player.rate == 0 { return }` it FAILS with the document on the last
  playing tick (1010036) and the player at 1022677 (`short·1` fails too).
- **S1 is not proven fixed.** It failed 1 of 8 before and 0 of 8 after, which is
  weak evidence at that rate. If that 0 came from a restore's landing with the
  player really at 0, the new guard would not drop it.
- **T4** (#209 item 2): one `ClipPane` with action 10 selected, then the action
  cleared and reselected, each followed by `binding.invalidate()` and
  `pane.refresh()`. The tag is read through `walk(pane)`, never `clipTags` or
  `sections`, which rebuild. It needs exactly one tag each time, the SAME
  instance, hidden false, true, false. The run reads `tags 1, same true` three
  times, hidden `false; true; false`. `tag-frozen` (the first `refresh()` decides
  for good) fails T4 alone. `tag-hidden` and `tag-always` now name T4 beside T1
  and T2. CT-7 in `docs/manual-checks.md` drops its "clip" tag step.

## Issue batch B54 — P15 measures in the shipped faces, and a capped live proof that the API accepts tool-result clearing (`assistant_tab_proof.py` P15 and `--mutant no-plex`; `assistant_clearing_proof.py` X0–X4, H, K and `--mutant clearing-off`; #207, #208)

- **P15's faces (#207).** `assistant_tab_probe.swift`'s `registerShippedFonts`
  runs once, before the mode dispatch, for every mode. It registers every
  `.ttf` and `.otf` in `--fonts <dir>` for the process, which replaces the
  `--badge` branch's own loop. `rows_p` now passes `--fonts app/Resources/Fonts`
  (`FONTS`, which `row_p14` uses too). P15 also needs the label's face to be
  `IBMPlexMono-Regular`, `--fonts` given, and the shipped
  `IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf` registered. Registered means the call answered
  true, or false with `kCTFontManagerErrorAlreadyRegistered` (105). The
  detail starts `face … (wanted IBMPlexMono-Regular) …; fonts …;
  IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf registered …; font file …`. The file is reported and
  not scored, because Plex Mono is also installed in `/Library/Fonts` on this
  host. The default run printed `face IBMPlexMono-Regular (wanted
  IBMPlexMono-Regular) true; fonts …/app/Resources/Fonts;
  IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf registered true; font file
  …/app/Resources/Fonts/IBMPlexMono-Regular.ttf`.
- **P9, P12 and P13 in Source Sans 3.** The default run now has Source Sans 3
  registered (the host has only `SourceSansPro-*`), so these rows measured in
  the shipped face for the first time. All three passed, and none was
  repinned.
- **`--mutant no-plex`** (`MUTANTS`, `Theme.swift:129`): `DS.mono`'s regular
  face is named `NoSuchFace-Regular`, so it takes its real fallback,
  `.monospacedSystemFont`. P15 FAILED on the face guard alone: `face
  .AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced-Regular (wanted IBMPlexMono-Regular) false;
  … font file none`. Every fit, ladder, tooltip and width check in its detail
  still passed. Without the face guard, the fallback face would have passed P15.
- **The clearing proof (#208, spec §11 AI-20).** `assistant_clearing_proof.py`
  (port 4886, `work/assistant_clearing/`) launches one Release app with
  `-ReelcutAssistantAutoCompact NO -ReelcutAssistantClearToolResults YES`. It
  points the app at `ClearingRelay`, a subclass of
  `assistant_prompt_eval.Relay`, and sends two turns through `assistant_send`
  without `pane`: "Add a marker called Alpha at 1 second." and "Add a marker
  called Beta at 2 seconds." The rows are listed in its docstring.
  - **The relay lowers the forwarded `max_tokens` to 8,000.** The helper always
    asks for 32,000 (`agent/src/main.ts`). Spec §11 P-6 reserves each POST at
    the body's bytes / 3 at $20/MTok plus `max_tokens` at $50/MTok. A helper
    body of about 227 KB therefore reserves about $3.17, and under `--cap 3`
    the relay would refuse every POST unchanged. At 8,000 the worst case is
    about $1.91 (the rehearsal's H printed a worst POST of $1.9270).
  - **X3 proves that the rewrite is the only change to turn A's bodies.** It
    compares each body as the app sent it (`relay.sent`) with the body
    forwarded (`relay.exchanges`). The rehearsal printed, for both turn-A
    POSTs, `max_tokens 32000 → 8000, keys that differ ['max_tokens'], the rest
    identical True`.
  - **Turn B carries a lowered edit.** On turn B the relay also replaces
    `context_management.edits` with `[LOWERED_EDIT]` (trigger 1,000 input
    tokens, keep 1 tool use, no `clear_at_least`). This is the only way $3 can
    show the API clearing, because the shipped trigger is 150,000 tokens. X4
    SKIPs, naming the API's message, if the API refuses that edit with a 400.
- **`anthropic_fake.py`.** A reply may carry `"context_management"`. It is
  copied to the final `message_delta` (not to `message_start`, and not on a
  `"cut"` reply) and to the non-stream Message. A reply without it keeps its
  bytes. The rehearsal's turn-B reply carries `applied_edits` with one
  `clear_tool_uses_20250919`, and the helper reported it as
  `tool_results_cleared` (`tool_uses` 1, `tokens` 1200).

Run on 2026-10-01, the change over `5293283`:

## Issue batch B57 — sheet sites that bypass the document's alert queue (`sheet_queue_probe.py`; #210)

#210 asked whether the 25 `beginSheetModal(for:)` sites in `app/Sources`,
which attach straight to the editor window rather than through
`ProjectDocument.present(_:)`'s queue (B51), can be asked for while another
sheet is up, and lose or reorder an alert when they are. The batch measured
it before changing anything: **every row passed on the baseline, so no site
is routed.** `DocumentAlertQueue` keeps its B51 shape (no `Entry`, no
`enqueueSheet`), relink's `queue-off` mutant keeps its text, and no
`entry-at-once` mutant is defined. The one app change is three private
methods made internal for the probe, with no behaviour change:
`EditorViewController.frameSaved(_:in:)` (`+SaveFrame`),
`addImageBackground(from:into:in:)` and `placeImageBackground(_:into:in:)`
(`+AddClips`). Every `beginSheetModal` token stays in its function and on
its line; `inventory.py --check` 5/5.

- **`sheet_queue_probe.py [--sources DIR] [--mutant NAME] [--only IDS]`** —
  no instance. `sheet_queue_probe.swift` is built with
  `relink_sheet_probe.py`'s swiftc line and run once in its own process
  under `tools/proof/work/sheet-queue/<tree|mutant-NAME>/`, with a 240 s
  wall. Each row gets a fixture of its own: an untitled `ProjectDocument`,
  with its `EditorViewController` as the content of a 1440×900 window
  (`graphics_menu_probe.swift`'s set-up) whose `NSWindowController` is
  added to the document, so `windowForSheet` is that window. The process
  uses `.prohibited` activation. No media from `tools/proof/media`: the
  probe writes its own garbage `.png` and a valid 4×4 PNG. E1 and E2 are
  `present(_:)` of "probe alert one" and "probe alert two". An attached
  sheet is ended with `endSheet` 0.3 s after it attaches, unless a row
  holds it.
  - **B0** the probe builds.
  - **C0** (CONTROL) `windowForSheet` is the window, no sheet is attached,
    and `addMediaFiles:` validates true.
  - **V1** with E1 attached, each of `exportCaptions: importCaptions:
    addImageBackground: addMediaFiles: consolidateMedia:
    insertGraphicFromFile: addGraphicFont: addGraphicImage:
    insertGraphicTemplate: setTransitionKind: saveFrame: removeTrack:`
    validates false.
  - **P1 / P2** a stand-in `NSOpenPanel` (P1) or `NSSavePanel` (P2) is
    attached, then E1 is presented and waits. The panel is ended with
    `.cancel`. Its completion handler records whether E1 is attached and
    then asks for an `NSAlert` "probe handler". Passes when E1 was not
    attached at the handler, and the handler's alert then E1 are shown in
    that order, with none more within 2 s.
  - **X1** (`ExportSheetController.swift:582`'s shape) a bare sheet is
    presented and dismissed, an `NSSavePanel` sheet is asked for, then E1.
    Passes when nothing but the panel attaches while it is up (1 s), and
    after it ends E1 appears within 2 s, with none more.
  - **S1–S4** E1 is attached, the site is called, E1 is held (2 s for S2,
    1 s for the others), then E2 is presented and E1 is ended. Passes when
    the sheets show [E1], [the site's text], [E2] in that order, with none
    more within 2 s. S1 `frameSaved(.failure(NSError "probe frame"))`
    (`+SaveFrame` :209). S2 `addImageBackground(from: garbage.png)`
    (`+AddClips` :179); the text is what `MediaImporter.probeBlocking`
    throws for the file. S3 `placeImageBackground` of the 4×4 PNG's
    descriptor at `width = 70000` (`+AddClips` :236); the text is what
    `add_media` throws. S4 `consolidateAfterSave(didSave: true)` on
    the document given `fileURL = work/probe.reelcut` and no media
    (`+Consolidate` :67); the text is what `MediaConsolidator.plan` throws.
  - A P1, P2 or X1 panel that does not attach within 3 s is an instrument
    failure (`instrument: panel did not attach within 3 s`), and so is an
    E1 that does not attach within 5 s in V1 or S1–S4. Such a failure is
    never the row's verdict. Exits follow rule R (1 / 0 / 2): a plain
    run's instrument failure is a scored FAIL, exit 1, and a `--mutant`
    run with any instrument failure exits 2.

**The fixture is per row** (the spec had one for the whole run). The first
`--mutant no-sheet-wait` run used one document and printed "S1–S4 fail —
instrument: E1 did not attach within 5 s" with P1, P2 and X1 FAIL, then
"the control could not be performed — instrument failure in S1, S2, S3,
S4", exit 2. P1 had left that document's queue jammed (E1 was dropped while
the handler's alert was up), so no later row's E1 could attach. With a
fresh document per row, each row measures the queue on its own.

## Issue batch B58 — §7.7's import formats re-measured on macOS 26, and the capture spike's three waits (`formats_probe.py`; `capture_spike/` run once; #46, #132)

#46 asked to re-measure §7.7's format list, which was last written for macOS
15. The new probe asks the product's own question,
`MediaImporter.waitForProbe` (AVFoundation, or ImageIO for an image, with
no ffmpeg rewrap), about ffmpeg-made files. §7.7's last paragraph is now
this run's table. For #132, the spike's three bare run-loop waits are now
`ProbeSupport.pump()`, and the spike was run once.

- **`formats_probe.py [--mutant junk-good]`** — no instance. It writes the
  fixtures into `tools/proof/work/formats-probe/fixtures/` with
  `ffmpeg -y -v error`, each 1 s at 128×72 (`testsrc2`, a 440 Hz `sine`), at
  most 60 s each. `heic.heic` comes from `png.png` through `sips`, and
  `junk.mov` is `random.Random(58).randbytes(4096)`. It builds
  `formats_probe.swift` with every `app/Sources/*.swift` except `main.swift`
  on `peaks_probe.py`'s swiftc line (B0, at most 600 s; a failed build is a
  scored FAIL). It then runs the binary once over every fixture it made, at
  most 300 s. The binary prints one `HOST` line
  (`VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported` for AV1, VP9 and HEVC) and one `ROW` line
  per file. The verdicts:
  - `opens`: the probe answered, and so did the first-frame `AVAssetReader`
    read (32BGRA), the first-buffer read (LPCM float32), or the
    `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex`, each bounded at 15 s.
  - `probe-only`: the probe answered and the decode did not.
  - `refused`: the probe threw.
  - `not made`: ffmpeg could not write the fixture.
  - `expired`: the binary's bound ran out before the file's row arrived.

  C1: `mov_h264_aac.mov` opens. C2: `junk.mov` is refused.
  `--mutant junk-good` hands C2 the C1 file. Exit 0 needs B0 and both
  controls. WebP is not made, because this ffmpeg has no libwebp and `sips`
  cannot write webp.

scale. The cause, measured by the batch's design spike on a standalone
composition: an audio-mix input sits at the default 1.0 before its first

frames (25 ms at 48 kHz), starting AT the change. A second format family's
composition track also carried the plan track's ramps up to its own first
segment. `CompositionBuilder.volumeLegs` (`CompositionBuilder+AudioTracks.swift`)
now holds each composition track's envelope at its own first segment's value
from time 0. A gain change on ONE composition track with sound on both sides
still slews; the owner accepted that on 2026-10-01 (spec §11 #87).

  (< −60 dBFS) in its first 25 ms and every window after. The shared hard

## Issue batch B60 — a normalised export gains the float mix and quantises once (`export_gain_proof.py` G0–G5; `phase5_proof.py` 5d; `phase5_chrome.py` 9(d); #86 part 1)

#86 part 1: the write pass decoded the mix to Int16 and applied the
loudness gain to that, so a mix past full scale was clipped before the gain
turned it down, and every normalised sample was rounded twice. Now a
normalised export reads the mix through `ExportAudioGain.floatMixSettings`,
the dictionary the measurement reads. `ExportAudioGain`
(`ExporterAudioGain.swift`) multiplies each buffer by the gain, clips it and
rounds it once into a new 16-bit buffer in the encoders' unchanged format.
An un-normalised export keeps the Int16 decode and its bytes.
`ExportLoudness.mixClipped` is now true only for a hot mix written with no
gain (spec §11 #86). Part 2 (24-bit WAV/AIFF) is not in this batch.

**The file paid first.** `ExporterWriter.swift`'s
`// MARK: - Settings → AVFoundation` section moved verbatim to
`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift` (1098 → 807 lines), with `private` dropped
from the seven members `ExporterWriter.swift` calls. It was gated alone.
The `diff` of the moved lines against HEAD printed nothing. `make
typecheck` gave 0 errors and the 4 baseline warnings, and `make app`
printed BUILD SUCCEEDED. `video_configuration_proof.py` `capture` gave
2/2, and `--mutant keep-frame-duration`, whose patch now targets
`ExporterWriter+Settings.swift`, printed "V7 FAIL" and exited 1, as
expected. After step 2, `ExporterWriter.swift` is 782 lines and
`Loudness.swift` 674 (from 742; `LoudnessInt16Gain` is gone).

- **`export_gain_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock --record <dir> | --against <dir>`**
  (a port before the road map 14 merge) — the caller owns the instance. `--record` runs on the build before the change
  and writes `manifest.json` and every export's decoded PCM into `<dir>`.
  `--against` runs on the build after it and compares. Fixtures are
  `work/fixtures/gain_tone.wav` (L 0.5·sin 440 Hz, R 0.5·sin 660 Hz) and
  `gain_quiet.wav` (0.02), 2 s, 48 kHz stereo s16, both from ffmpeg
  `aevalsrc`. The seven presets with sound are `h264`, `hevc`,
  `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`
  (the video rows at 640 × 360). Each gets these exports: `tone`
  un-normalised twice, `toneoff` (the tone at `volume` 0.9) normalised down
  to −23 LUFS / −1 dBTP, `quiet` (its clip at `volume` 0.9) normalised up
  to −14 / −1, and `hot`
  (the tone at `volume` 4, a +6 dBFS mix) at −14 / −1. One more
  un-normalised `audio_wav` is taken of `hot`. Every export is decoded to
  s16le by ffmpeg, and every project is closed with `close_project`. The
  run takes about 8 s.
  - **G0** (CONTROL), per preset: the two un-normalised exports decode
    identically.
  - **G4**, per preset, the hot normalised export: no decoded sample at
    ±full scale, BS.1770-4 (`phase5_proof.integrated`) within ±0.5 LU of the
    report, and no "clipped" in the summary.
  - **G5**: the hot un-normalised WAV says "clipped" and holds full-scale
    samples.
  - **G1** (`--against`), per preset: the un-normalised decode is
    byte-identical to the reference's. Where G0 failed, it is an instrument
    failure instead.
  - **G2** (down) and **G3** (up) on the LPCM rows: equal length and
    max |Δ| ≤ 1 LSB (down) or ≤ ceil(g/2) + 1 LSB (up). G3 also needs at
    least one differing sample. On the AAC rows the checks are
    |ΔLUFS| ≤ 0.01 and difference RMS ≤ −55 dBFS.

**Measured.** `--record` on the step-1 build gave 8/15, exit 1. G0 passed
7/7, and G5 passed with 128240 full-scale samples. G4 FAILED 7/7, as it
should on the unfixed build: −17.914 / −17.915 LUFS decoded against
−13.995 reported, and the summary ended "measured on the mix, which clipped
at +6.0 dBFS before it was written". `--against` on the step-2 build gave
36/36, exit 0. G4 decoded −13.993 (AAC) / −13.995 (LPCM) LUFS, with 0
full-scale samples and a summary "Peak −13.4 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS". G1 was
byte-identical on all seven presets. With `down` on the 0.9-volume tone
(after review; the reference re-recorded on the same step-1 bundle, again
8/15 with G4 failing 7/7), G2 found 6080 of 192000 samples differing on
each LPCM row, max |Δ| 1 LSB against the bound of 1, and on the AAC rows
|ΔLUFS| 0.0012 and difference RMS −83.0 dBFS (gain −15.46 dB both builds).

**Two departures from the spec, each with its measured figure.**
- **The `quiet` clip, and the tone `down` exports, are at `volume` 0.9.**
  With the spec's fixture at
  volume 1.0, G3 found 0 of 192000 samples differing on every LPCM row,
  and AAC |ΔLUFS| was 0.0000 (gain +20.59 dB both builds). A 16-bit source
  at unity reads as k/32768 exactly in float, and the old path rounded k·g
  the same way the new one does. At 0.9 the mix is off the 16-bit grid
  (gain +21.5 dB). There, 176720 of 192000 samples differ, max |Δ| 6 LSB
  against the bound of 7.
- **The AAC RMS bound is −55 dBFS, not −70.** The step-2 run measured
  −61.3 dBFS on G3's three AAC rows, with |ΔLUFS| 0.0037. The encoder's
  INPUT differed by −79.3 dBFS (the `audio_wav` decodes), but AAC's own
  coding error on that export (the m4a decode against the wav decode of the
  same build) is −58.4 dBFS (−57.9 on the reference). So any change to the
  input reads at about that level, and −70 cannot be met. ΔLUFS ≤ 0.01
  still catches a wrong gain.

**Which references moved.** No reference is committed anywhere, so no
stored file moved. Exported bytes move only for NORMALISED exports, and
only where the mix is off the 16-bit grid or past full scale. A 16-bit
source at unity volume normalised down (−16.37 dB) or up (+20.59 dB) wrote
identical PCM on every preset. The 0.9-volume mix normalised up moved by at
most 6 LSB (G3), and normalised down by at most 1 LSB on 6080 of 192000
samples (G2). The hot normalised mix moved from a clipped −17.91 LUFS to
the reported −14.0. `phase5_proof.py` 90/90: its over-scale rows are
inverted (normalised: no "clipped", the file within ±0.5 LU of the report
at −14.0024 against −14.0023, 0 full-scale samples; un-normalised: "clipped"
and 192480 full-scale samples). `phase5_chrome.py` 82/82: 9(d) adds the
un-normalised hot case.

**Residue.** A gained export has no 16-bit fallback. If the reader ever
refused the float output, a normalised export would fail with "The audio
mix could not be read for export." instead of writing clipped audio. Every
gained export in these runs had its float read accepted, and no proof row
reaches the refusal. A decoded buffer of zero frames is skipped on the gain
path, as the old Int16 kernel passed it through; none was seen in these
runs, so no proof row reaches that skip either.

## Issue batch B62 — a speed change that silences a clip asks first, and an agent's answer says so (`speed_audio_probe.py`; #212)

Since B52b (spec §11 #190) a clip above `audio_max` (×12) has its audio left
out of the plan. #212 asks for a question before a person's edit does that,
and for an agent's answer to name the clips. `SpeedAudioDrop.swift` holds the
crossing (read off the core's trial `applying`, never a rate computed in
Swift), the copy (the owner's option B), and the app's one alert sheet for it
(`ask`); `EditorViewController+SpeedAudio.swift` holds the inspector's door
(`inspectorEdit`, behind `inspector.onEdit`) and the rate stretch's
(`timelineLiveUpdated` / `timelineLiveEnded`); the Speed sheet's Apply asks on
the sheet's own window; `AgentServer.editResult` merges `audio_left_out` /
`audio_note`. A rate stretch that crosses is put back
(`endLiveEdit(_:cancelled: true)`) BEFORE the question, so nothing is live
while it is up. `inventory.py --check` 5/5 with the new
`SpeedAudioDrop.swift` site (`ask`, reached after `showSpeedSheet:`).

## Issue batch B70 — the spec indexes checked, a pending-reverse lead measured, the capture probe as an app (`spec_index_proof.py`; `mixed_audio_proof.py` `pending-first` and `--mutant old-onset`; `capture_spike/` `--bundle-only`, `--route`, `--activation`; #220, #218, #132)

- **#220 — `spec_index_proof.py`, a line of `make test`.** It checks the
  Lines cells in `designs/spec/README.md` and `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md`
  against `wc -l` (the number of newline bytes). The `11-decisions/` folder
  row must read `<N> in <M> files`, where N is every `*.md` in the folder
  summed, its README included. Every link must exist, every spec file must
  have exactly one row, and every subdirectory must have a folder row. A
  problem names the index, the row and both numbers. `--selftest` copies
  `designs/spec` to `work/spec_index/` and runs a CONTROL, which must show
  0 problems, and four mutants, each on a fresh copy, which must show
  exactly one problem naming its row: M1, the `07.6` cell +1; M2, the
  folder cell's N +1; M3, the `deepening.md` cell +1; M4, a new empty
  `zz-unindexed.md`. Recounted at HEAD `4d9b80a` (after B66 and B69):
  `04.3a` 358 → 361, `06b` 348 → 354, `07.6` 42 → 46, `deepening.md`
  556 → 584. The folder cell went from 3065 to 3066 in 13 files, because the
  sentence this batch added to the decisions README is one line.
- **#218 — `mixed_audio_proof.py` `pending-first`.** It sits between
  `missing-first` and `CONTROL same`, on its own session. `aac.m4a` itself
  (not a copy, and never altered) goes at 0 and `pcm.wav` at the AAC clip's
  duration (no gap) on one track, with the WAV muted. **The hold:** the
  session's `cache/reversed` is created as an EMPTY REGULAR FILE, then
  `set_reversed` makes the AAC reversed, then the export runs. **Why it
  holds:** `ReverseCache.existing` finds no file under `cache/reversed/`, so
  the clip is in `ReverseResolution.pending`. The render that
  `ensureReversedMedia` starts reaches `createDirectory(at: cache/reversed)`,
  which throws because a file is there. `ReverseRenderer.run` turns that into
  a failure, and `refusedReverseMedia` never retries it, so the clip stays
  pending whether the job is still running or has failed. A forward read
  would be the loud tone (`mixed`'s row), and a finished reverse would be the
  same tone backwards, so only pending leaves the lead silent. The failed
  render's sheet stays up on that session's window, and the session is never
  saved. There are five rows. Three are CONTROLs: no `missing_media`;
  `cache/reversed` still a regular file after the export; the lead silent
  from 0.25 s to `at − 0.25`. The other two: the WAV silent in its first
  25 ms, and silent from `at + 0.025` to `at + 1.975`. 22 checks.
  `--mutant old-onset` puts back the pre-B61 onset (`git show 16d4934`:
  `family.segments.filter { $0.duration > 0 }.map(\.start).min()`) in a tree
  copy (`tree_copy.make_copy`, `work/mixed-audio-mutant`), with the anchor
  asserted once, and builds it with the copy's own `make app`. It launches
  the copy on its port, with the parity grep of its log required empty, runs
  every row, and terminates only that child. Exit 0 means caught: both
  first-25 ms rows FAIL while all four CONTROL rows pass. Exit 1 means it
  survived, and exit 2 means the control could not be performed.
- **#132 — the capture probe as a LaunchServices app.** Every spike run now
  assembles `work/capture_spike/CaptureProbe.app` after the build (the
  binary, the five resources, an `Info.plist`, an ad-hoc signature), and a
  failed assembly fails B0 as `bundle: <why>`. Modes launch through
  `open -n -W -F --stdout … --stderr … CaptureProbe.app --args <mode> …` by
  default. On expiry, only the PIDs running the bundle's executable are
  killed. `--route direct` is the bare binary, as before. The probe gains
  `ProbeAppDelegate` (no untitled document on launch or reopen), fonts
  through `ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory`, and an `activation` mode
  (`runActivation`, X0) that is not one of `rows.py`'s modes, so a full run
  is still 38 rows with the same digest scheme. `--bundle-only` launches
  nothing. It checks `plutil -lint`, `codesign --verify --strict`, that the
  executable is the built binary, and that every resource is present. The
  executable comparison is made with both signatures removed and
  `__LINKEDIT`'s vmsize zeroed, because `codesign` replaces the linker's
  signature and the removed one had rounded that field (2 bytes differed).
  `--activation` runs the `activation` mode over `direct` (the CONTROL) and
  `bundle`. **A bundle-route run takes keyboard focus** and puts the probe's
  windows in front for its length (about 3 minutes in full), so run it only
  when nobody is typing at the Mac. `--route direct` does not take focus.

Runs on 2026-10-02 over `4d9b80a` plus this batch. The instance for the
first proof ran on 4870, with an empty parity grep.

|---|---|
| `spec_index_proof.py` | before the recount, 131/135, exit 1, with the four cells above named; after it, 135/135, exit 0 |

(`DecoderSupport.decodesFirstFrame`). A file is refused as `undecodable`, in
a sentence naming the codec and with no ffmpeg offer, only when the reader

## Issue batch B73 — WebM and Matroska open by a built-in rewrap (`container_rewrap_probe.py` W1–B3a and X19; `container_import_proof.py` M0–M6; #216 stage 2, phase 1; spec §11 #216-R)

The core indexes a WebM or Matroska file (`rc_container_*`) and
`ContainerRewrap` copies its first video and audio stream, unchanged, into
`~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/Rewrapped/<stem>-<16 hex>.mov` with
`AVAssetWriter`; the import funnel takes that path with no question when
AVFoundation refuses a file that begins with an EBML header.

- **`container_rewrap_probe.py [--mutant NAME]`** — makes its fixtures with
  ffmpeg (640×360 `testsrc2`, 2 s, a 440 Hz sine), builds
  `container_rewrap_probe.swift` with every `app/Sources/*.swift` but
  `main.swift` over the harness's swiftc line (`-D REELCUT_DEV_TOOLS`), and
  calls `ContainerRewrap.rewrap` on each into its own scratch destination
  under `work/container-rewrap-probe/scratch/`, each call on its own thread
  and bounded at 60 s (a copy that has not returned is the row's `hung`).
  Fixtures P1–P19 and rows W*, F*, S*, R7–R10, N11, K12, X19, A13, V15, D16,
  T17/T18, B* are in its docstring.
  Two departures from the design's text, each measured: P15 needs
  `settb=1/1000` and `-enc_time_base:v 1/1000` (without them ffmpeg 9 wrote
  the jittered times back onto 1/30 s and V15's fail-first `retime` row
  failed on the fixture, as it was built to); and the payload rows read the
  written movie through its edit — a passthrough read answers MEDIA times,
  and the writer shifts a B-frame H.264 track's media one frame later so its
  decode times start at 0 — while the audio row compares the whole track in
  order, because AAC cannot be paired by PTS (the writer puts Apple's 2112
  priming samples before its edit where ffmpeg's MKV has 1024). T17/T18,
  added for that reason, hold the sound's place against the picture: an
  impulse at 1.000 s decodes from the copy within 1 ms of where ffmpeg
  decodes it from the source. Each source mutant edits a copy of
  `app/Sources` (`work/container-rewrap-probe/Sources-<mutant>`), its
  `before` text matching exactly once or the run answers 2, and must fail
  exactly the rows `EXPECTED` names; then it prints `MUTANT PASS` and exits 0.
  X19 (review fix, 2026-10-02): `rewrap`'s third seam, `refuseAudioAt`,
  declares one audio packet 4096 bytes longer than its data, which fails the
  writer (-12703) some appends later; P19 is a 20 s file so that lands
  mid-copy (on the 2 s P1 it surfaced only at the finish in one run of
  four). Measured on macOS 26.5.1: a failed writer asks each input again and
  every pending append answers false, so the writer's old unbounded
  `group.wait()` alone did not hang (an ad hoc `bare-unbounded-wait` run
  scored 27/27). The hang needs a pump that never acts on the failure, which
  `deaf-pump` makes (every pump returns without finishing once the writer
  has failed); with the sliced wait it fails nothing, and with the wait also
  put back to one `group.wait()` (`deaf-pump-unbounded-wait`) X19 answers
  `hung` with `p19.partial.mov` left behind.
- **`container_import_proof.py [--mutant ffmpeg-copy]`** (`--port <port>`
  before the road map 14 merge) — launches its own Release instance on a
  scratch socket with `-RCFFmpegImport never` and kills
  only that one; runs over the real `Rewrapped/` and removes only the
  digest names it created there, parent-checked. `render_frame` snaps `t` to
  the canvas grid, so M2 sets the canvas to five times the media's rate to
  put ±0.4 frame on it.

Run on 2026-10-02 over `901bb80` plus this batch's diff, macOS 26.5.1,
Apple M2 Max, `hw_av1 False`; re-run after the review's fixes (X19 added)
the same day. `container_rewrap_probe.py` printed `passed 27/27`, exit 0,
among them X19 "error failed 'Could not copy p19.webm into a movie: The
operation could not be completed.'; scratch []", W1 `('ok', 640, 360, [30, 1], True, True)`, W2

16.9 MB free", A13 "audio 2.033333333333333 s against video 2 s", V15
"retimed False …, samples 60 vs index 60, duration 2.0083333333333333 vs
ffprobe 2.009", T17 and T18 "the impulse decodes at 1 s from the copy, 1.0 s
