## Issue batch B75 — proof-tooling cleanup (`mcp-proxy/tests/stdio.rs`; `project.yml`'s Build Rust Core; `tree_copy.py` T5, `stale_registrations.py`; `agent_socket_proof.py` K14; `e1_proof.py`'s `ReferenceMCP`; `recording_probe.py` `hide-picked-only`; #230 #225 #223 #224 #215 #229)

Proof tooling and one `project.yml` line; no product code changes.

- **#230, `ping_is_answered_while_a_call_is_held`.** Measured first, with
  temporary timings in the old test: under `make test` the copied proxy's
  first line came 0.65, 1.13 and 1.30 s after its spawn, and the ping took
  340, 820 and 990 ms. Run alone, those were 0.31 s and under 0.5 ms. The
  old test slept 300 ms after the spawn and then started the ping's 1 s
  clock, so the clock was running before the proxy was reading stdin. The
  test now sends `initialize` (id 0) and waits for its answer. A new
  `holder` stub signals on a channel when the call reaches it (it replaces
  the sleep), and then the ping is timed against `PING_BOUND`. After the
  rewrite the ping took 0.18, 0.38 and 1.28 ms over three `make test` runs
  (0.07–0.19 ms alone), so `PING_BOUND` stays 1 s and `CALL_HOLD` 3 s. The
  ping mutant (`session.rs`'s `"ping"` arm made `{}`, reverted) fails it
  with "no answer within 1s".
- **#225, a copy's Build Rust Core rebuilt the tree's `core/target`.** Cargo's
  reason (`CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info`) is
  `EnvVarChanged { name: "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET", old_value: None,
  new_value: Some("26.0") }` on rquickjs-sys's build script, which makes
  rquickjs-core, rquickjs, graphic and reelcut-core dirty in turn. The step's
  environment, printed in a scratch `tree_copy` copy, has
  `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=26.0` and `SDKROOT=…/MacOSX26.2.sdk`. CC, CFLAGS,
  HOST_CC and CRATE_CC_NO_DEFAULTS are unset, and the shell sets none of the
  six. Before the fix, that copy's `make app` compiled the five crates in the
  Makefile's `make rust` and again in the Xcode step (11.4 s); Build MCP
  Proxy compiled nothing (0.21 s). The step now runs `env -u
  MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET -u SDKROOT cargo build --release`. After the fix,
  the copy's Build Rust Core finished in 0.05 s and the staticlib's mtime did
  not move.
- **#223, LaunchServices.** `tree_copy.unregister_apps` and `remove_tree`
  (the paragraph in B7's section). The removal sites now go through
  `remove_tree`: the five assistant proofs' `base`, the assistant spike's
  `build_app`, `graphics_prefetch_proof.py`'s and `graphics_proof.py`'s
  `WORK`, `makefile_env_proof.py`'s `WORK`, `mc1_spike.py`'s `ditto`,
  `mcp_proxy_proof.py`'s two, `cloud_spike/local_rows.bundle` (also
  `words_spike/speech_rows.py`'s) and `capture_spike.bundle`. `e1_chrome.py`
  and `phase8_chrome.py` delete no bundle. `tree_copy.py --selftest` adds T5
  (no LaunchServices effect): a fake `.app` under `work/tree_copy/ls/` is
  found, one under an `Intermediates.noindex/` is not, and `remove_tree`
  leaves nothing. `stale_registrations.py` lists what is left. It is dry run
  by default, and its `--selftest` (S1–S3) registers, deletes and
  unregisters one bundle of its own in a `mkdtemp`, with a CONTROL that the
  count outside that folder does not move. The existing stale entries are
  NOT unregistered by this batch.
- **#224, a quit with a call in flight: K14.** M saves a 600 s 1920×1080
  rectangle (C1: `unsaved_changes` false, so no save sheet). One raw
  `POST /mcp` of `export` follows, and 2 s later `select` shows nothing to
  read (C2). Then the quit event: the pid-targeted
  `NSRunningApplication.terminate` that K6 and K7 use, which is an Apple
  event with no activation and no window. The agent's `export` is its own
  `Exporter`, not the export queue, so no "An export is still being
  written" alert can appear. The `waits-for-call` mutant joins a
  `get_project` served on a background thread (async plus a semaphore) in
  `applicationWillTerminate`.
- **#215, the e1 reference.** The reference stays at `1c3e92e` and listens
  on TCP. `mcp.py` gains a `_connection()` hook and stays AF_UNIX only.
  `e1_proof.py`'s `ReferenceMCP` overrides the hook with TCP for the
  reference alone. The second argument is now the reference's LOG, and
  `reference_port` reads its last `listening on` line. The reference is
  launched with `RC_AGENT_PORT=0` (the reference paragraph in "Running one").
  `e1_chrome.py` never reaches an agent server.
- **#229.** `hide-picked-only` now replaces the `hidesForRecording` guard
  with `guard currentChoice().source == .picked else { return }`. Its
  structural kill is 5u in `chrome_pause`. 9c's driven kill is in section 9
  (`granted`), which needs the screen grant and puts the panel on screen, so
  this batch did not run it.

## Road map 14 — the MC1 spike (`mc1_spike/`)

The spike behind MC2's socket and MC3's `reelcut-mcp`: whether an Xcode
script phase can write the catalog snapshot into the bundle before signing,
in Release and Distribution, and the runtime fallback's cost (q1); what a
background `open -n -g` launch costs and shows, cold, warm and quarantined
(q2); whether Claude Code refetches on `notifications/tools/list_changed`,
from its docs and a stdio stub, with no model call (q3); and the socket
path's length and `tiny_http`'s `http_unix` against existing files (q4).
`tools/proof/mc1_spike/README.md` has the rows and the instruments; **the
answers are in `archive/reelcut-roadmap-14.md`'s MC1 record (condensed in `designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`)**. q1 builds only
in a `tree_copy.py` copy (`work/mc1_spike/tree`), which alone gets the
`-RCWriteCatalog` hook and the phase that ad-hoc signs the just-linked
(unsigned: `-no_adhoc_codesign`) executable in place and runs it; q2 launches that copy's Release product from paths
under `work/mc1_spike/` and signals only those pids. The stub
(`mc1_spike/stub_mcp.py`) is the fixture of `docs/manual-checks.md` AC-1 and
AC-2.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/mc1_spike/mc1_spike.py                 # q4, q1, q2, q3, then Z1
python3 tools/proof/mc1_spike/mc1_spike.py --only q4       # a subset; the other rows carry forward
```

## Road map 14 — MC2, the socket (`agent_socket_proof.py`)

The app binds the agent server on a Unix socket at every launch
(`app/Sources/AgentServer+Socket.swift`, spec §11 MC-1, MC-2, MC-6), beside
the TCP listener MC4 removes. The proof launches its own instances one after
another, each a `Popen` it owns with `-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES
-AgentServerEnabled YES` and `RC_AGENT_PORT` = `--port` + k, and every one
but K10's with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` in a `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rcs-")`
folder under `$TMPDIR` (MC1: a path under `work/` can pass macOS's 103
bytes). Logs are `work/agent-socket/<a…g>-<port>.log`; every other child
runs under `graphics_spike/bounded.py`. HTTP over AF_UNIX is a local
`http.client.HTTPConnection` subclass (MC4 moves it to `mcp.py`). Only the
proof's own pids are signalled; a quit is a pid-targeted quit event
(`osascript -l JavaScript`, `NSRunningApplication…terminate`). Nothing under
`~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/` is created, written or unlinked:
K10 only `lstat`s.

- **P1** `agent_socket_probe.swift` (built like
  `export_cancel_proof.build_probe`, Swift sources and the staticlib only,
  into `work/agent-socket/probe/`) prints `AgentServer.socketPlan` for five
  cases: `{}` binds the default; `RC_AGENT_PORT` alone skips with the interim
  rule's reason; port plus socket binds the socket; an empty
  `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` binds the default; a nil default skips with "no
  Application Support folder". A probe that will not build is a FAIL.
- **K0** CONTROL: the scratch path ≤ 103 bytes, under `$TMPDIR`, not under
  the support folder, its folder `0700`. **K1** A logs `listening at <path>`;
  the file is a socket at `0600`. **K2** the raw `tools/list` body is
  byte-equal over the socket and TCP. **K3** a marker added over the socket
  is read back over TCP and one added over TCP over the socket.
- **K4** B at the same path logs `not bound: another instance answers…`, the
  file's dev and ino unchanged, A still answers. **K5** SIGKILL A (B
  stopped): the leftover refuses `connect` (ECONNREFUSED) and C binds over
  it. **K6** the proof unlinks C's file, D binds, C quits within 20 s, and D's
  file keeps its inode and answers (MC1's S7 at the app's quit). **K7** D
  quits within 20 s and its file is gone.
- **K8** a `0755` folder: E logs `not bound` naming `0755`, no file. **K9** a
  regular file at the path: F logs `not bound…not a socket`, bytes unchanged.
- **K10**, run only when P1 is ok: G with `RC_AGENT_PORT` and no
  `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` logs the interim rule, and the default `Agent/` folder and
  `agent.sock` `lstat` the same before the launch and after its quit.
- **Z1** no `Reelcut: ` in any log; **Z2** no proof pid alive.
- `--mutant no-connect-first` (the `connect(2)` replaced by ECONNREFUSED;
  K4 must FAIL) and `--mutant no-mode-check` (the folder-mode statement
  removed; K8 must FAIL) build a `tree_copy.make_copy` copy by its own `make
  app` and run every row on it. `--mutant no-port-rule` (the port arm
  removed; P1 must FAIL) builds and runs ONLY the probe over a copy of
  `app/Sources` — no app is launched, so the person's socket is never at
  risk. Exit 0 caught, 1 survived, 2 control not performed.
- The S7 guards are Rust, which `tree_copy` links rather than copies, so
  their two mutants are made by hand against `cd core && cargo test
  --release --test agent_socket`: `shutdown`'s `is_current` guard removed
  fails `shutting_down_a_listener_whose_file_was_replaced_leaves_the_new_one`,
  `release`'s fails `releasing_a_listener_whose_file_was_replaced_leaves_the_new_one`.

MC4 rewrote this proof (K2, K10 and `no-port-rule` retired with TCP; K11–K13
and four mutants added): its section, "Road map 14 — MC4, TCP goes", has the
rows and the commands. The commands as MC2 ran them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/agent_socket_proof.py --port 4941
python3 tools/proof/agent_socket_proof.py --port 4951 --mutant no-connect-first
python3 tools/proof/agent_socket_proof.py --port 4961 --mutant no-mode-check
python3 tools/proof/agent_socket_proof.py --mutant no-port-rule
```

## Road map 14 — MC3, the proxy (`mcp_proxy_proof.py`)

`reelcut-mcp` (`mcp-proxy/`, spec §11 MC-3, MC-4, MC-6) is the stdio MCP
server bundled as `Contents/Helpers/reelcut-mcp`; `project.yml`'s "Write
Agent Catalog" phase puts its snapshot, `Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`,
in the bundle. The proof `ditto`s the Release app (`--app`) to
`work/mcp-proxy/<run>/Reelcut.app` and drives that copy's proxy over stdin and
stdout, as a client would; the copy is removed at the end unless Z1 finds an
instance of it alive. Every socket is in its own
`tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rcm-")` under `$TMPDIR`; an instance is any pid
`pgrep -f <copy>/Contents/MacOS/Reelcut` prints, the only pids ever signalled
(SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10 s), and "N instances" counts pids new since the row
began. Children run without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`,
`CLAUDECODE` or `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, under `graphics_spike/bounded.py`
where not interactive. Nothing under `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/`
is created, written or unlinked (Z2 only `lstat`s), nothing is registered with
a Claude client, and no model is called.

- **X0** CONTROL: each socket path ≤ 103 bytes, under `$TMPDIR`, not under the
  support folder. **X1** no instance: `initialize` (negotiated version,
  `listChanged: true`, the bundle's version), `ping`, `tools/list` = the
  snapshot's `tools` as JSON; 3 s later no instance and no socket file.
- **X2** `tools/call get_project` with no instance: one instance, the app's
  answer (no proxy sentence), the socket, and `reelcut-launch.log` beside it.
  **X3** the proxy's forwarded `tools/list` and the proof's own
  HTTP-over-AF_UNIX one each equal the snapshot as JSON values.
- **X4** two proxies on a fresh socket, calls released together (a
  `threading.Barrier`): both answer, exactly one instance. **X5** SIGKILL
  X2's instance; the same proxy's next call launches exactly one and answers.
- **X6** a `0755` folder, `RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT=5`: the timeout sentence naming
  the copy, the socket and `5 s`, in 5–15 s; a second call answers the
  stranded sentence within 2 s and starts no second instance.
- **X7** a `socketserver.UnixStreamServer` stub (one request at a time, a
  connection closed before a request ignored) holds `tools/call` 5 s: a
  `ping` sent 0.5 s in is answered before the call and within 1 s. **X7b**
  the stub holds proxy A's call 10 s: proxy B's `tools/list` sent 0.5 s in
  answers the snapshot within 4.5–7 s.
- **X8** a list from the snapshot, then a stub listing other tools: the call is
  followed by `notifications/tools/list_changed`; CONTROL: none within 3 s when
  the stub lists the snapshot's tools with every object's keys reversed.
- **X9** every stdout line of every proxy is JSON-RPC 2.0; **X10** no
  `Reelcut: ` in any launch log; **Z1** no instance alive; **Z2** `lstat` of
  the person's `Agent/`, `agent.sock` and `agent.launch.lock` unchanged.
- It writes `work/mcp-proxy/ac-mcp.json`, `docs/manual-checks.md` AC-3's
  fixture: `mcpServers.reelcut` with the TREE's Release proxy as its command.
- `--mutant launch-on-list` (X1 must FAIL) and `--mutant no-lock` (X4 must
  FAIL) copy `mcp-proxy/` (no `target/`) and `core/src/mcp_versions.rs` into
  `work/mcp-proxy/mutant-<name>/`, replace one anchor found exactly once in
  `mcp-proxy/src/` (`tools_list`'s `let answers = …` line; the
  `lock.lock()` statement), `cargo build --release --offline`, put the binary
  in a fresh bundle copy signed `--options runtime` ad hoc, re-sign the copy
  `--preserve-metadata=entitlements,flags`, and run every row. Exit 0 caught,
  1 survived, 2 control not performed.

`dist_check.py` D15–D24 hold each bundle's proxy (present, hardened runtime,
no entitlements) and snapshot (`{version, tools}` at `CFBundleShortVersionString`,
Release naming every flag-on `devHandlers` key, Distribution none);
`dist_check_mutants.py`'s skeletons now carry `Contents/Info.plist`, the proxy
and the snapshot for every case, and its eight new cases are:

| Case | The mutation | Expected FAIL |
|---|---|---|
| `no-proxy-release` / `-dist` | no proxy in the skeleton | D15 D17 D19 / D16 D18 D20 |
| `proxy-no-runtime-dist` | the proxy re-signed ad hoc without `--options runtime` | D18 |
| `proxy-entitlement-release` | the proxy re-signed `--options runtime` with allow-jit | D19 |
| `no-snapshot-dist` | no snapshot | D22 D24 |
| `snapshot-version-release` | the snapshot's `version` rewritten | D21 |
| `dist-snapshot-in-release` / `release-snapshot-in-dist` | the other side's snapshot | D23 / D24 |

## The road map 14 merge into main (2026-10-02)

`worktree-side-work` (road map 14, #127's prefetch, Include Reelcut windows)
merged into main at `c2b1100` (B52a–B73), whose proofs were all written
against TCP. What the merge changed in the proofs:

- **Moved to the socket** (`mcp.py`'s scratch socket, spec §11 MC-6):
  `codec_import_proof.py` and `container_import_proof.py` (no `--port`;
  each launches on its own scratch socket), `export_gain_proof.py`
  (`<dir>/agent.sock` where `<port>` was), `mixed_audio_proof.py` (the

non-modal "Copying Movie" window (`RewrapProgressWindowController`) whose

  (P2 for C29's `.mov`), run after B73's rows; the rows are in its
  docstring. The probe makes a `PresentCountingController` (an

## Issue batch B78 — a WebM or Matroska copy remembers its original (`container_rewrap_probe.py` O31–O43 and seven mutants; `container_import_proof.py` M8–M11; #228 part 3; spec §11 #228-O)

The built-in copy records the file it was made from as the media's
`original` (format version 11); `MediaSnapshot.name` reads it, Reveal in
Finder opens it, the row's tooltip says where the copy lives, and
`ProjectDocument.recopyingMissingCopies` copies a copy that is gone (or in
the Trash) again on open. The core's half — the field, its normalisation,
the relink's probe, paste, the schema and its key order — is
`core/tests/media_original.rs` and `core/tests/schema_v11.rs`.

- **`container_rewrap_probe.py`** gains one job of `kind: "original"` on a
  scratch copy of P1 named `o1.webm`, run last; the rows are in its
  docstring. O41's original is a scratch `.mov` with a movie put at its
  digest name, so a re-copy without the Matroska guard would succeed
  (`assist` reuses a movie at the digest name) and the guard is what O41
  holds; a `.mov` original with nothing there fails the copy either way.
  O42 asks FileManager for the home Trash's URL and never lists or writes
  it; O43 holds the Trash case through the `trashed` seam on a scratch
  `fakeTrash`. Every row discards the digest names it made.
- **Measured: `no-original` also fails O40 and O43.** Their re-copy relinks
  with a probe that, under the mutant, carries no original, which clears the
  one the project held (`relink_media`'s rule).
- **Measured (M9): a re-copy can land under another digest name.** The
  original's bookmark resolves to the file's real path (`/private/var/…` for
  the proof's `/var/folders/…` temporary directory), the digest is over the
  path, and the probe records the resolved path as the new `original.path`.
  On a path with no symlink in it the name is the same.

## Issue batch B79 — a rewrapped copy's movie timescale, and an agent's `open_project` read off main (`container_rewrap_probe.py` W23, F23, G24, G25 and `--mutant movie-600`; `agent_open_proof.py` A0–A7 and four mutants; `container_import_proof.py` M12; #232, #231; spec §11 #232, #231)

`ContainerRewrapWriter.write` sets the copy's movie timescale to the least
common multiple of 600 and its tracks' timescales
(`ContainerRewrapWriter.movieTimeScale`, with a 31-bit guard and two
fallbacks), and `open_project` is an `offMainTools` member whose read runs
on the lane's thread inside `MediaImporter.withoutAsking`.

- **`container_rewrap_probe.py`**: P23 is P2's video alone (`-an`). W23 it
  probes 640×360 at `[30000, 1001]` with no sound; F23 its frame 47 answers
  its own time; G24 reads each written copy's `mvhd` timescale out of the
  file's own atoms in Python (P1, P2, P3, P14, P15, P23) and holds it to
  `math.lcm(600, …)` of the track timescales the probe's own index reports
  and to four literals; G25 is one job of `kind: "timescale"`, the function
  over ten fixed cases. Mutant `movie-600` replaces the one assignment,
  `writer.movieTimeScale = scale`, with `_ = scale`. `main-watch`'s anchor

## Issue batch B80 — the opt-in ffmpeg conversion records its original, and copies a constant-rate VP9 stream checked on the copy (`ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py` F0, O1–O5, T1–T3, V1–V8 and six mutants; #233, #227; spec §11 #233, #227)

`MediaImporter.probeConverted` records the file an ffmpeg conversion was
made from as the descriptor's `original`. `FFmpegRewrap.plan(for:with:)`
(now in `FFmpegRewrap+Plan.swift`, a pure move gated alone) copies a VP9
Profile 0 or 2 stream that has a frame rate: the copy is snapped
(`-bsf:v setts=time_base=D/N:prescale=1`), written MP4-format under the
`.mov` digest name, and kept by `convert` only when
`FFmpegRewrap.keepsFrameGrid` finds every packet of the partial on the
rate's grid; a copy that fails, fails that check or will not open is
re-encoded once (`assist(…, reencodingVP9: true)`).

- **`ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py [--mutant NAME]`** (new, not a line of
  `make test`; needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` with libvpx-vp9) builds
  `ffmpeg_rewrap_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` under
  `tools/proof/work/ffmpeg-rewrap-build/` and runs it once, a `.prohibited`
  process on `agent_open_probe.swift`'s pattern: every import runs on a
  background thread while main spins. The rows, the fixtures, the wrapper
  and the count are in its docstring.
- **Scratch home.** The script removes `tools/proof/work/ffmpeg-rewrap/` at
  start and at exit and runs the probe with `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=<work>/home`
  and `-RCFFmpegImport always -RCFFmpegPath <work>/tools/ffmpeg`; F0 printed
  "Rewrapped/ is …/tools/proof/work/ffmpeg-rewrap/home/Library/Application
  Support/Reelcut/Rewrapped, inside the scratch home …: true;
  FFmpegRewrap.tools()?.ffmpeg is …/ffmpeg-rewrap/tools/ffmpeg, the wrapper:
  true; ffprobe /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe; policy always". `ls -la` of the
  owner's real `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/Rewrapped/` taken
  before the first run and after the last (three baseline runs and twelve
  mutant runs between them) compared equal (`cmp`).
- **The wrapper** is a Python script the proof writes with the real
  ffmpeg's resolved path baked in (here
  `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/ffmpeg/9.0.2/bin/ffmpeg`); the probe writes
  `<work>/mode` before a row and reads `<work>/ffmpeg.log` after it. The
  encoder query (`-encoders`) is a log line with no `-i` and is counted by
  no row.
- **Measured: CoreMedia names the copy's sound `aac `, not `mp4a`.** The
  first run of V1 and V2 compared the audio track's CoreMedia media subtype
  with `mp4a` and failed both: "video vp09, audio aac ; first frame 128×72
  BGRA true, decodesFirstFrame true; 1 -i run(s) [-c:v copy -f mp4]; the
  count at 30/1: 30/30 right, 30/30 distinct", `passed 15/17`. `mp4a` is the
  sample entry's own tag in the file, so V1 and V2 now read it with the
  real ffprobe (`codec_tag_string`) and print CoreMedia's subtype beside
  it. Nothing in the product changed between that run and the next.
- **Measured: `no-original` and `vp9-encode` fail more rows than their
  subject's.** `no-original` also fails O5 ("the media's path is the digest
  file false … original nil": with no original there is nothing to re-copy
  from) and V4, V5, V7 and V8, which each import with "original nil".
  `vp9-encode` also fails V4, V5, V7 and V8: with no copy tried each prints
  "1 -i run(s) [an encoder -f mov]", not two. Their EXPECTED sets are those
  runs' sets.

## Issue batch B81 — one document per path while a person's open is in flight, the two rewrap measurements explained, and B79's and B80's leftovers (`agent_open_proof.py` A8–A14 and `--mutant no-inflight`; `agent_socket_proof.py` K15 and `--mutant no-controller`; `ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py` V9, V10, G1, C1, P1, M1 and four mutants; `container_rewrap_probe.py` T22; `recording_proof.py` section 3's stop-ceiling row; #234, #235; spec §11 #234, #231, #227, #228-V, #232)

`ProjectDocumentController` (new, made at the top of `main.swift`) counts the
opens AppKit has in flight, per canonical path; `open_project`'s two
main-thread steps wait for one, up to `AgentServer.personOpenWait` each, and
`refuseHeldPath` refuses a path being opened. `FFmpegRewrap.assist` takes
the first attempt's plan (`planned`) and answers a re-encode this process
already made and kept; `probeConversion` discards only the file it probed;
`import_media`'s wait (`AgentServer.probeCeiling`) is the sum of every bound
the step has; the frame check's arithmetic is the pure `onFrameGrid`.

- **The EXPECTED sets were written before the first build**, as
  predictions: `no-inflight`'s, `no-recheck`'s and `open-on-main`'s new rows
  in `agent_open_proof.py`, and `discard-kept`'s, `plan-twice`'s,
  `pure-rows`'s and the three V9 additions in `ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py`.
  **Every prediction held:** each of the fourteen probe-mutant runs below is
  that mutant's FIRST run, and each printed MUTANT PASS. No set was
  corrected.
- **`agent_open_proof.py` A8–A14** race a person's open of `a4.reelcut`
  against an agent's call. The probe's controller is the app's own
  `ProjectDocumentController`, subclassed: `opens(of:)` notes an ask that
  answered above 0; the public open's override counts its entries and
  records its completion's document and error; `beginOpenPanel` answers the
  package with no panel; `presentError` counts; and the two `makeDocument`
  overrides call `super` and then HOLD the finished read, off main, until
  the other side has got as far as the row needs — a person's read until
  `opens(of:)` has answered above 0 or the agent's call has answered (mode
  `seen`), or until that call has answered (mode `answered`); an agent's
  read, where the row says so, until the person-style open has been
  called. Each hold is bounded at 120 s and an expired hold fails its row
  by name; no row sleeps for a guessed time, removes a copy or waits on a
  partial tick. No hold expired in any run below.
- **The establishing run is `--mutant no-inflight`** (`isOpening` answers
  false: the app as it was before #234). It printed, for A8, "open_project
  mid-read: already_open absent …; 2 open documents at the package's path,
  the person's open's own false", for A9 "1 reads by the agent during A8 (1
  by the person)", for A10 "its document among the open ones true; 2 open
  documents at the package's path", for A11 "1 read(s) by the person, 1 by
  the agent; 2 open documents", for A12 "open_project: ok: {"project": …
  after 0.172 s (no sooner than 1 wanted); 1 read(s) by the agent; then 2
  open documents", for A13 the same shape, 0.192 s after the person's open
  was called, and for A14 "new_project {path: a4.reelcut}: error: Timed out
  saving a4.reelcut.; project.json's bytes unchanged true (2781 → 2781);
  then 1 open documents at the package's path …; 2 open project(s) in all":
  with the person's read held until the call answered, the Save As waited
  for the open until `save`'s own bound, and left a second, untitled
  project open.
- **The doors AppKit has were read, not run** (spec §11 #234 lists them).
  The reading is a disassembly of the 3,513 AppKit methods and blocks whose
  names match `NSDocument`, `NSApplication(NSAppleEventHandling)`,
  `RecentItemsMenuController`, `Seamless`, `DocumentOpen`,
  `NSPersistentUI`, `NSWindowRestor` or `NSWorkspace`, one `disassemble`
  per symbol in a batch file, on macOS 26.5.1 (the designer's second pass;
  its output was a scratch file and is not kept):

  ```sh
  lldb -b -o "target create <a binary that links AppKit>" \
       -o "disassemble -n '-[NSDocumentController openDocument:]'"   # … one -o per symbol
  ```

  A8 drives File ▸ Open's own action, A10 the direct call the app's own
  doors make, A11 reopen.
- **#235 (1): T22's 0.000667 s was the reference's rounding, and the copy is
  not wrong.** `ffprobe` on the fixtures (this batch's run): `p22.webm`'s
  audio packets are stamped "0, 22, 43, 64, 86, 107, 128" ms and its first
  video packet 0.022 s; `p22.ogg`'s packets read "-1040,1024 -16,1024
  1008,1024 2032,1024 3056,1024" (pts, duration, in 1/48000 s).
  `container_rewrap_probe.py`'s T22 now holds the copy to a sample-exact
  reference (`click_reference`: the first audio Block's `pts_time`, plus the
  first Ogg packet's duration in samples and the sample of ffmpeg's plain
  decode that first passes 0.3, over 48000), bound 0.0001 s, and prints
  ffmpeg's timeline reading beside it, held to nothing. It printed "P22:
  the impulse decodes at 1.0213333333333334 s from the copy,
  1.0213333333333334 s by the sample-exact reference (first Block 0.000 s +
  (lead 1024 + plain-decode click 48000) / 48000), |difference| 0.000000 s,
  bound 0.0001 s; ffmpeg's timeline reading 1.022 s, |difference| 0.000667
  s, not bounded".
- **#235 (2): the slow re-copy waited in the disk write** (the designer's
  measurement, recorded in spec §11 #231; host state). What this batch
  changes is the instrument: each `open_project` row prints where its
  seconds went, and A2 and A5 want at least 3 partial ticks, "a count; the
  copy's seconds are the disk's". The baseline below printed, for A1,
  "1.146 s (0.252 s before the .partial.mov was first seen, 0.210 s while it
  was written, 0.684 s after it was last seen); 41 main ticks, 22 saw the
  .partial.mov", and for A4 "0.452 s (0.065 s before …, 0.208 s while it was
  written, 0.179 s after it was last seen); 30 main ticks, 19 saw the
  .partial.mov". `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` read 112 GiB free of 926
  directly before that run, against 23 GiB during the designer's.
- **`ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py`** has a second wrapper, `<work>/tools/ffprobe`,
  beside the ffmpeg one, so the product finds it as the sibling: it appends
  its argv to `<work>/ffprobe.log` and execs the real ffprobe. A PLAN of a
  source is a line there that holds `-show_streams` and ends in its path.
  Mode `bad-encode` writes 64 bytes of junk to the output of a `-f mov` run
  and exits 0. A mutant is a LIST of replacements, each exactly once.
- **The build folders are kept, and a mutant's is not.**
  `tools/proof/work/agent-open-build/` and `…/ffmpeg-rewrap-build/` each
  keep `probe/`, the baseline's, so a repeat run does not rebuild (`du -sh`:
  30 M each after the runs below); a mutant's `mutants/<name>/` is rebuilt
  on every run, because its sources are copied afresh, so each run removes
  its own at exit. `--clean` on either script removes the whole build
  folder and exits 0, running nothing: run after the last run below, each
  printed "removed …/tools/proof/work/<name>-build" and the folder was gone.
- **`agent_socket_proof.py` K15** is a quit with an `open_project` read in
  flight, on the built app in a scratch home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME=
  <work>/k15-home`; control C0 holds that the home took before any call).
  The quit sender is one bounded `osascript` armed BEFORE the call, polling
  for a trigger file every 10 ms, so the event costs no osascript start-up

  last step, and the row was corrected once:** "N2 exited False in 20.0 s

  project first (`close_project {discard: true}`, K14's C1 rule: no save
  sheet can appear). Nothing in the product changed between that run and
  the next. The second and third runs printed `17/17`.

  `try controller.makeDocument(withContentsOf: url, ofType: known.type)`;
  its old anchor had not matched since B79, so K12's open half had no
  runnable control.

Read and found NOT to write there (the designer's reading): `agent_open_proof.py`,
`ffmpeg_rewrap_proof.py`, `agent_socket_proof.py` K15 (scratch homes
already); `agent_socket_proof.py` K12 (`ContainerRewrap.rewrap` runs

`codec_import_proof.py` (`ImportError.undecodable.invitesFFmpeg` is false);

written); `cloud_captions_probe.py`, `harness/main.swift`,

the app sets `RC_AGENT_SOCKET`. No MCP tool writes `ExportPresets.json`.

- **What a scratch home moves** (the designer's measurements, 2026-10-04,
  `4c41af9`, macOS 26.5.1). In a process under `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=<dir>`,
  `NSHomeDirectory()` and FileManager's `.applicationSupportDirectory` are
  under `<dir>`. `.trashDirectory` is NOT moved: `appropriateFor:` an
  existing scratch file or folder answers the real `~/.Trash`, a missing
  file throws, and `nil` answers the real Trash. One `UserDefaults` write
  was seen to land in the real `~/Library/Preferences/`; nothing more about
  defaults was measured, and this batch moves no defaults domain (probe
  binaries write one named for the executable, the app its own).
  `AppSupport.directory` asks FileManager with `create: true`, so it makes
  `Library/Application Support` in whichever home it runs, and nothing under
  it: that folder appearing is the import proof's H0 and I1's guard.
- **The unchanged scripts under a scratch home** (the designer's runs, its
  drivers not kept): the rewrap probe `passed 60/60` (fixtures 14.1 s, build
  120.4 s, probe 2.2 s), O42 answering `trash_found true, trashed true`,
  which is the real Trash's URL; `trash-plays` MUTANT PASS; `no-mkdir`
  failing D16 and nineteen more rows; `container_import_proof.py` `passed
  15/15` in 8.6 s; `export_cancel_proof.py --only import` `2/2 rows ok in 47
  s`; `phase7_chrome.py` `78/78 checks passed`.
- **`container_rewrap_probe.py`.** `run_probe` is the only call that
  executes a probe binary, under `CFFIXED_USER_HOME=<work>/home` with that
  folder as the binary's second argument; before each run the home is
  removed and made again as `Library/Application Support` and nothing more,
  so `Reelcut/Rewrapped` is the product's to make. `child_env` raises
  before anything is executed for a home that is not under the work folder.
  Row **H0** is the probe's first: where `AppSupport.subdirectory
  ("Rewrapped")` is and whether that is inside the home it was named; when
  it is not the probe exits before it reads its jobs. The script makes the
  comparison again itself and both must agree, or a baseline scores no other
  row (`passed 0/1`, exit 1) and a mutant's control could not be performed
  (exit 2). The baseline is 61 rows.
- **`--control decoy-home`** (both scripts) runs the binary, or the
  instance, under a SECOND scratch home, `<work>/decoy-home`, while the
  first is the one looked in. It passes when H0 FAILS and nothing ran: for
  the probe, the `Rewrapped/` it answered is under the decoy, the binary
  printed no other row and nothing is under the decoy's
  `Library/Application Support/Reelcut`; for the import proof, no tool was
  called, and the decoy holds `Library/Application Support` and no
  `Reelcut/Rewrapped`. Each was run before its script's baseline, as the
  changed binary's or script's first execution. No script of this batch was
  run in its HEAD form, and no rewrap probe binary, app instance or presets
  mode was executed without a scratch home.
- **O42 no longer needs the home Trash.** It answers `isInside`'s three
  cases; `isTrashed` of the copy and of a path in the scratch `fakeTrash`
  that does not exist (both false); whether FileManager answered a Trash
  for the copy's own volume (`appropriateFor:` the copy, the product's
  first lookup), and `isTrashed` of `b82-probe.mov` in it, a path that is
  never listed, written or created. It passes with a Trash found and that
  path trashed, or with none found. O43 was already through the `trashed`
  seam on both legs. The product's own `isTrashed` still asks FileManager
  for the Trash in `recopyingMissingCopies`' default (O36–O41); that lookup
  reads and never writes, and no probe change can stop it.
- **`no-mkdir` fails twenty rows where it failed one.** A fresh home has no
  `Rewrapped/`, which the real home always had, so with `ensureDirectory`
  gone no copy lands there. The run below printed, for D16, "P16: error

- **`--mutant` takes names.** One name, several, or `all`; the fixtures are

## Issue batch B83 — proofs and the owner's `UserDefaults` (`proof_defaults.py` P1–P9, P5s and three mutants; `defaults_proof.py` C0, G1–G5, R1, R2 and two mutants; `mcp.py`'s guard; #238)

B82 put four proofs' Application Support under a scratch home and measured
that this does not move `UserDefaults`. This batch closes #238 as measured:
no environment moves `UserDefaults`, a proof session moves no setting the
owner sees, and a probe's domain can only be removed after it exits. So
there are two things: a guard in `mcp.py` that FAILS a script whose session
moved a key, and a removal recipe with a gated sweep for the proofs' own
domains. No file under `app/`, `core/`, `graphic/`, `mcp-proxy/` or `agent/`
changed, and no spec §11 decision was made.

**Measured** (the designer, 2026-10-04, `a31b9da`, macOS 26.5.1; drivers not
kept; key names only):

- **(a) refuted.** A throwaway executable writing `UserDefaults.standard`, a fresh name per run,
  under `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`; that + `__CFPREFERENCES_AVOID_DAEMON=1` (scratch `Library/Preferences`
  absent, then pre-made); the variable alone; `HOME` + it; all three: every run left
  `~/Library/Preferences/<name>.plist` and nothing in the scratch home. `__CFBundleIdentifier` did
  not rename the domain; a `sandbox-exec` profile denying `com.apple.cfprefsd.*` did not stop it.
- **(b) in-process refuted; after exit it works.** `removePersistentDomain` in the process, or
  `defaults delete <name>` alone, leaves a 42-byte plist. `defaults delete <name>` (rc 0 or 1) THEN
  unlinking the plist, after the process exited, left no file and no domain at once and 10 s
  later, in five cases (with and without `synchronize`, with and without an in-process removal).
  Unlinking without the `defaults delete` after an in-process removal: the file came back.
- **(c) holds for the app's domain.** The real `com.kgalligan.Reelcut` (47 keys, by name and
  salted digest; another session's pid 85319 running; an 8 s no-launch control unmoved) was
  unmoved across a bare `mcp.launch`, `new_project` + `close_project`, and every clone session.
  The clone is the built app with `CFBundleIdentifier` replaced (`cp -c -R`, `plutil -replace`; it
  launched without re-signing and wrote the new identifier's domain), so a same-value rewrite
  shows. It ran `new_project`/`close_project`; `screens.PINS` + `View ▸ Assistant`,
  `select_inspector_tab`, `Reelcut ▸ Settings…`; `screens.py --app <clone>` (23 pass); `v2_menu.py
  --only T,N,D,U,R,S,L` (23 pass). Keys written, in all — AppKit's, re-saved from the same domain:
  `NSWindow Frame NSColorPanel`, `NSToolbar Configuration com.apple.NSColorPanel`, `NSSplitView
  Subview Frames NSColorPanelSplitView`, `NSNavPanelExpandedSizeForOpenMode`,
  `NSOSPLastRootDirectory`. No `Reelcut*` or `RC*` key.
- **The one route to an owner-visible write is `perform_menu_item`:** on the clone, `["View",
  "Snapping"]` wrote `ReelcutSnappingEnabled`, seen by `defaults export` while running and at
  once after `stop()`. No MCP handler writes defaults, no script runs `defaults write`/`delete`,
  no `-Key value` was persisted, and no path a proof performs today persists an app key.
- **Probes.** 90 executable names under `tools/proof/work`, 22 with a same-named plist; no shared
  runner (93 scripts carry their own `swiftc`). `harness.plist` holds two Rasterize keys as well.
- **(d) not taken and not measured:** (c) holds, and the request allows (d) only when (a)–(c) fail.
- **The app's persisted keys** are `Reelcut*` and `RC*` (`RCFFmpegImport`).
- **Ownership under the rules below, read with `plistlib`: 36 names.**
  `executable` 22, `source` 2 (`agent_open_probe`, `ffmpeg_rewrap_probe`),
  `prefix` 8 (`com.kgalligan.reelcut.…`), `keys` 4 (`probe-mutant`,
  `probe-pristine`, `homecheck`, `sweep`). All hold only the families a
  probe compiled from `app/Sources` writes, except `harness`
  (`ReelcutInspectorWidth`, `ReelcutTimelineHeight` beside Rasterize's
  `toolOptions.*`): `shared`.
- **Unattributed: 29.** 28 by name and `dbg` by its two `Reelcut*` keys; 11
  `com.kgalligan.rasterize.*` names are refused, never listed. The Mach-O
  walk of `tools/proof/work` finds 90 names, among them `reelcut-agent` (a
  product helper's name).
- **Exit status.** Python 3.14.7: `SystemExit` raised in an `atexit` handler
  leaves status 0; `os._exit(3)` there gives 3. `ps -axo pid=,comm=` prints
  each executable's full path.

This batch's own reading at the same commit agreed: `owned_domains()` was
compared in code with those 36 (identical name and rule, 36 of 36, none with
a `refusal`), and `executables()` answered 90 names with `reelcut-agent`
among them.

**The guard** (`mcp.py`). A record per socket path: the domain, its key
names against salted digests (`proof_defaults.snapshot`, which runs
`defaults export <domain> -` and nothing else), the Reelcut pids sharing the
domain then, and the pids the record owns. `scratch_socket()` records
`com.kgalligan.Reelcut`; `launch()` re-records the binary's own bundle
identifier before `Popen` and owns its child (a record that already owns a
pid, a relaunch on the same socket, is compared first, so nothing is lost);
`MCP()` records a socket that has no record, a handed one, under the domain
of the executable holding it, that pid owned. Since issue batch B84 the
record and the compare both run `defaults export` with no
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` (`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a script run under a
scratch home that is not there at one of the two is compared with itself
(rows H1 and H2 below; the measurement is in B84's phase-2 section).
`remove_scratch()` compares
before it deletes, and one `atexit` handler, registered at import so it
runs after any a script registers later, compares every record still held:
a script that never calls `remove_scratch`, leaves early by `sys.exit` or an
exception, or was handed its socket. A moved key outside AppKit's `NS*` and
`Apple*` families prints

    mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED in <domain>: <names> (other Reelcut pids: <list|none>)

on stderr. When no other Reelcut shares the domain the handler reprints
those lines last and ends the process with `os._exit(3)`; when one does, the
line is all there is, because the write may be that instance's. Others are
the sharing pids then and now, less every pid a record of this process has
owned and the pid holding the socket. Each guard body catches `Exception`
and says so (`mcp: the defaults guard is off for <socket>: <type>`, the
exception's type and never its text); an `lsof` or `ps` answer the guard
cannot read counts as no pid, except a handed pid whose executable `ps` will
not name: it is owned, its record guards the app's domain, and that is said;
and a moved key already found is appended and printed whatever `ps` and
`lsof` then answer. A domain `defaults export` will not
answer for is said on stderr, at the record or at the compare (`mcp: the
defaults guard could not read <domain> at the record|at the compare …`):
that record can see no moved key. The status does not change.
`defaults_moved(socket)` answers every moved key name of a guarded socket. Existing signatures and
returns are unchanged; the exit status changes in that one case.

**What the guard does not reach.** A script killed by a signal, interrupted
while a compare is running, or leaving by `os._exit` (none in `tools/proof`
does); a script that never imports
`mcp.py` (`dist_check.py`); a write by a Reelcut that started after the
record and quit before the compare would be blamed on the script; a write
by a script with two instances of its own alive, launched by its own
`Popen`, counts the other as another Reelcut and only prints. When the guard
ends a script, `os._exit` skips whatever would have run after its handler:
an `atexit` handler registered before `mcp` was first imported, and the
flush of any file the script still holds open. The script's own status (1 or
2) becomes 3; its rows are already flushed above the line. A probe's or the
harness's writes at their source are not stopped: their domains are swept
afterwards.

**`defaults_proof.py`** proves the guard on a clone of the built app whose
`CFBundleIdentifier` is `com.kgalligan.reelcut.defaults-proof`
(`tools/proof/work/defaults-proof/Reelcut.app`, `cp -c -R`, removed through
`tree_copy.remove_tree`), so the write it makes on purpose, View ▸ Snapping
through `perform_menu_item`, lands in that domain and none of the owner's.
Each G row runs the script again as a `--child` that scores nothing and
ends `sys.exit(0)`; the parent scores its status and stderr.

| Row | Child | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | — | the clone is made, its domain removed, it comes up with `perform_menu_item` and no parity complaint, and a bare launch moves no owner-visible key |
| G1 | `write`: `mcp.launch(clone)`, `new_project`, View ▸ Snapping, `defaults_moved` as JSON, stop, `remove_scratch` | the JSON holds `ReelcutSnappingEnabled`; status 3; stderr's last line is `DEFAULTS MOVED` naming it and `none` |
| G2 | CONTROL `quiet`: `new_project`, `close_project` | status 0, no such line |
| G3 | `write-no-remove`: never calls `remove_scratch` | status 3 |
| G5 | `write`, while S2 (a second instance of the clone the parent started by `Popen` on its own folder, no `mcp` record) is alive | status 0; the line names S2's pid |
| G4 | `write-handed`: `MCP(S2's socket)` only | status 3, and the key is among `defaults_moved` at the first reading after the call |
| H1 (B84) | `absent-home`, with `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` naming an absent folder under the work folder: `mcp.launch(clone)`, the folder made (by the instance, else the child), `new_project`, `close_project`, stop, `remove_scratch`. The parent first seeds the CLONE's domain with `ReelcutDefaultsProofSeed` (`defaults write`, that domain only) and counts its keys | the record held as many keys as the parent counted; the home absent at the record and present at the compare; status 0, no such line |
| H2 (B84) | `home-removed`: the folder is there at the record and the child removes it after `stop()`, before `remove_scratch` | the same, the home present then absent |
| R1 | the REAL build in this process: `mcp.launch`, `new_project`, `close_project`, stop, `remove_scratch` | no owner-visible key of `com.kgalligan.Reelcut` moved (one retry when another Reelcut shares the domain, then FAIL naming keys and pids) |
| R2 | — | the real domain across C0 and the G and H rows: no owner-visible key moved |

`--mutant` reaches the children by argv: `no-compare`
(`proof_defaults.moved` answers `[]`) must fail exactly G1, G3, G4, G5;
`no-exit` (`mcp._exit_failed` is a no-op) exactly G1, G3, G4;
`home-followed` (B84: `proof_defaults.read_env` answers None, so `defaults
export` inherits `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` as it did before) exactly H1, H2.

**`proof_defaults.py`** is the other half and imports nothing from
`tools/proof`. `remove_domain(name)` is `defaults delete <name>` (0 and 1
both accepted) THEN unlinking the plist. `refusal(name)` is asked first and
names what is never acted on: the empty name, a name holding `/` or
starting `.` or `-`, `NSGlobalDomain` and `Apple Global Domain`, `reelcut`,
`reelcut-agent` and `reelcut-mcp`, `com.apple.*`, any name containing
`rasterize`, and `com.kgalligan.Reelcut` in any case with its capital-R
namespace and any name that extends it without a dot
(`com.kgalligan.Reelcut-Dev`, `com.kgalligan.ReelcutHelper`). A call on the real Preferences folder asks that rule a second
time under no mutant, and a scratch folder with no stand-in runner raises
`ValueError`. A plist with no `refusal` is a proof's own by the first rule
that holds: `executable` (a Mach-O of that name with an exec bit under
`tools/proof/work`, the walk skipping `*.app`, `*.dSYM`, `node_modules`,
`.git`, `Intermediates.noindex`, `target` and symlinks), `source` (the stem
of a `*_probe.swift` under `tools/proof`), `prefix` (the name starts
`com.kgalligan.reelcut.` or `reelcut.`, case-sensitive), `keys` (at least
one key, every one starting `Reelcut`). The sweep, per owned name: `busy`
(the plist is under 60 minutes old, a process of that basename is running,
or one's bundle identifier is the name), read immediately before acting, is
left and reported (for a probe the caller names with `--ran`, whose plist
holds only `NS*`/`Apple*` keys, the age is not asked); else, with every key in `Reelcut*`, `RC*`, `NS*`,
`Apple*` (or none), `remove_domain`; else `shared`, `defaults delete <name>
<key>` for its `Reelcut*` keys only and the file never unlinked; a returned
reason is `denied` and is not worked around. The busy gate cannot see a
write `cfprefsd` has not flushed from a process that already exited into a
plist older than 60 minutes; `phase7_chrome.py`'s `defaults-write` then
`defaults-read` is the only read-back in `tools/proof` (the designer's
reading).

The selftest's P1 and P2 are real, on `reelcut.proof-defaults-selftest.<pid>`
made with `defaults write`; P3–P9 run over scratch folders under `$TMPDIR`
with a recording runner that executes nothing. Each refused name a file can
bear has a plist and a Mach-O (a copy of `/usr/bin/true`) in a folder of its
own beside the row's control: P3 the app's names, P4 the global and
option-like names, P5 Rasterize's, P6 the product helpers', each with a
control that IS removed; P5s the `shared` branch and its removed-whole
control; P7 one name per rule and an `NS`-only `x-probe` owned by none; P8
the busy gate; P9 the raise. P8's running process is `/bin/sleep` started
through a symlink of the name, whose path is what `ps` prints: a COPY of
`/bin/sleep` exits 137 at exec on this host (run twice), while a copy of
`/usr/bin/true` runs. Its plist is owned by `keys`. `--mutant no-unlink`
skips the unlink in the real Preferences folder only, since over a scratch
folder there is no daemon and the unlink is the whole removal.

Run on 2026-10-04 over `a31b9da` plus this batch's diff, macOS 26.5.1,
Python 3.14.7, another session's Reelcut (pid 85319, an Xcode build)
running throughout and never this batch's.

**Three handed sessions showed no moved key, and it was not explained.**
Before a writing child toggled until the key showed, the handed child (G4)
printed "status 0; defaults_moved []; stderr's last line '(no stderr)'" in
two of the first four proof runs, and one of four handed sessions in a
driver that was not kept showed no `ReelcutSnappingEnabled` among
`defaults_moved` within 15 s, on a domain removed just before. The first
proof run was timed at 100 s; the final one took 9 s by its output file's
timestamps. It did not happen again: in 51 further handed sessions (drivers not kept, and the runs
above) the key showed at the first toggle; in 12 of them the menu item's
state agreed with the stored value before and after; 2088 `defaults export`
calls made during 12 sessions all answered a dictionary; `socket_pid` found
the instance 75 times of 75; and `MCP()`'s record named the clone's domain
and pid 18 times of 18. Three causes fit the print and none was caught: the
toggle writing the value already stored, the record guarding the wrong
domain (`socket_pid` answering None, so `com.kgalligan.Reelcut`), or a
snapshot that could not be taken (silence). So each child toggles up to
three times, waiting up to 3 s each, and prints its record's domain, its
owned pids, how many keys its first snapshot held, whether
`ReelcutSnappingEnabled` was among them, how long the session took to open,
and for each toggle whether and when the key showed. A key that shows only
at a later toggle FAILS its row (one that shows at none is said to have
shown at none), and G4 also fails when the first reading
after the call lacks the key, which is what a handed script exiting at once
would be compared on. The later toggles are an instrument and never a retry.
For a real build the second cause leaves the domain right
and the record owning no pid: the handed instance, alive when the record was
made, then counts as another Reelcut, and a moved key is only printed unless
`lsof` answers at the compare with the instance still up. So `MCP()` asks
`lsof` twice and says on stderr when a socket's file is there and no pid
holds it.

## Issue batch B84 — delete, rename and restore a graphic, over the last 10 kept texts of each module (`graphics_store_probe.py` H1–H18, C7 and fifteen mutants; `graphics_files_proof.py` and `--mutant rename-unreconciled`; #103 part 1, phase 1; spec §11 G-27, G-28, G-29)

Phase 1 of the batch: the records, the store, the three document bodies,
the three tools and their proofs. Phase 2 — File ▸ Rename Graphic…, Delete
Graphic…, Restore Graphic Version… and their sheet — is the subsection at
this section's end (`graphics_menu_proof.py`, spec §11 G-30).

**What is proved, and by which instrument.**

- **The probe** (`graphics_store_probe.py`, nineteen new rows beside its
  twenty-six; no app, no MCP) drives `GraphicStore` and
  `ProjectDocument+GraphicFiles.swift`'s bodies directly, every text
  compared as text and every revision against hashlib:
  H1 a replacing `write` + `rescan()` and an in-place outside rewrite each
  keep the replaced text, newest first, the outside one in ONE post; H2
  `restoreGraphic` twice, then a kept file rewritten by hand refused in a
  sentence naming it and the other kept revision, nothing written; H3
  thirteen writes keep the 10 newest of the 12
  replaced, and `keep` of a text already kept lists it once; H4 delete
  refused while used, then done, `fonts/` and `assets/` left, the change
  count unmoved; H5 a timeline clip and a nest clip through rename, a taken
  name, a bad name and an open nest refused, `undo()` and `redo()`; H6 a

  H7 Undo never moves a live module under a deleted one's name; H8 a rename

  newest pairs, newest first, a repeated pair once; C7 an untitled

  folded back): `b.js` and its kept text stay, the clip names `a`, the
  pair `[a, b]` is still journalled, and with that file removed a
  committed change repairs — `a.js` back with its kept text.

**Not claimed.** How the three acts look to a person: the sheets are
phase 2's below, and what only a person can judge of them is
`docs/manual-checks.md`'s GR-7. A crash between `removeModule`'s `keep` and
the file's removal was not made to happen: H12 builds the state it leaves
(the current text also the newest kept) by hand. **The repair's three
limits** (spec §11 G-28 (f)). The first no row can measure: with the pair
`[a, b]`, clips that name `a` with no file and nothing kept for a reason
other than Undo — repointed onto a new `a.js` that was then removed
outside the app — cannot be told from an Undo, because the store cannot
see a removal made outside the app, and an undrawn `b.js` is moved under
`a`. The mirror of it, a file removed at a pair's SECOND name, is H10 and
is not repaired. The other two are a crash INSIDE `moveModule`, which no
row makes happen; each row builds by hand the state the crash leaves.
**That a rename killed part-way is healed is NOT claimed**: killed after
the file moved and before the pair was written, nothing is repaired (H6's
CONTROL is that state); killed after the pair was written and before the
history was folded, it is healed only when the old name had nothing kept
(H6), and with kept texts under the old name the repair reads it as a
deleted module and moves nothing (H15, which also runs the default
restore G-28 (f) speaks of in that state). The way out is by hand:
`set_graphic {name: <to>}` on the clips. **That a rename refused at the
clips puts everything back is claimed for the file, its history, the
clips and the journal, not for a deleted module's kept texts**: onto a
deleted module's name they end under the renamed module (H18's LIMIT
part, G-28 (d)). H18 refuses through the probe's own `apply`; no row
makes the CORE refuse a rename's `set_graphic`, and no MCP row reaches
that arm. A kept file changed by hand is
still LISTED (`kept`, `history`): H2 measures the listing and the refused
restore, and nothing claims the list ignores it (G-29 (d)).

```sh
  python3 tools/proof/graphics_store_probe.py --mutant $m                 # MUTANT PASS each
done
python3 tools/proof/graphics_files_proof.py                               # 10/10, exit 0 (launches the app; not in make test)
python3 tools/proof/graphics_files_proof.py --mutant rename-unreconciled  # MUTANT PASS (builds an app in a tree copy)
```

## Issue batch B85 phase 1 — path helpers in the graphics standard library (`graphic/tests/js/path.test.js` T1–T9, `graphic/tests/path.rs` R1–R5, six hand mutants; `graphics_path_proof.py` H0, M0–M3, Z1; #103 part 2; spec §11 G-31)

`getLength(d)`, `getPointAtLength(d, length)` and `evolvePath(progress, d)`
are `graphic/src/path.js`, pure JavaScript. Phases 2 (`paste_attributes`
between graphic clips) and 3 (HEVC with alpha) are their own pipelines.

**What is proved, and by which instrument.**

- **`path.test.js`** (`cargo test --release --test stdlib path_test_js`; in
  `make test`). Each row is a function run in its own `try`; the render
  throws ONE `Error` joining `"<row>: <message>"` for every row that threw,
  so a single run names every failed row. T1 lines, exact to 1e-9 (the
  relative spelling, implicit pairs, two subpaths, `M0,0L.5.5-1-1`); T2
  arcs against closed forms at 1e-4 relative (a circle of radius 500, a
  quarter arc, the ellipse 200 by 100 plain and turned 30°, radii scaled
  up, a zero-radius arc, unseparated flags); T3 the parabola as a `Q` and
  as a `C`, a `T` and an `S` equal to their explicit spellings; T4 the
  cusp; T5 points and headings on the circle (0.01 px, 0.05°), the two
  ends, the clamps, a second subpath, a corner, an arc drawn the other
  way (sweep 0); `T5 the limit at a start`
  and `T5 the limit at an end`, the two zero-derivative rows, scored apart
  so one run can show both failing; T6 nothing drawn; T7 `evolvePath`
  (`D === getLength(d) * 1.001`, the offsets, the clamps, `"none"`, and
  the LONGEST subpath for two paths of several); T8 the two error
  sentences whole, each named for the function called; `T8 a number
  that is not finite`, twelve cases each run though another failed (the
  fix pass, below); T9 forty paths, then the first again.
- **`path.rs`** (`cargo test --release --test path -- --nocapture`; in
  `make test` without the prints). R1 pixels through `common::render`: a

## Issue batch B85 phase 3, phase A — the size an export reports is the size written (`core/tests/export_size.rs`, five new and three rewritten tests, five hand mutants; `hevc_alpha_proof.py --rows size` H0, T0, R1–R4, E2, B1, B4, G1, Z1; `hevc_alpha_baseline.json`; #103; spec §11 G-33)

On every export row that needs even pixel dimensions the core resolves and
lists the even size the file will have (`Preset::even_sized`,
`export_size::even_size`), so the Size popup, the sheet's readout and
fields and the `export` tool's `width` and `height` say the file's size.
This is phase A of G-33, gated alone and committed as fcfeebf. Phase B —
the `hevc_alpha` row, the fill rule, the encoder outcome — is the next
section, and added its rows, mutants and controls to the same script. This
section is the record of phase A's gate ON PHASE A'S BUILD: **on a build
that holds phase B, `--rows size` prints 10/11 and exits 1, by design** —
its row G1 requires the pad and an unknown `hevc_alpha` — and says so on
G1's line and on its last line (next section, "Gate A after phase B").

**What is proved, and by which instrument.**

- **`core/tests/export_size.rs`** (in `make test`), through the FFI, every
  oracle a literal written by hand.
  `an_odd_document_row_is_evened_on_the_rows_that_need_it`: 1000 × 667,
  321 × 181, 181 × 320, 1619 × 1080 and 1 × 1 list `("document", "Document
  (even)", …)` at 1000 × 666, 320 × 180, 180 × 320, 1618 × 1080 and 2 × 2 on
  the six even-sized rows, and the canvas as `"Document size"` on
  `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng`; 1600 × 900 is `"Document size"`
  everywhere. `every_preset_is_even_sized_or_keeps_an_odd_edge`: every id
  `rc_export_presets` lists is in exactly one of the test's two literal

  `a_listed_movie_size_sent_back_resolves_to_itself`: every row of every

  `the_long_edge_rounds_to_the_nearest_even_integer`,
  `a_long_edge_that_lands_on_an_odd_integer_goes_up` and
  `the_audio_only_formats_list_what_h264_lists`;
  `the_first_row_is_the_document_for_every_movie_format` keeps its two even

- **`hevc_alpha_proof.py --rows size`** (not in `make test`: it launches
  the app). Its own Release instance in a scratch home
  (`tools/proof/work/hevc-alpha/home`, removed at start and exit) on its own

  width at 280 and the export choice pinned to `{"preset_id":"hevc_alpha"}`.
  One menu item, File ▸ Export…; its sheet is cancelled. Neither that nor
  the `export` tool writes the remembered export choice (below: "The
  owner's defaults"). Every export is one second; the largest frame is
  1280 × 720.
  H0 the scratch home took. T0 `export`'s `size` description holds "written
  one pixel smaller on that edge". R1, R2 a 321 × 181 and a 181 × 320
  document with no `size` as `h264`, `hevc`, `prores_422` (and `hevc` at

  no `size`: 640 × 360 on four rows. E2 the sheet: the Size popup "Document

  (even) · 1000 × 666", not truncated (intrinsic width 207 in a 240 pt

  popup reading "H.264 (MP4)" or "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)" (what that shows

  fixed parameters (its byte counts are printed, not compared: "The baseline

  sizes equals the baseline's size and digest. G1 the six odd-canvas files
  equal the baseline's frame-0 digest and eight edge pixels, a black one
  among them, and `hevc_alpha` is an unknown preset that writes no file —
  so phase A moved no pixel where it acts, and the row is red on a tree that

  size`). Z1 every project closes and the log holds no `Reelcut: ` line.

**The baseline**, `tools/proof/hevc_alpha_baseline.json`, was recorded
twice on the build of main at 055a5ed, before any core or Swift edit
(`--record-baseline`; 17 cases; the two recordings, each its own launch,
agreed on every value, the frame digests included, so nothing is stored
`null`). The recorder refuses to write unless `git status` shows `core/`
and `app/` unchanged, the answer for both odd documents says the canvas's
size over an evened file on each of `h264`, `hevc` and `prores_422`, and
each of those files' eight pixels holds a black one. On a tree with G-33's
resolver the recorder exits 1, so it is not re-recorded on this one. It
also holds what
phase B's rows are read against: the right-hand edge of a 334 × 222 white
canvas at `720p` (columns w−1 and w−2 black, w−3 white on all three opaque
rows), a 400 × 100 white canvas at `[402, 100]` (the middle row's black
pixels are columns 400 and 401 on all three), and that `prores_4444`
refuses that size.

**The baseline is one host's bytes and one build's, and says which**
(fix pass 1 of phase A's review). Its cases are hardware H.264 and HEVC
bitstreams, ffprobe's values for one of them, and ffmpeg's RGBA
digests, so another Mac, another macOS or another ffmpeg can differ in
every one of them with nothing wrong in Reelcut. (ffprobe's byte counts
for that file — the stream's `bit_rate`, the file's `size` and `bit_rate`
— are held in the baseline and printed, and since fix pass 2 of phase B's
review compared on no host, this one included: "B1 compares no byte
count", in the next section.) The file carries `host` —
the chip (`sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string`), the macOS version and
build (`sw_vers`) and the first three words of `ffmpeg -version` — and the
rows print it on the line under their heading. **On a host that is not
the baseline's, phase A's script scored nothing, named both hosts and
exited 2**: the instrument, not the product. Phase B changed that to what
this paragraph left open — the rows that read no digest are scored there
and only B1, B4 and G1 withheld, still with exit 2 (next section, "Another
host"). Such a host
records its own baseline: a git work tree of a commit before G-33's code
(055a5ed), `make app` in it, then THIS script twice with `--record-baseline
--app <that tree>/build/Build/Products/Release/Reelcut.app`. A recording at
another commit or on another host than the file's starts the file over, so
that baseline replaces the committed one in the working tree.
`head` is the commit of the BUILD's tree, not of the checkout the script
sits in: the recorder takes `--app`'s own work tree (`build_tree`: the app
has to be `build/Build/Products/Release/Reelcut.app` at the top of a git
work tree), stamps that tree's `git rev-parse HEAD`, holds THAT tree's
`core/` and `app/` to `git status`, and records nothing for a build
anywhere else (a proof's tree copy has no `.git`). What it cannot see is a
stale build inside its tree — `make app` there first. **The committed
file's `host` was stamped, not recorded**: the recorder cannot run on phase
A's tree, so the host `host()` reads today (Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1
(25F80), ffmpeg version 9.0.2 — the machine and the day of both
recordings, and what this section and G-33 already named) was added to the
existing document by a few lines of Python (load, `d["host"] =
hevc_alpha_proof.host()`, write with the recorder's own `json.dumps(…,
indent=1, sort_keys=True)`). The SHA-256 of the `cases` object was the
same before and after (a29eac32…), a `diff` of the two files is the five
`host` lines alone, and `head` was already the build's (the recordings
used the default `--app`, this tree's build at 055a5ed). The 17 cases are
the two 055a5ed recordings, untouched. By import, with no launch: the
unstamped file and a copy stamped with another chip each answer `instrument
failure: …` naming both hosts and return 2; `record` on this tree answers
`NOT RECORDED: core/ or app/ of <tree> differs from its HEAD`, and with
`--app /Applications/Reelcut.app`, `NOT RECORDED: the build's commit cannot
be read`. The recorder as it now stands has not written a baseline: both
recordings were made before `build_tree` and the host stamp existed, and its
writing path — the merge on `head` and `host`, and `--app` aimed at another
tree — needs a built work tree of 055a5ed to run, which this pass did not
make.

**The owner's defaults.** The instance shares the owner's
`com.kgalligan.Reelcut` domain (#238), and before the pin was sent as a
`<string>` its launches READ the owner's remembered export choice (next
paragraph). Nothing the proof does can WRITE it, by reading: the key's one
writer is `ExportChoice.remember()` (`ExportPresetsStore.swift:174`, the
`UserDefaults.standard.set` at `:180`), whose one caller is
`ExportSheetController.commit(queue:)` (`ExportSheetController.swift:568`),
reached only from `exportClicked` and `queueClicked` (`:521`, `:527`);
`cancel_sheet` (`AgentServer+MenuItem.swift:112`) presses the sheet's
Escape button through `UISheet.cancel` (`UISheet.swift:66`) — Cancel, which
`makeButtonRow` gives that key (`Sheets.swift:90`) — and its action,
`cancelClicked` (`ExportSheetController.swift:516`), is `dismiss(self)` and
nothing else; the `export` tool's handler,
`exportProject` (`AgentServer+Render.swift:260`), is in a file that names
`UserDefaults` nowhere, and neither do `Exporter*.swift`,
`ExportSheet*.swift` or `ExportQueue*.swift`. (Line numbers at 055a5ed;
phase A's diff touches none of these files.) By a run, `mcp.py`'s guard is
the instrument: a moved owner-visible key is a `mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED` line
on stderr, and status 3 when no other Reelcut shares the domain. **The
stderr of the two recordings and of the gate's red and green runs was not
kept**, and another session's Reelcut was alive then, so a moved key would
only have printed — nothing is claimed of those four runs from their
output. Fix pass 1's run
kept both streams apart: 11/11, exit 0, **stderr empty** (0 bytes) — no
`DEFAULTS MOVED` line and no line saying the guard could not read the
domain. Another Reelcut (`/Applications/Reelcut.app`, the same bundle
identifier) was alive during it, so a line, not status 3, is what a moved
key would have been.

**A launch argument the argument domain drops.** `-ReelcutExportChoice
{"preset_id":"hevc_alpha"}` is NOT taken: a value that begins with a brace
and is not a property list is discarded, `UserDefaults` answers the owner's
own remembered choice, and the sheet opened on it (measured on this host:
a format and a Quality tier that are not the build's defaults). Sent as `<string>{"preset_id":"hevc_alpha"}</string>` the
key reads as that text. E2 also requires the Format popup to read "H.264
(MP4)" or "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)", which fails the row when the pin did
not take and the owner's remembered format is another one (as it was on
this host); in phase A, where a taken pin names a row the build lacks and
the sheet falls back to H.264, an owner who last exported H.264 cannot be
told apart — phase B's row requires "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)" exactly.
`screens.py`'s own pin is the empty string, which is taken as it is.
