## Issue batch B85 phase 3, phase B — HEVC with alpha, the fill within a pixel, and a missing encoder (`core/tests/export.rs`, three new tests; `hevc_alpha_proof.py`: 30 rows, 2 controls, 3 mutants; #103; spec §11 G-33)

`hevc_alpha`, "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)", is the tenth export row: a QuickTime
movie whose frames carry the canvas's alpha. Every movie row FILLS the
frame when it is within a pixel of the canvas's shape (`ExportWriter.shapeGap`,
one integer test the alpha guard shares) and letterboxes past that, where
the two alpha movie rows refuse instead; a Mac with no encoder for a row
answers the preset's own sentence and leaves no file
(`Exporter.encoderOutcome`); the Document tab's note counts the alpha
formats once there are three. The first arm of the fill rule is the one
G-33 (c) records as amended in fix pass 1: a canvas-SHAPED size less at
most one pixel on each axis — `(bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw`, `a` and `b`
each 0 or 1 — is filled on the strength of the fill's overshoot, at any
scale, so no size of the canvas's own shape is refused for being odd.

**What is proved, and by which instrument.**

- **`core/tests/export.rs`** (in `make test`; 38 tests). `EXPECTED` holds
  ten rows with `hevc_alpha` after `hevc`.
  `hevc_alpha_is_a_mov_avfoundation_writes`: every key of the resolved
  settings — `mov`, `com.apple.quicktime-movie`, the codec `hevc_alpha`,
  `…HEVCHighestQualityWithAlpha`, picture, sound, alpha, the document's
  size and rate, no bit rate unasked, `optimize_for_network` false by
  default and true when asked, an asked bit rate echoed.
  `hevc_alpha_sits_directly_after_hevc`: the menu's order and the row's
  name. `the_hevc_row_is_what_it_was`: the `hevc` preset row and its
  resolved settings, with nothing asked and with all four optional
  overrides, against literals the tree printed BEFORE the row was added
  (the test was written and passed first, then the row).
  `only_prores_4444_hevc_alpha_and_apng_carry_alpha`: the three ids, in
  menu order. `core/tests/export_size.rs` (20 tests): `hevc_alpha` is in
  `MOVIE_FORMATS`, in the even-sized list (so
  `every_preset_is_even_sized_or_keeps_an_odd_edge` classifies it), in the
  asked-size loop and in both "lists what `h264` lists" loops.
- **`hevc_alpha_proof.py`** (not in `make test`: it launches the app). One
  Release instance per run in a scratch home under
  `tools/proof/work/hevc-alpha/` (removed at start and exit), on its own
  socket, with every key of `screens.py`'s `PINS` as a launch argument, the
  inspector at 280 pt and the export choice pinned to `hevc_alpha`. Two
  menu-driven acts, neither persisting: File ▸ Export… (opened, read,
  cancelled — nothing in a sheet is pressed) and the inspector's Document
  tab. Twelve fixtures, every export one second, the largest frame
  1296 × 728. The full rows and the two controls, three launches, took
  25 s together here.
  The phase A rows are scored again with `hevc_alpha` added to R1 and R2
  and with E2 requiring the Format popup to read "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)"
  alone, so a pin that did not take fails E2 (the phase A build could not
  tell). T0 reads B6's four phrases off `tools/list`.
  **A1** a hard-edged opaque red card on a clear 640 × 360 canvas as
  `hevc_alpha`: the answer says `hevc_alpha` / `mov` / `hevc_alpha`, the
  path ends `.mov`, ffprobe says `hevc` / `hvc1` (and `yuv420p` — it cannot
  see the alpha), and decoded the frame holds two alphas, 0 and 255, with
  no pixel wrong more than 4 px from the card's edge. **A2** the card at
  half opacity decodes (129,0,0,128) at its centre. **A3** on an opaque
  canvas every alpha is 255. **A4** at `720p`: 1280 × 720, corner 0,
  centre 255. **A5** with a tone on a second track: an `aac` stream, 48000
  Hz, 2 channels, and `loudness` in the answer ("Peak −14.0 dBTP · −14.7
  LUFS").
  **S1** 640 × 480 on 640 × 360 as `hevc_alpha`, and **S2** 402 × 100 on
  400 × 100 as `prores_4444` and as `hevc_alpha`, are refused in the shape
  sentence, naming both sizes, with no file.
  **O1** a clear 321 × 181 and a clear 181 × 320 document as `hevc_alpha`
  with no size, and `[321, 181]` asked on 640 × 360: written at the even
  size the answer names, every pixel of all four edges alpha 0, the centre
  255. **O2** `prores_4444` keeps 321 × 181, and writes a typed 180 × 320
  on 181 × 320 (which the earlier guard refused) with all four edges 0.
  **O3** `apng` keeps 321 × 181. **O4** the 321 × 181 document at `720p`
  as `hevc_alpha`: 1276 × 720, all four edges 0. **O5** (fix pass 1) on
  the clear 640 × 360 document, `hevc_alpha` asked `[400, 225]` and
  `[1296, 729]` — odd sizes in the canvas's own proportions, one smaller
  than it and one larger — is not refused: the answer and the file are
  400 × 224 and 1296 × 728, all four edges 0, the centre 255; and
  `prores_4444` at a typed `[400, 224]` is written the same. The build
  before the first arm was amended REFUSED all three in the shape sentence
  ("…and 400 × 224 is a different shape…"), which is this row's red.
  **P1**, **P2** a clear
  334 × 222 document at `720p` (1084 × 720, 0.76 px off shape) as
  `hevc_alpha` and `prores_4444`: all four edges 0.
  **B2** a white 334 × 222 document at `720p` as `hevc`, `h264` and
  `prores_422`: the last three columns of the middle row read 253–254
  where the baseline's last two are black. **B3** the two odd red
  documents on those three rows: all eight edge pixels red (253–254 on
  321 × 181, 250 on 181 × 320) where the baseline has two black among
  them. **L1** 334 × 222 at `[640, 640]` is letterboxed, black at the top
  and bottom. **L2** 400 × 100 at `[402, 100]`: exactly two black pixels in
  the middle row, columns 400 and 401, the baseline's.
  **N1** the Document tab reads "Transparent — kept by 3 export formats."
  once, 183 pt wide, not truncated. **E1** the sheet opens on "HEVC with
  Alpha (MOV)", its footnote's text is "HEVC_ALPHA · MOV · alpha", and the
  footnote's `tooltip` in the layout dump is that same whole line.
  B1, B4, H0 and Z1 are phase A's. **X1** is scored only under
  `--mutant encoder-refused`.

**What E1 does NOT score, and why it is printed.** The spec's row also
required that no `truncated` problem name the footnote. That is false on
the built app and was before this phase: beside the sheet's three buttons
the footnote's slot is 88 pt, and "HEVC_ALPHA · MOV · alpha" — like the
shipped "PRORES4444 · MOV · alpha" — needs 144, so both are drawn cut with
a tail ellipsis, before the word "alpha" (measured, all three rows
compared: "H264 · MP4" is 60 pt in 64). What E1 DOES score since fix
pass 1 is where the whole line can still be read: `syncReadout`
(`ExportSheetResolve.swift`) writes the footnote's tooltip after its text
and clears it with the text, the layout dump carries each view's `tooltip`
(`UISnapshotLayout.swift`; first 200 characters, `null` for none and for a
secure field), and E1 requires the footnote's to equal its text. Its red:
on a build with the dump's key and without those two lines the tooltip
read the empty string `sheetFootnote("")` set once, and E1 failed.
Only the `hevc_alpha` sheet is opened; ProRes 4444's footnote takes the
same two lines and has no row. E1 still prints the cut on its line in
every run: giving the summary room on the sheet's FACE (a line of its
own, a wider sheet) is a visible change to every format's sheet and the
owner's choice, not a row's. G-33 (a) and (h) and the manual check SE-9
say the same.

**Controls** (no build), each exit 0. `--control plain-hevc-reader`: A1's
and A2's pixel readers over plain `hevc` exports of the same two projects
both FAIL (every alpha 255: 203,100 pixels outside the card are not 0;
the half card's centre is (129,0,0,255)). `--control sheet-default`: with
`screens.py`'s empty export choice the sheet opens on "H.264 (MP4)" and E1
FAILS.

**Mutants**, each one `tree_copy.make_copy`, every anchor asserted to
occur once, built by the copy's own `make app` (99–133 s here), each exit
0. `encoder-refused` — an encoder specification nothing satisfies for
`.hevcWithAlpha`: A1 FAILS and X1 PASSES ("This Mac cannot export with the
“hevc_alpha” preset.", nothing at the path); relaunched with
`RC_MUTANT_UNMAPPED`, which turns `encoderOutcome` off, X1 FAILS: the tool
answers "Cannot Encode" and a 0-byte file is left. `report-and-fill` —
`Preset::even_sized` false and `fillsTheBox` false: R1, R2, R4, E2 FAIL
(the answer and the sheet say 321 × 181 over a 320 × 180 file) and O1,
O5, P1, P2, B2, B3 FAIL (edges at alpha 15–16 on `hevc_alpha` and 255 on
`prores_4444`; two black columns or rows), while R3, S1, S2, L1, L2 PASS.
`shape-and-note` — the guard skipped for `.hevcWithAlpha`, the note
always joined, `limit` `max(cw, ch)` for every frame: S1, N1, L2 and S2
FAIL (S2's `prores_4444` half by the limit alone: 402 × 100 is written;
L2 has no black column; the joined three-name note is truncated) while L1
and O1 PASS; relaunched with `RC_MUTANT_FILL_ALL`, L1 FAILS (white at the
top and bottom). **The copy's `core/` is its own for `report-and-fill`**
(`own_core`): `make_copy` links `core` to the tree's, so an anchor
replaced through the link would be replaced in the TREE; the script
refuses any anchor whose file resolves outside the copy, copies `src/` and
the two Cargo files, links `include/`, and clones the tree's release
artifacts (`cp -c`) so the copy compiles the local crates only. The first
run of this mutant found a fault in the SCRIPT, not the product: a mutant's
launch was not handed the baseline, so L2's "columns equal the baseline's"
clause failed; mutants and controls are handed it now, and that mutant was
built again (four mutant builds in all).

**Gate A after phase B.** `--rows size` on this build prints 10/11 and
exits 1: G1 requires the pad the baseline recorded and an unknown
`hevc_alpha`, and this build fills and lists the row. G1's line ends "RED
BY DESIGN: this build holds phase B…" and the last line reads "10/11 — G1
is RED BY DESIGN on a build that holds phase B; it is Gate A's row and
the only one that failed". The gate was passed where it belongs, on the
phase A build (fcfeebf). The exit status stays 1 on purpose: a gate that
answered 0 here would no longer be red on a tree that already fills.

**Another host.** The baseline is this host's bytes (previous section).
Phase B's decision on what that section left open: on a host that is not
the baseline's, **the rows that read no digest are scored**, B1 and B4
(and G1 under `--rows size`) print a `skip` line naming both hosts, L2
drops its "columns equal the baseline's" clause and says so, the last line
is `n/n — not scored: …`, and the script exits **2** when everything it
scored passed — the claim is incomplete there, which is the instrument's
answer and not the product's — and 1 when a scored row failed. Run once
here by import, the baseline aimed at a copy stamped "Apple M1 · macOS
15.6 · ffmpeg 7.1": 27/27, B1 and B4 skipped, exit 2. So a macOS or ffmpeg
update on this Mac no longer silences the alpha, fill and size rows; it
withholds the two "the old file is byte for byte the old file" rows until
a baseline is recorded for the new host.

**I1, printed and never scored** (for the issue G-33 (h) names): a
half-opaque red card over an opaque white canvas, re-imported from the
`hevc_alpha` file, renders (191,127,127) at the card's centre, and from
the `prores_4444` file (193,129,127); a correct composite is about
(255,128,128). The files' own centre pixels decode (129,0,0,128) and
(129,0,0,129).

**Fix pass 1 (2026-10-05, the review of phase B).** Two findings, each
shown red before its fix. *The first arm.* As first built — the canvas
ITSELF less at most a pixel on each axis — `shapeGap` refused an odd size
typed in the canvas's own proportions on `hevc_alpha` (the core evens
`[720, 405]` on 1920 × 1080 to 720 × 404: gap 1920, limit 1080). The arm
is now a canvas-SHAPED size less at most a pixel on each axis, and O5 is
its row. *The tooltip.* E1's new clause, above. **The red build** was the
tree with the dump's `tooltip` key and neither fix: 28/30, O5 FAILED (all
three exports refused in the shape sentence, naming 400 × 224, 1296 × 728
and 400 × 224) and E1 FAILED (`tooltip ['']`). On the fixed build 30/30.
`report-and-fill` names O5 and was built again (O5 FAILS there: the answer
says `[400, 225]` and `[1296, 729]` over files of 400 × 224 and
1296 × 728 with edge alphas 0, 15 and 16, and `prores_4444`'s edges hold
255), and `shape-and-note` was built again unchanged (its third anchor is
the line under the one that changed); `encoder-refused` was not — its two
anchors still occur once and its rows did not change. **The integer
sweep**, run again with the amended arm as its own column (`shaped`,
beside `pad` and `tight`; 9 s, no encoder; `r12b.swift` and
`run12-rule-shaped.txt` are in the batch's handoff folder under
`measurement/fix-1/`, not in the repository): the evened Document rows
(4,196,351 exact, 12,572,674 filled, 0 neither) and the standard rows
(1,961,452 / 65,114,648 / 0) are the tight arm's counts, no standard row's
verdict differs, and 4,094 of the 8,192 one-pixel-edge canvases are still
neither. Of every size in the canvas's own proportions with each edge in
2…8192, evened, the tight arm refused or letterboxed 256 of 512 on
1920 × 1080, on 640 × 360 and on 1080 × 1920, 1,023 of 2,047 on
400 × 100, 1,364 of 2,729 on 300 × 100 and 12 of 25 on 181 × 320 (none
on the other four); the amended arm none, on each of the ten canvases.
Typed frames within 8 px of nine canvases that the amended
arm newly fills: 396 × 98 and 404 × 100 on 400 × 100 on the even-sized
rows, seven there on `prores_4444`, none on the other eight; none that
the tight arm wrote is letterboxed or refused. The frames of L1, L2, S1
and S2 — and 736 × 90 on 728 × 90, 2560 × 1080 on 2558 × 1080, 394 × 98
on 400 × 100 — are past the limit under both. A typed size of ANOTHER
shape is judged as the even frame it becomes: 1279 × 720 on 1920 × 1080
is filled on `prores_4444` and, as 1278 × 720, past the limit on
`hevc_alpha` (arithmetic; no row).

**B1 compares no byte count (fix pass 2, 2026-10-05, the second review
of phase B).** What led to it: the first full run on fix pass 1's build
printed 29/30: B1, `hevc` on an even canvas, "differs in ['format',
'stream']" with frame 0's digest, the alphas and the corner equal — and
the values were not on the line, and the file was gone with the work
folder. Read again on the same build: equal alone, equal after T0, R1, R3
and R4 (the rows that precede its export in a full run), equal in the
next full run (30/30) and equal in five more launches — eight of eight.
The build before that fix read it equal too, and nothing in that pass
touches an exact-shape frame's encoder dictionary (`gap == 0`). The row
then compared ffprobe's exact `size` and `bit_rate` of a 3,782-byte
hardware HEVC bitstream: byte counts, which the encoder does not promise
to repeat and which are not what the row is for. **What the row does
now:** it drops the stream's `bit_rate` and the file's `size` and
`bit_rate` from BOTH sides before `held` — `B1_UNSCORED`, a constant of
its own, so `STREAM_KEYS` and `FORMAT_KEYS` still read them and the
baseline file is as it was recorded — and prints them under its line as
"printed, not scored", beside the baseline's. Still compared: the
stream's `codec_name`, `codec_tag_string`, `profile`, `level`, `pix_fmt`,
`width`, `height`, `r_frame_rate`, `avg_frame_rate`, `nb_frames` and four
colour values; the file's `format_name`, `nb_streams` and `duration`; the
extension, the answer's and the file's size, the alphas, the corner,
frame 0's digest and the samples. B4, G1 and L2's baseline clause read
decoded pixels only and did not change. **Shown by import** (`demo_b1.py`
and its kept output, in the batch's handoff folder under
`measurement/fix-2/`, not in the repository): one launch, one export,
and `row_b1` itself scored over today's case and six altered copies of
it. As the app wrote it, and with only the three values altered (to
21082, 3839 and 30712): ok, "equal". With `stream.profile`,
`stream.nb_frames`, `format.duration` or `frame0` altered, and with the
three values AND the profile altered: FAIL, each line naming the one
value that moved and none of the three — 7 of 7 as expected. In every
read of this pass the three values were the baseline's own (19848, 3782,
30256). **Which values moved in the one failed run is not known** — no
run printed them — so nothing here says it was these three; had it been
the frame count or the duration, the row still fails, by name, and that
would be the product's. **What the row gives up:** a change of the
encoder's rate no longer fails it. On this 640 × 360 fixture it could
not see the line of `defaultVideoBitrate` phase B changed in any case:
483,840 at 0.07 bits a pixel and 967,680 at 0.14 are both raised to the
1,000,000 floor (arithmetic, not run). `held` prints every value that
moved (fix pass 1's change), which stays.

**The dump's `tooltip` key and its other readers (fix pass 2).** Fix
pass 1 added `tooltip` to every view's record in the layout dump
(`UISnapshotLayout.swift`) and ran E1, `phase7_chrome.py` and
`phase7_proof.py` after it; two readers of the dump were not run. No
reader compares whole dumps — `screens.py --compare` and
`v2_snapshot.py`'s `same_bytes` compare PNGs, and every reader takes a
record's keys by name — and both were run on the same build to hold it:
`v2_snapshot.py` (which builds `v2_layout_probe.swift` over
`UISnapshotLayout.swift`; 120 s) on an instance of its own in a scratch
home with V2a's pinned launch arguments, an empty `-RCSecretFolder` and
a `-RCSpendFolder` that does not exist: 29 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip — O2,
the named host skip "editor occluded without the cover" — P1–P7 and
L1–L3 among the passes, O5 "38 of 38 captures had active false", no
`Reelcut: ` line; and `screens.py --only 12-export-sheet` under a scratch
home, light then dark: 6 pass of 6, 0 new problems, each dump 60 records
with the key on every one and the footnote's `"H264 · MP4"` as both its
text and its tooltip. Spec §7.9a's sentence on what a record holds now
names the tooltip.

**What is not proved here.** Any other Mac's encoders; playback in Safari,
QuickTime Player and Final Cut (SE-9), and that the footnote's tooltip

## Publishing — the app the workflow is about to pack (`published_check.py` P1–P16; spec §11 PUB-1..PUB-5)

`.github/workflows/publish.yml` archives the Distribution configuration with a
Developer ID identity, exports the archive (which signs the app a second
time) and runs this over the exported `Reelcut.app` before it builds the DMG;
a failed row fails the step and nothing is packed, notarized or released.
`make dist` runs it too, after `dist_check.py`, over the local Distribution
build and with no `--version` or `--build`, so the instrument is exercised on
every local Distribution build. It holds what Apple's notary does not look
at, read with `dist_check.py`'s own readers (imported, not copied):

- **P1** the needle reads from the seam; **P2** the binary exists; **P3** it
  does not hold the needle (no positive control here: that is `dist_check.py`
  D4, which needs a Release bundle the workflow never builds);
- **P4** the app is signed with the hardened runtime and `codesign --verify
  --strict` accepts it, which also fails when anything nested was changed
  after the app was sealed; **P5** its entitlements are exactly `audio-input`;
- **P6–P9** the assistant helper: present, hardened runtime, entitlements
  exactly `allow-jit`, no needle;
- **P10–P12** the MCP proxy: present, hardened runtime, no entitlements;
- **P13** the catalog snapshot is at the bundle's version; **P14** it names no
  dev tool;
- **P15** `CFBundleShortVersionString` is `--version` (without one: two or
  three dot-separated integers); **P16** `CFBundleVersion` is `--build`
  (without one: an integer).

No row is skipped; the last line is `published_check: <passed>/16` and the
exit is 0 only at 16/16.

```sh
make dist                                                   # → dist_check: 24/24, published_check: 16/16
python3 tools/proof/published_check.py --app APP [--version V --build N]
```

**Measured, 2026-10-04.** The workflow's own archive line, run locally with
the ad-hoc identity and `MARKETING_VERSION=0.2.999 CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=999`
after `make project`, exits 0, and the archived app scores 16/16 with
`--version 0.2.999 --build 999` (the snapshot reads `0.2.999`, 86 tools); the
same line had passed from a COLD `core/target` and `mcp-proxy/target` before
the base moved to the `VERSION` file. `make dist` scores 24/24 and 16/16, the
Distribution bundle reading `0.2` and `0`. What no local run reaches — the
Developer ID identity, the `developer-id` export's re-sign, the notary, the
release — is first tested by the first push to `publish`.

**The `VERSION` file (spec §11 PUB-2), made to fail.** `make project` in a
folder holding the tree's `Makefile` and `project.yml` and no `VERSION` stops
at `cat: VERSION: No such file or directory`, exit 1, and writes no project.
A copy of the Distribution bundle with `CFBundleShortVersionString` set to
the empty string — what a bare `xcodegen generate` builds — scores 13/16: P15
FAIL, and P13 and P4 with it. `tree_copy.py` copies `VERSION` beside
`project.yml` and `Makefile` (`COPIED_FILES`), because a proof's `make app`
in a copy runs `make project` there; its selftest is 5/5, T2 naming all
three files.

**The cold archive found a defect in "Build Rust Core"**, fixed in the same
change: with `SDKROOT` unset (#225) and Xcode's toolchain `clang` first on
the script's `PATH`, a cold build of rquickjs-sys's C stopped at
`'stdlib.h' file not found` (measured: that `clang` with no `SDKROOT` fails
on a one-line `#include <stdlib.h>`, `/usr/bin/cc` does not). `make app` never
met it because `make rust` builds first. The step now puts `/usr/bin` ahead,
and #225's property still holds: after the cold archive, `make rust` finishes
in 0.19 s and compiles nothing.

## Issue batch B86 phase 1 — three word-caption looks in the model, the recipe and the picture (`core/tests/word_looks.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v12.rs`, four core mutants; `word_looks_proof.py` H0, B1, W3, G1–G3, F1–F3, D1–D3, S1, R1, Z1 and six mutants; `word_looks_baseline.json`; `words_picture_probe.py` P2, P10, P11–P16, seven mutants and `--power-selftest`; #96; spec §11 W-12, W-13, W-14)

`word_style` gains three keys, each off by default — `active_pill.glide` (the
pill slides), `active_fill` (the active word fills as it is said) and
`pause_dim` (the page dims in a pause) — at format version 12; the recipe
carries `word_glide`, `word_fill` and `word_dim`; `LayerRenderersWords.swift`
draws them. They are reachable through `set_text` only: the Generate
Captions sheet and `transcribe` are phase 2.

**What is proved, and by which instrument.**

- **`core/tests/word_looks.rs`** (in `make test`), through the FFI, every
  expected number computed in the test from the four durations written out
  there. Per key: a word boundary, inside a word, a pause on each side of
  0.25 s (one tick apart), the first and the last word, the tail against the
  clip's duration (one tick apart again), a late first word (the page opens
  dim, no ramp down), two abutting pages (the first ends dim; the second
  opens with `word_glide` null, `word_fill` 0, `word_dim` 0), a word shorter
  than the 0.6 s cap (full at its `end`) and one longer (full at the cap,
  1.0 after), a next word sooner than the 0.2 s glide, equal starts, an
  unsorted list and `i64::MIN` / `i64::MAX` ticks (in 0..1, no panic), all
  three null on an unstyled page, an untimed styled page, a count mismatch
  and the burn-in, the keys' order in the source text, the hash (two fill
  fractions, two glide fractions and two dim levels differ; a dim plateau
  and two instants past the cap are equal), and `pause_dim`'s refusals by
  name at `set_text` and `add_text_clip`. The recipe's numbers are compared
  at nine decimals: the FFI's JSON reads back an ulp from the f64 written.
- **`core/tests/schema_v12.rs`** (in `make test`): versions 9–11 read with
  the three keys off and 1–8 with no style; a version-11 style keeps its six
  keys and its pill's three; absent equals spelled-out defaults (the written
  text); the key order off the written text (`glide` closes the pill,
  `active_fill` then `pause_dim` close the style, `word_style` still closes
  the text); a page with all three round-trips twice to the same bytes; each
  key patched alone keeps the others; a wrong kind and an unknown key are
  refused by path. No test writes the current version as a literal.
- **`word_looks_proof.py`** (not in `make test`: it launches the app, twice,
  each in the scratch home `tools/proof/work/word-looks/home`, on its own
  socket, performs no menu item, closes what it opens). H0 and Z1 are
  CONTROLS. **B1** holds a hand-written version-11 package's 41 frames —
  the five shipped word styles, an untimed styled page, a plain title and a
  typewriter, a `word_fade` and a `line_rise` title, at the instants its
  docstring lists — to the SHA-256 digests in `word_looks_baseline.json`.
  **The baseline is one host's bytes and one build's, and says which**:
  recorded by `--record-baseline` (two launches, written only when every
  digest agrees) from the build of `d8fa4fa`, BEFORE any B86 code, on host
  `25F80 arm64`. So on that host B1 says an existing project draws exactly
  as it did before the three keys. On another host, or with no file, B1 is a
  control FAILURE that says to re-record — never a pass or a skip — and a
  re-recording pins the build it is made on instead (`recorded_from` says
  which); the pre-B86 anchor holds for the recording host only. **W3** runs
  `words_picture_proof.py` (road map 8's R1–R7, R6 reading `set_text`'s
  description) on the second launch. G1–G3 the glide, F1–F3 the fill, D1–D3
  the dim, each read off `render_frame` PNGs of a 640×360 fixture with no
  pop and saturated colours on black (the plate red, spoken ink green,
  upcoming ink blue), through the script's own PNG decoder; S1 the door.
  Three things the fix pass added: **F1 also holds the fill's edge to a
  whole pixel** (at ¼ and ¾, where the edge falls inside a letter, the last
  active-colour column and the first upcoming-colour one are adjacent, and
  at no fraction does a pixel of the word carry both colours); **D3** is the
  dim as ONE opacity over the words and the pill together (white active ink
  over a red pill: on the plateau the ink is grey, `1 − pause_dim` of
  itself with no plate through it, where an opacity applied to each drawing
  in turn would leave it a quarter red); and **R1** is the recording's own
  gate: **`--record-baseline` refuses, exit 2, before it launches anything,
  while `git status --porcelain -- app core graphic` prints a line** (or
  cannot be read), because `recorded_from` names a commit and a build of
  uncommitted sources is no commit's picture. R1 shows it on a sample
  status, on an unreadable one, and — when the tree it runs in has such
  changes — by calling the recording itself, and holds the baseline file to
  the bytes it had.
- **`words_picture_probe.py`** (not in `make test`: it compiles
  `app/Sources`). P2's sweep now draws every page, at every word and pop,
  also half FILLED and — a config with a pill — GLIDING at `glide` 0 and 0.5
  (word ≥ 2), over the same bitmap, so `overflow_px` is the worst of all of
  them: no look puts ink outside the box. **P10** times
  `text(_:hash:reveal:)` on a cache miss — a raster and an upload, the
  words spike's q5 method — on the Highlight preset's own page
  (Montserrat-Black at 0.075 × min(w, h)) at 1080×1920 and 3840×2160: one
  untimed warm-up, then the median of 20, for `pop` 0.5 (the shipped
  comparator, never scored), `fill` 0.5, `fill` 0.5 with `dim` 0.5 at
  `pause_dim` 0.5, and `glide` 0.5 with the default pill; measured before
  the sweep. Since the fix pass it also times the fill with the dim in ONE
  WORD's style — the largest type a preset ships, 0.12 × min(w, h), and a
  dim's layer costs by the box. **P10 scores two pages in the presets' own
  styles**: Highlight's line and, as `oneword-page fill+dim`, One Word's
  page, which is one word (`maxWords` 1). Beside them it prints, never
  scored, as `pop` is, a HAND-MADE page of large type:
  `oneword-line fill+dim (hand-made)`, the same six words on one line at One
  Word's size, which no preset makes and `set_text` can write. (Pass 1 of
  the fix scored that line, as `oneword fill+dim`, and printed the one-word
  page; pass 1b swapped them.) **Every P10 page is one line (`width`
  nil)**, where a generated page is cut to its style's width, so Highlight's
  scored line is wider than any its pager makes. Budgets: 4 ms at 1080×1920 (half of spec §7.5's 8 ms
  frame: a fill pays it on every frame of a word), 8 ms at 3840×2160.
  `--raster-budget-ms N` replaces both; a `--mutant` run does not score P10.
  **P10 is judged only on an unthrottled host**: the probe reads
  `ProcessInfo`'s Low Power Mode flag and thermal state before the first
  raster and after the last, the scorer prints them beside the medians, and
  with Low Power Mode on or a thermal state above nominal the row is
  `P10 not judged: <why>` — a control FAILURE with the medians printed,
  never a pass or a skip. `--power-selftest` feeds the scorer made-up
  answers (T1–T8: Low Power Mode, each thermal reading, no power state, an
  unthrottled host under budget and at budget 0, a throttled one at budget
  0) and builds nothing. **`--only P10` runs P10 alone** — under two
  minutes, nearly all of it the probe's build — through the probe's
  `--quick`, which stops before the sweep; `--only` takes any of P10–P16.
  **P11–P16** are the looks' geometry, each value the recipe would carry
  set exactly and the picture read off `textBitmap`: P11 the gliding
  plate's four edges between two LINES (x, y and width all travel, at
  `easeOut`); P12 the plate popping about its own centre; P13 the one-piece
  condition (a token that wraps over two lines takes the settled pill,
  sliding onto it and off it); P14 a wrapped token filling each piece by
  the same fraction; P15 a full word drawn whole (on an outlined build
  page `word_fill` 1 is the unfilled page byte for byte, though the stroke
  reaches past where 0.999 is cut); P16 a value outside 0…1 drawing as the
  nearest one inside, for `word_fill`, `word_glide`, `word_dim` and
  `pause_dim` on each side, and a full dim at `pause_dim` 1 drawing nothing.

**What P10 says, and the limit it does not score.** As measured in phase 1;
phase 3 took the dim out of the raster — see that section. A fill and a glide
cost what the shipped pop costs on the same page (about 1.2 ms at 1080×1920
and 2.5 ms at 3840×2160). The dim is the cost: it draws the words and the
pill inside one transparency layer over the whole text box (spec §11
W-14), so it costs by the box. P10 scores two pages in the presets' own styles,
and judged in High Power each is inside its budget: a fill with a dim took
7.174 ms on Highlight's line at 3840×2160 and 4.982 ms on One Word's
one-word page (7.382 ms and 4.915 ms in pass 1b's run). **A hand-made page
of large type is over, and is a known limit, not a scored row**: six words
on one line at One Word's size, which no preset makes and `set_text` can
write, read 9.529 ms at 3840×2160 on a dim's ramp frames against the 8 ms
budget (2026-10-05, High Power, on battery, thermal state nominal; 9.759 ms
in pass 1b's run). The dim is paid on the frames of a ramp only (0.1 s
down, 0.1 s up per pause); the plateau is one cached texture. The probe is
an unoptimised build, so the numbers are an upper reading of the app's.
`designs/adr/roadmap-08-word-captions.md`'s Known limits carries it.
**The verdict depended on the power state**, which is why P10 reads it: in
Low Power Mode the first pass read 9.268 ms on Highlight's page at
3840×2160, over the budget the judged run is inside. An earlier run of that
day scored a page nobody ships (pill, pop, outline and a 0.55-alpha upcoming
colour at once), measured after the ten-minute sweep, on which the shipped
pop itself read 9.111 ms at 3840×2160; P10 was then re-based on the
Highlight preset's own page and moved ahead of the sweep, budgets unchanged.

**Limits.** P11–P16 read `textBitmap`, the bitmap `renderText` uploads,
not a `render_frame` PNG. No row can see two things, because removing each
changes no pixel: the early return at a full dim (a layer at opacity 0
composites nothing either), and the clamps named above that P16's mutant
left standing, each taken alone. No row of phase 1 sees the plate's HEIGHT travel: every line of a page
in one face has the same ascent and descent (phase 2's P17 does, on a page
whose second line is set in a fallback face — the next section). B1's anchor to the picture
before B86 holds on the recording host only. No row plays a page: whether a glide looks right, whether a fill
keeps time with a voice and whether a dim reads well are a person's, and
phase 2 lists them in `docs/manual-checks.md`. `render_frame` is the one
door measured; preview and export draw text through the same `Compositor`
(`Compositor.swift` → `LayerRenderers.text`), so there is no export row.

## Issue batch B86 phase 3 — the pause dim leaves the transparency layer (#245, spec §11 W-16)

One host, **2026-10-07, 09:22–10:15 CEST**: on AC power, `pmset -g | grep
powermode` reading 0 every time it was read — at the start, and before and
after every timing run and `make test`. Every proof launch ran under a
scratch home and its stderr was empty; no run printed `DEFAULTS MOVED`.

**What is proved, and by which row.** On a timed page with NO backdrop the
pause dim is the text layer's opacity in the compositor
(`RecipeLayer.drawnOpacity`), and the bitmap is the undimmed page's byte for
byte: `words_picture_probe` **P18** (and the rule's amounts and clamps); a
dim therefore adds nothing to a raster: **P10**'s "the dim adds", each
`… fill+dim` against its `… fill` twin of the same run; the dimmed frame is
still one opacity over the words and the pill: `word_looks_proof` **D1**,
**D3** (now the compositor's multiply), with **B1** and **D2** holding the
undimmed bytes. On a page WITH a backdrop the dim is still W-14's
transparency layer in the bitmap, and the backdrop never dims: **D4** (new),
P18's backdrop half, and **P19** (new), which prints the layer's distance from
the probe's own arithmetic. P16 now reads the clamps off `drawWords` itself.

**Step 2's gate and outcome: not begun.** The spec designed a second step for
the backdrop page — the words and the pill drawn first, one `destinationIn`
multiply, the backdrop filled under them with `destinationOver`, no layer —
to be kept only at or under 5.0 ms at 3840×2160 and 2.5 ms at 1080×1920 on
`karaoke-2line-backdrop fill+dim (hand-made)`, and gated first on the same
page with NO dim. Both judged step 1 runs read that page at 6.359 ms and
6.341 ms at 3840×2160 — over the keep limit before any dim is drawn — so no
draw of the dim could meet it, and the step was not built. The backdrop pair
stays printed and unscored; P19's distance stays printed.

**Limits.** D4 is one backdrop colour on one page. No row plays a ramp: D1's
ramp frame is one frame. There is no export row: `MetalRenderer.uniforms(for:)`
is the one reader of a layer's opacity for preview, `render_frame` and both
export passes, and `textBitmap` the one bitmap, so no line an export-only
mutant could change exists. There is no nest row: the core flattens a nest
into ordinary layers drawn by the same loop, a nested text layer keeps its
`.text` source and reveal, and a nest has no code of its own here. The probe
is an unoptimised build, so its medians are an upper reading of the app's.

## Issue batch B87 phase 2 — an action animates a graphic's props over MCP (`graphic_prop_action_proof.py` H0, T0, F0, A1, B1, S1, U1, C1, E0, E1, R1–R3, N1, F1, F2, Z1 and two mutants; #239, spec §11 G-34)

**What it proves.** `set_action_end`'s handler (`AgentServer+Actions.swift`)
fills `schema` from the CURRENT revision of the module the action's clip is
drawn by — found in the call's scope — when the patch names `graphic`, and
the evaluated props reach the picture: `render_frame` halfway through the
action, a `prores_422` export with the graphic prefetch on and off, and
undo. The module is the proof's own `ramp` (one rectangle whose `x`, `fill`
and `mode` are props) on a 640×360, 30 fps canvas; the action runs 0.5–1.5 s,
linear.

    python3 tools/proof/graphic_prop_action_proof.py
    python3 tools/proof/graphic_prop_action_proof.py --mutant recipe-stored-props
    python3 tools/proof/graphic_prop_action_proof.py --mutant handler-no-schema

Two instances, one after the other, each launched by the script under the
scratch home `tools/proof/work/graphic-prop-action/home` and stopped by its
own pid; everything it writes is under `tools/proof/work/graphic-prop-action/`,
removed at the start and at exit. Instance 2 runs with the launch argument
`-ReelcutGraphicPrefetchOff YES`, which lives in the volatile argument domain.

Under `--mutant` (rule R: 0 caught, 1 survived, 2 not performed) a row
marked failed only because its fixture was never built is not a catch: the
run answers 2 unless F0 held, and for `recipe-stored-props` (C1) unless the
still control Q was built too (added after review, 2026-10-07).

**Rows.** H0 (CONTROL) the scratch home took. T0 (CONTROL) the tool publishes
no `schema` and the gate refuses one ("set_action_end does not take schema.",
after `mcp.ToolError`'s `set_action_end: ` prefix). F0 the fixture (the
default curve is already linear, so `set_action`'s "made no change" is
accepted and the curve read back). A1 the end lands with `props` and the
op's `kinds`, and the clip's props hold the three defaults. B1 at the mid
tick the edge is at x = 96.5 — (80,60) background where the still frame is
red, (150,60) #800080, (96,60) the half-covered column — and the frame 20000
ticks later differs (CONTROL). S1 the string switches at the END tick. U1
undo answers "Action End" and restores the project and the mid frame's
bytes; redo restores the animated bytes. C1 the mid and end frames are
byte-equal to a STILL control clip holding the evaluated values (project Q).
E0 (CONTROL) Q.mov's decoded frames 10 and 30 — one still picture — are
byte-equal: the encoder is stable for identical input frames. E1 P-on.mov's
frame 30 is byte-equal to Q.mov's frame 30 and differs from its own frame 10;
this byte comparison rests on ProRes 422 being INTRA-frame (a frame's bytes
depend only on its own picture, which E0 shows for this encoder), and no PNG
is ever compared with a ProRes frame (lossy 4:2:2 YUV). R1 a shape clip's
action: "clip N is not a graphic clip". R2 after v2 (`x` max 100, a new `h`):
`{x: 129}` refused by v2's range, `{h: 40}` lands and the clip gains `h: 10`,
so the CURRENT revision went. R3 after a v3 that does not compile: a value is
refused ("needs its module's schema to animate, and none came with the op")
and `{mode: null}` still removes. N1 with `scope` = the nest's id, the nested
clip's end takes `x: 30`. F1 P-on.mov equals P-off.mov (`same_movie`). F2 the
one `graphic prefetch:` line instance 1 logged between the start of the
P-on export and the start of the Q export says hits > 0 and mismatched 0
(read from log offsets, since the Q export logs its own line); instance 2
logs none. Z1 (CONTROL) no `Reelcut: ` line; each log's tail printed.

## Issue batch B87 phase 4 — a long checkbox label gives way to "at end" (`graphics_inspector_proof.py` K18c and two more mutants; #239, spec §11 G-34 (l))

**What it proves.** O8's last gap: a row with no popup gives its widest
checkbox the 749 (`inspectorRow`), so a module's boolean whose label is longer
than about 200 pt narrows while keyed and its "at end" stays whole. K18c
relabels six's `showBox` "Show the long descriptive label for this toggle" —
wider than the keyed row's 222 pt and narrower than the unkeyed row's 264 pt in
both the app's Source Sans 3 (228) and the system face the probe draws in
(260) — keys it, and lays Properties out at `DS.panelWidth`, held: the
checkbox 222/260, its compression resistance 749 against the tag's 750, the
tag 40/40 inside the inset; not keyed, no tag and the checkbox 260/260. The
checkbox draws its title from a point and a view does not clip to its bounds
by default (macOS 14 on), so a narrowed one drew its title on under the tag;
the rule clips that checkbox, and K18c reads the row's cached drawing: no ink
between the checkbox and the tag, and over the tag exactly the tag's own ink
alone (409 against 409). The priority is asserted, not only the widths: with
the checkbox and the tag tied at 750 this solver happens to narrow the
checkbox anyway (measured under `checkbox-fixed-width` before the assertion,
checkbox 222 and tag 40/40), and a tie is an ambiguity, not a rule. The gap is
read with the tag-region comparison because the first form, the 3 pt gap
alone, landed on the space between "this" and "toggle" and missed the spill.

| Mutant | Anchor | Must fail | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkbox-fixed-width` | `InspectorRows.swift` `(popups.isEmpty ? checks : popups)` → `popups` | K18c | `MUTANT PASS`, exactly that, 111 s (compression resistance 750 against 750; over the tag 840 against 409) |
| `checkbox-title-unclipped` | `InspectorRows.swift` the `if narrowing is OptionCheckboxControl { narrowing.clipsToBounds = true }` line deleted | K18c | `MUTANT PASS`, exactly that, 116 s (over the tag 840 against 409) |
| `popup-fixed-width` | (phase 3) now fails K18c too: the same 749 is the checkbox's | K18a K18b K18c | `MUTANT PASS`, exactly those, 116 s (the checkbox 1000, 258/260, the tag cut to 4/40) |

**Its record** (2026-10-07, `powermode 0`): `graphics_inspector_proof.py`
91/91, exit 0, Z1 empty, no `DEFAULTS MOVED`; the three mutants above
`MUTANT PASS`. The other 27 mutants were not run again: none has an anchor in
`InspectorRows.swift`, and K18c writes its end through the probe's own
`set_action_end` (as K3 and K11 do) and reads only layout and drawing.
`clip_inspector3_proof.py` 31/31 and `clip_inspector4_proof.py` 46/46,
`spec_index_proof.py` 141/141.
The first run of K18c (91 rows, 90 passed) failed it on its own fixture: the
label was "… for this toggle box", 282 pt in the probe's face, wider than the
unkeyed row.

## Road map mattes — MT0, the matte spike (`matte_spike/`; spec §11 MT-6)

**What it answers.** Which route an unmatted layer takes once the layer stage
samples a matte coverage at `texture(1)` — V1, a 1×1 white placeholder bound
there, or V2, a `kMatte` function-constant specialization — and what a matte
costs, at 1920×1080 and 3840×2160. Nothing is merged into `app/`.
`matte_spike/README.md` has the variants, scenes, rows and statistic.

```
python3 tools/proof/matte_spike/matte_spike.py --check                       # B0–B2, K3/K4 (10 frames a scene)
python3 tools/proof/matte_spike/matte_spike.py --check --mutant resolve-writes-one|anchor-missing
perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/matte_spike/matte_spike.py --measure   # H0, C0, T0–T2, M0; recorded
python3 tools/proof/matte_spike/matte_spike.py --check --tree                # MT5: the tree's own shader, B0–B2, K3/K4
perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/matte_spike/matte_spike.py --measure --tree   # MT5's record
```

**Its record** (2026-10-08, Apple M2 Max, `powermode 0`, AC power):
`--check` exit 0 (B0–B2, K3/K4 for both routes at both sizes); `--measure`
exit 0: C0 noise floor 0.038 ms at 1080p and 0.002 ms at 4K; S1 overhead over
V0 0.014 ms (V1) and 0.019 ms (V2) at 1080p, 0.052 ms and −0.003 ms at 4K;
route V1; with V1, S3 − S2 −0.082 / 0.066 ms and S4 − S2 0.040 / 0.542 ms
(1080p / 4K), within 0.50 / 2.00 ms. Mutants: `resolve-writes-one` killed by K3
and K4, `anchor-missing` by B0. The full table is `archive/mattes.md`'s MT0
record.

The spike patches the shader as it stood before MT2 (`git show
464a3aa:app/Resources/Shaders/Compositor.metal`), the one its anchors were
written against, so `--check` and `--measure` keep answering for MT0's routes.
`--tree` (MT5, below) measures the tree's own shader instead.

## Road map mattes — MT2, the matte track end to end over MCP (`matte_proof.py` C0, A1, G0, U0, P6, MM, V5, H0, B0, A2, N0, R0, L1–L3, Z1 and eight mutants; `core/tests/matte.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v14.rs`; #240, spec §11 MT-1..MT-6)

**What it answers.** That `set_track {matte}` makes a track a matte for the
track directly behind it, through the core's recipe (`matte`, `mattes`) and
the compositor's matte pass, in `render_frame`'s bytes: alpha and inverted
alpha against two references, luma and inverted luma against a formula over
measured bytes, the movie itself as a luma matte, and every case MT-2 says
cuts nothing (no clip at `t`, a hidden matte track, a back-most matte, a
matte in front of a matte), plus undo, the model's own values for blend,
shadow and reflection (MT-4) and the unknown-mode refusal. The module
docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py                          # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --only C0,A1,L1           # run and score only these rows
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --mutant NAME             # one of the eight below
cd core && cargo test --release --test matte && cargo test --release --test schema_v14
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/matte/home`), makes a 2 s 640×360 `testsrc2` movie with
ffmpeg in its work folder, performs no menu item, closes both projects it
opens, and removes its work folder at the start and at exit. `--mutant`
builds a tree copy (`tree_copy.make_copy`, `own_core` for a `core/` anchor,
with the tree's `core/tests` linked in) with one anchor replaced, asserted to
occur once, and scores rule R: exit 0 when every named row failed, 1 when one
survived, 2 when the control could not be performed. A core mutant that
names CT also runs `cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test matte --test
matte_nest` in the copy's core (`matte_nest` since MT3) and names the files
that failed.

|---|---|---|
| `shader-no-multiply` | step 7c's multiply by the coverage made `1.0 + 0.0 ×` it (`alpha *= matteCover;` since MT3) | A1 A2 L1 |
| `source-drawn` | `render`'s skip of a layer with a non-null `into` emptied | A1 B0 MM |
| `resolve-mode-ignored` | the resolve reads every mode as `kMatteAlpha` | A2 L1 L2 L3 |
| `core-no-prune` | a group is listed whether or not a layer is drawn into it | V5 H0 |
| `core-matte-behind-matte` | `matte_target` ignores that the track behind is a matte | MM |
| `core-untargeted-into-null` | an unlisted group's `into` is written `null` | B0 MM CT |
| `core-no-override` | `layer` is told no layer is drawn into a matte | P6 |
| `handler-drops-matte` | `set_track`'s handler sends `matte: nil` | A1 G0 |

**Its record** (2026-10-08): on Debug 16/16; recorded on the third gate's
Release build (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`) 16/16, beside `phase6_proof.py` 168/168
and `phase8_chrome.py` 150/150 for the layer stage every layer now goes
through. Every mutant caught, `core-matte-behind-matte` after the instrument
and the matte pass were fixed (MM made A1's region claims itself; a cut naming
a matte not drawn before it fails the frame before any encoder opens) — the
two passes are `archive/mattes.md`'s MT2 record.

## Road map mattes — MT3, nests, dissolves, shadow, reflection, Preview Quality, every export (`matte_proof.py` N1–N7, T1–T3, S1, RF1, E1–E7, F1; `matte_probe.py` B0, Q0–Q2; `core/tests/matte_nest.rs`; #240, spec §11 MT-3, MT-5, MT-6)

**What it answers.** That a matte holds through `nest` and `unnest` (the
nest clip lands on the front-most selected track that is not a matte, a
nested track keeps its matte only above the copy of its target, `unnest`
lines the front-most non-matte track up with the nest clip's), inside and
around nest clips (a nest clip as the matted clip, as the matte, a matted
nest holding its own pair — the product — and a split nest clip in a
dissolve, each half cut by its own matte); that a dissolve under a matte is
exact (between two matte clips, between two matted clips under a hard and a
soft matte — the outgoing half's correction weighs its partner's cover by
the matte, spec §11 MT-3); that a matted clip's drop shadow is the cut shape
offset and its reflection is cut where it lands; that all seven export
presets write what `render_frame` shows, alpha included, and a graphic matte
is prefetched for an export; and, in the probe, that the matte's edge and a
matted layer's shadow sit at the same fraction of the frame at Full, Half and
Quarter. `matte_proof.py`'s and `matte_probe.py`'s docstrings list every row
and fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --only N1,N2,N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,T1,T2,T3,S1,RF1,E1,E2,E3,E4,E5,E6,E7,F1,Z1
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --mutant NAME             # MT3's seven below
python3 tools/proof/matte_probe.py                           # no app; builds through swift_build.py
python3 tools/proof/matte_probe.py --mutant coverage-destination-coords
cd core && cargo test --release --test matte_nest
```

`matte_proof.py` runs as MT2's section says (its own instance, scratch home,
no menu item, every project closed). The export rows need ffmpeg to decode
(frame 0.5 s, frame 0 when an encoder kept fewer — the fixture does not
move); a Mac with no HEVC-with-alpha encoder is a named host skip of E3,
never a failure. `matte_probe.py` launches no app: `matte_probe.swift` is
built as `main.swift` over every other `app/Sources` file through
`swift_build.build`, beside `Blank.mp4` and a `default.metallib` compiled
from the tree's shader, in `tools/proof/work/matte_probe/`, and renders
through `CompositionBuilder.build`, `Playback.previewComposition` and
`AVAssetImageGenerator` as `phase8_chrome.py`'s section 9 does. A build that
fails is its B0 FAILURE. Its mutant compiles a copy of the shader into its
own folder beside a copy of the same binary — no app build.

| `nest-always-carries` | `nest` keeps every nested track's matte | N4 |
| `nest-old-front-track` | the nest clip on the front-most selected track, matte or not | N1 |
| `unnest-old-depth` | `unnest` counts depth from the nest's front-most track | N6 CT |
| `core-group-by-track` | a group keyed by its matte track alone (no nest-clip path) | N7 CT |

| `coverage-destination-coords` (`matte_probe.py`) | step 7c samples at `position / coverage size` | Q2 |

## Road map mattes — MT4, the chrome (`matte_chrome_probe.py` B0, M1–M3, T1–T3, LN, NT, HT and ten mutants; `track_menu_probe.py`'s Matte rows; `screens.py` 10c; #240, spec §11 MT-7)

**What it answers.** That Track ▸ Matte and the track context menu's Matte
submenu come right after Solo with the five modes in order; that the
validator checks the CURRENT track's mode and the context menu the CLICKED
track's; that choosing a mode edits exactly that track as one undo step
named "Track Matte" and choosing it again is an identity (no change, no
step); that the header's tag reads "Matte · <mode>", or "Matte · nothing
behind" dimmed for a matte with no target; that on a Small text or audio
row's name line the three long tags read "Matte" alone, so the name keeps
at least 40 pt, and the header clips the name by exactly the drawn tag;
that the dimmed tag (muted words) keeps a WCAG contrast of at least 3:1
over the header in light and dark, over the host's accent and (since MT5)
over every corner of the sRGB cube in its place, and the undimmed tag (label-coloured
words on the accent tint) at least 4.5:1 in both — over the host's accent
and over every corner of the sRGB cube in its place, so no accent the owner
picks can fail it — with two host-independent controls (the header row's
own colour as text over the dimmed box is under 1.5:1, and the light and
dark rows resolved apart); that a matte
lane's clip is painted at half opacity over the lane (a `cacheDisplay`
of the timeline's content view, the window's own paint path); that the Clip tab's note is
MT-7's sentence exactly for single and shared-mode selections, the "Nothing
is behind…" sentence with no target, nil otherwise — as a function and as
the pinned block shows it on two sub-tabs; and that the canvas hits a matte
clip inside its box and the clip it cuts outside it. Its docstring lists
every row and the fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/matte_chrome_probe.py                    # no app; builds through swift_build.py
python3 tools/proof/matte_chrome_probe.py --mutant NAME      # the ten below
python3 tools/proof/track_menu_probe.py
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --only 10c-matte-track        # the matte fixture, light and dark
```

`matte_chrome_probe.swift` is built as `main.swift` over every other

`tools/proof/work/matte_chrome_probe/`; it launches no app, puts a real
`EditorViewController` in an offscreen aqua window and writes one JSON
answer. A build that fails is its B0 FAILURE. A mutant copies `app/Sources`'
Swift files into `work/matte_chrome_probe/mutant/NAME/Sources`, applies one
anchored replacement (asserted to occur once) and builds the probe over the
copy — no app build. LN reads the capture's pixels in its own encoding
(`NSCalibratedRGBColorSpace`), where the transparency layer is composited: a
0.5 mix converted to sRGB is not the mix of the two sRGB colours. The
probe's undo groups come from `groupsByEvent`, as an AppKit event's do — an
explicit begin/end pair around an identity would leave an empty step.

## Mattes follow-up B90 — nested dissolves and zooms measured (`matte_proof.py` DR, D0–D8)

**What it answers.** What a `cross_dissolve` or `zoom` with a nested half
draws TODAY, before #252's fix (issue batch B90 phase 1; no product code
changed). Each D row asserts its pre-fix prediction ("pre", from the full
formula in the module docstring of `matte_proof.py`)
and prints the exact mix beside it: nest ↔ nest (D0), N7's split nest under
two soft luma windows (D1), a dissolve inside a nest (D2), nest → plain under
a soft inner matte (D3), plain → nest (D4), overlapping layers in a nested
half (D5), a matte dissolve inside a nest (D6), a dissolve inside a
dissolving half (D7) and a zoom between nest clips (D8). DR is the control: a
timeline pair is exact (R + G = 255 ± 2) and gives p at T_A and T_B, so no
row reads p off its own frame (D2, D6 and D7's inner p come from the row's own
un-nested frame). Every transition is linear; each row is its own project,
background black, closed at the end. Phase 4 switches the rows to the exact
mix.

## Mattes follow-up B90 — the matte pool reuses and trims (`matte_pool_probe.py` B0, P1–P3 and four mutants; `matte_proof.py` `free-ignores-liveness`, `early-resolve`; #253, spec §11 MT-9)

**What it answers.** Whether a frame's mattes share composites as
`MattePlan` says, and whether `MattePool` keeps exactly what the renderer's
last 30 frames held (issue batch B90 phase 3). `matte_pool_probe.py` builds
`matte_pool_probe.swift` as `main.swift` over every other file in
`app/Sources` through `swift_build.build`, and asks the app's own
`MattePlan` and `MattePool` what they answer. It launches no app and builds
no shader. P1 is four plans: ten mattes each cutting its own set, two in one
set, two in two sets, and a set naming a group no step draws. P2 is a pool on
the real device at 64×64: take, give and take; a frame holding (3, 2) then
idle frames; and a fresh pool used (1, 1) at frame 20 alone. P3 is a size
change. The module docstring has each row's claim. The app-side ordering is
scored by `matte_proof.py`'s N5, under its two new mutants.

```
python3 tools/proof/matte_pool_probe.py                  # no app; builds through swift_build.py
python3 tools/proof/matte_pool_probe.py --mutant NAME    # no-release, give-ignored, trim-never, trim-early
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --mutant free-ignores-liveness --only N5,Z1
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --mutant early-resolve --only N5,Z1
```

A probe mutant builds the probe over a copy of one Swift file, with one
anchor replaced (asserted once), in place of the tree's. It builds into
`tools/proof/work/matte_pool_probe/mutant/<name>/`. A `matte_proof.py`
mutant builds a tree copy as MT2's section says.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `no-release` (`MattePlan.swift`) | no step gives a composite back | P1 |
| `give-ignored` (`Compositor+Matte.swift`) | `giveComposite` frees nothing | P2 |
| `trim-never` (`Compositor+Matte.swift`) | `endFrame` releases nothing | P2 |
| `trim-early` (`Compositor+Matte.swift`) | the window is `keepFrames − 1` frames | P2 |
| `free-ignores-liveness` (`matte_proof.py`) | each step gives back only its own composite | N5 |
| `early-resolve` (`matte_proof.py`) | a cut set resolves at its first matte's step | N5 |

**Its record** (2026-10-08, Apple M2 Max): `matte_pool_probe.py` 4/4. At
3840×2160, ten mattes each cutting its own set hold 116,121,600 B: one
composite live and ten coverages. MT-6's pool held 414,720,000 B for the same
frame. In P2, `held` was (3, 2) after frames 1, 29 and 30 and (0, 0) after
frame 31. The pool used at frame 20 held (0, 0) after frame 19, (1, 1) after
frames 20 and 49, and (0, 0) after frame 50. On Debug,
`matte_proof.py --only A1,MM,L3,N3,N5,N7,T1,T3,S1,RF1,D1,D3,D6,E1,F1,Z1` scored
16/16 and `matte_probe.py` 4/4. `make gate` PASS. Recorded on the gate's
Release build (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`), `matte_proof.py` whole scored 46/46
(E3 ran). Every row and printed value is identical to phase 2's recorded
run, once the instance, pid, socket and log-tail lines are set aside. All six
mutants exit 0. Under `free-ignores-liveness` and `early-resolve`, N5's frames
are missing: the released or unresolved matte fails the frame (`unordered`).

## Mattes follow-up B90 — nested dissolves and zooms mixed exactly (`matte_proof.py` D0–D8 exact and nine mutants; `matte_probe.py` Q3, Q4; `core/tests/dissolve_nest.rs`; #252, spec §11 MT-8)

**What it answers.** Whether a `cross_dissolve` or `zoom` with a nested half
now draws the exact mix (issue batch B90 phase 4). The core routes it
(`recipe_dissolve.rs`: the layer's `dissolve`, never its `transition`), and
the app draws each half alone into a pool target and mixes the pair
(`Compositor+Dissolve.swift`, `reelcut_dissolve_fragment`), a zoom's halves
scaled there about their anchors. The D rows of phase 1 now assert the exact
mix and print the pre-fix prediction beside it, from the same fixtures.
`matte_probe.py` Q3 and Q4 hold D0's and D8's fixtures, written by hand at
1920×1080, to the mix at Full, Half and Quarter through the app's own
preview path: Q3's "mix" class (R 85 ± 8, G 170 ± 8) covers at least 99.5 %
of each frame, and Q4's sits in the in-box (1/12 … 11/12 of each axis, within
1.5 destination pixels) with the out half alone around it ("border",
1 − (5/6)² of the frame within 0.4 %). `core/tests/dissolve_nest.rs` holds the
recipe: each routed case's entries, ids and contiguity, the matte-level stop,
the `transition` and `blend` rules, a routed zoom's `kind`, a moved and
cropped nest clip's anchor, and a timeline pair of plain clips left unrouted.

```
cd core && cargo test --release --test dissolve_nest
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --only DR,D0,D1,D2,D3,D4,D5,D6,D7,D8,Z1
python3 tools/proof/matte_probe.py                                # Q0–Q4, no app
python3 tools/proof/matte_proof.py --mutant NAME --only <its rows>,Z1
```

A core mutant's CT row runs `cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test
matte --test matte_nest --test dissolve_nest` in the copy's own `core/`.

|---|---|---|
| `core-dissolve-not-routed` (`recipe_dissolve.rs`) | `routed` answers false | D0–D8 CT |
| `core-zoom-not-routed` | `routed` admits `cross_dissolve` alone | D8 CT |
| `core-routed-keeps-transition` | a routed level also fills `transition` | D0 CT |
| `core-member-keeps-outer` | no matte-level stop | D1 CT |
| `core-chain-inner-first` | the chain left inner first | D7 CT |
| `mix-weights-swapped` (`Compositor.metal`) | the mix at 1 − p | D0–D8 |

| `zoom-scale-dropped` (`Compositor.metal`) | the mix fragment's z_out and z_in both 1 | D8 |

Three earlier mutants were re-pinned to their new homes and re-run:

## Issue batch B92 — the alpha movie rows written straight, a video frame read as labelled (`hevc_alpha_proof.py` A2, I1, M1, T1, T2, F1, F2, R0, Q1, B4, `--rows alpha-mode`, `--measure straighten-speed` and four mutants; `alpha_mode_probe.swift`; #242, spec §11 G-35)

The owner chose both of #242's halves on 2026-10-09 ("Compensate for other
apps, but export straight"). On import, a video frame whose buffer is labelled
`PremultipliedAlpha` is composited as premultiplied
(`MetalRenderer.declaresPremultipliedAlpha`), and any other as straight. On
export, `prores_4444` and `hevc_alpha` frames are un-premultiplied, each
transparent pixel within 4 px of a visible one takes the nearest one's colour,
and every buffer, plus `hevc_alpha`'s encoder key, says `StraightAlpha`
(`ExportStraightAlpha.swift`).

**The probe** is `tools/proof/alpha_mode_probe.swift`. It is compiled last
with every `app/Sources/*.swift` but `main.swift` through `swift_build.build`
(the tree's sources, also under a mutant), once per run, and run in a scratch
home. `write` is a third-party writer: one second of a 640 × 360 clear frame
with a 200 × 120 card of a given RGBA, labelled premultiplied, straight or
not at all. `read` reports the track's and the first decoded frame's alpha
mode and the centre pixel. `roundtrip` runs R0 over the product's
`straighten(bgra:…)`. A probe that does not build is a scored failure of M1,
T1, T2 and R0.

**Rows.** **A2** (rewritten): FAINT as `hevc_alpha` decodes alpha 128 ± 3
with red ≥ 250 and green and blue ≤ 5 (straight). **I1** (scored now): FAINT's
two files re-imported over white read (255, 128, 128) ± 6 at alpha 255.
**M1**: their first decoded frame reads `StraightAlpha`. **T1**: the probe's
premultiplied (128, 0, 0, 128) card, labelled, as each codec, re-imported over
white reads (255, 128, 128) ± 6. **T2**: its unlabelled (255, 0, 0, 128)
ProRes 4444 card reads the same. **F1**: DISC (a red 200 × 200 ellipse on a
clear canvas) as each codec, re-imported over white, against DISCWHITE (the
same on white) over every pixel: the largest channel difference is at most 6
on `prores_4444` and at most 20 on `hevc_alpha`. **R0**: all 32,895 pairs
0 ≤ c ≤ a round-trip, the 16 × 16 fill is exact, and a tie goes to the first
pixel in row-major order. **B4** (rewritten): `prores_4444`'s three files
match the baseline's sizes and five sampled alphas, and the digests are
printed, not scored. **F2** (the phase's review): DISC as each codec at
`720p`, scaled ×2 by the writer, re-imported over white at 1280 × 720: red
falls below 255 by at most 6 on `prores_4444` and 20 on `hevc_alpha` anywhere
(a red disc over white is red 255 everywhere, so a fall is a dark fringe);
DISCWHITE at `720p` as `prores_4444`, compared over every pixel, and both
files' edge down column 640 are printed. **Q1** (the review): the first
cached thumbnail of each movie I1, T1 and T2 re-imported — the JPEG the
filmstrip and the Media tab draw — reads (255, 128, 128) ± 6 at the card's
centre. `--rows alpha-mode` runs H0, A2, I1, M1, T1, T2, F1, F2, R0, Q1 and
Z1 on FAINT, DISC and DISCWHITE alone, with no baseline. The full run is 39
rows. `--measure straighten-speed` builds the probe `-O` with whole-module
optimisation and prints `straighten(bgra:…)`'s time at 1920 × 1080 and
3840 × 2160 on three frames (an opaque card, soft alpha everywhere, one
visible pixel in each 9 × 9 block); it launches nothing and scores nothing.

**Mutants**, each a `tree_copy` naming only the rows above, with only their
fixtures:
- `import-straight`: the helper answers false. T1 FAILS and I1 passes.
- `export-premultiplied`: pass 1 divides nothing. A2 and I1 FAIL.
- `label-premultiplied`: the attachment and the key say premultiplied. M1
  FAILS.
- `no-bleed`: `bleedRadius` is 0. F1 FAILS on its `hevc_alpha` half, and F2

Each also names a half that has to fail by measurement (`half`: T1's

python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --mutant no-bleed     # MUTANT PASS

## Issue batch B93 phase 1 — the proxy tests time a request, not a proxy's start (`mcp-proxy/tests/stdio.rs`; #244)

#244 saw `make test` stop in `mcp-proxy/tests/stdio.rs` with `no answer within
5s` / `8s` on a host in Low Power Mode under another app's load, a different
test each run. Each bound timed the proxy's exec as well as its request: the
fourteen tests start fourteen copied binaries at once, and one exec measured
0.65–1.30 s under `make test` in B75. Now `Proxy::start` sends
`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ready","method":"ping"}` and requires its empty result
within `START_BOUND` (60 s) before it returns, so every later bound times only
its own request. Every timeout's panic names the host:
`no answer within {within:?} (host: <pmset -g's powermode lines>; vm.loadavg
{ … })`, read only (`pmset -g`, `sysctl -n vm.loadavg`) and only when a bound
expires. No other bound changed, and no test or Makefile line says not to run
it on any power setting.

**Its record** (2026-10-09, Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, on AC, `powermode 0`
before and after every set). Throttled runs are
`perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 taskpolicy -b cargo test --release
--test stdio` in `mcp-proxy/`. The control, HEAD edbfa89's test, passed 14/14
in all three runs (6.49, 6.40, 6.72 s): this host did not reproduce #244, so
the control is no evidence for the fix. After the change, three runs passed
14/14 (6.99, 8.15, 7.56 s), with no `no answer within` line. With
`START_BOUND` set to 1 ns for one run (the file restored byte for byte
after), `ping_is_answered_with_an_empty_result` panicked with
`no answer within 1ns (host: powermode 0; vm.loadavg { 7.72 6.41 9.50 })`.
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` were clean.
`make gate` PASS (101 s), and the stdio tests in it passed 14/14 in 6.48 s.

## Issue batch B93 phase 2 — the straight-alpha fill finds its nearest through a row table (`hevc_alpha_proof.py` K1, `--rows straighten` and four probe-only mutants; `alpha_mode_probe.swift`'s `equivalence`; #254, spec §11 G-35 (d), (f))

#254 measured B92's fill at 61.4 ms per 3840 × 2160 frame when visible pixels
are scattered (one per 9 × 9 block): each transparent pixel walked the 80
offsets of its 9 × 9 square, sorted by distance, until it met a visible one.
Now pass 1 also writes, for each row that holds a visible pixel, a table of
every column's nearest visible pixel in that row (`nearestInRow`: the signed
dx with the smallest |dx| ≤ 4, a tie to the left, `noVisible` when none). It
does this in one left-to-right sweep, and a row with no transparent pixel is
a plain fill of zeros. Pass 2 (`fill`) lists the band's rows that hold a
visible pixel once per row, then for each transparent pixel reads that row's
entry top to bottom, keeping only a strictly smaller dx² + dy². That is the
pixel the sorted square named: the smallest distance, then the smallest dy,
then the smallest dx. `offsets(_:)` is gone. `bleedRadius`, pass 1's
division and both labels are unchanged.

**K1** is the probe's `equivalence` mode. It runs the product's
`straighten(bgra:…)` against `referenceStraighten`, which is commit 7308ace's
fill copied verbatim into the probe as the oracle, and compares the two byte
for byte over whole planes, padding included. The planes are 65 frames and
3,160 pairs:
- seeded frames of 1 × 1, 3 × 17, 17 × 3, 64 × 64 and 257 × 129, each with
  16 bytes of padding a row and every byte random, at visible densities of
  0.2 %, 1 %, 5 % and 30 % (three seeds each);
- 64 × 64 frames whose every fourth row is wholly visible (the table's fast
  path; three seeds);
- `timing`'s 9 × 9 lattice, and an 8 × 8 lattice of distinct colours, both at
  1920 × 1080;
- every pair of distinct visible pixels in a 9 × 9 plane around a transparent
  centre.

K1 is scored when no case and no pair differs, there was at least one case,
and at least one pair was a tie. `--rows straighten` runs R0 and K1 with no
launch and needs no app. `--rows alpha-mode`, and the full rows, gain K1.
`--measure straighten-speed` now times the oracle beside the product, on the
same frames in the same run, the two alternating, and prints the host's
`vm.loadavg`.

**Mutants**, probe-only: each copies `app/Sources` into `work/`, replaces one
anchor of `ExportStraightAlpha.swift` asserted once, builds the plain probe
from the copy and scores R0 and K1. Exit 0 when either FAILS.
- `row-tie-right`: a visible pixel takes over a transparent one on its left
  at an equal distance, so a tie in a row goes to +dx.
- `rows-tie-last`: `<` becomes `<=` across the band's rows, so a tie goes to
  the last row.
- `reach-past-radius`: the row table admits |dx| = 5.
- `full-row-unseen`: a wholly visible row's entries say `noVisible`.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --rows straighten            # 2/2, exit 0
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --mutant rows-tie-last       # MUTANT PASS
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --measure straighten-speed
```

**Its record** (2026-10-09, Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, ffmpeg 9.0.2, on AC,
`powermode 0` before and after each measurement). On Debug, `--rows
straighten` scored 2/2, exit 0: R0 had 0 mismatches and the tie went to (4,8);
K1 had 65 cases and 0 mismatched, and 3,160 pairs with 216 ties and 0
mismatched. All four mutants printed MUTANT PASS, exit 0:

| Mutant | R0 | K1 cases mismatched | K1 pairs mismatched |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row-tie-right` | FAILED, (8,8) took (12,8)'s colour | 25 | 140 |
| `rows-tie-last` | passed | 34 | 1,340 |
| `reach-past-radius` | passed | 19 | 396 |
| `full-row-unseen` | passed | 4 | 0 |

R0 passes under `reach-past-radius` because its lone pixel's band never
reaches a column five away. K1 is what catches that mutant.

The speed, from `--measure straighten-speed`, is the probe built `-O` with
whole-module optimisation, 12 cores, best of five. Other sessions loaded the
host: `vm.loadavg` read 25.39 before the run and 10.99 after it. The "before
B93" column is the oracle in the same run, so both columns ran under the same
load:

| Frame | 1920 × 1080 | before B93 | 3840 × 2160 | before B93 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opaque card | 0.53 ms | 0.56 ms | 0.87 ms | 0.71 ms |
| Soft alpha at every pixel | 0.81 ms | 0.86 ms | 2.98 ms | 2.87 ms |
| One visible pixel per 9 × 9 block | 0.88 ms | 14.78 ms | 3.33 ms | 59.16 ms |

B92 recorded 15.1 and 61.4 ms for the last row. Two earlier versions of the
table were measured the same way and replaced:
- Two sweeps per row, with the band's rows filtered per pixel: sparse 4K
  7.46 ms, but soft 4K 5.22 ms against the oracle's 2.86 ms.
- An outward search from each transparent pixel.

The final version replaces the sweep over a wholly visible row with a fill
of zeros. One
intermediate version wrote to column −1 when a row's first pixel was visible.
K1 caught it as the probe's crash (rc −11) before any other check ran.

`make typecheck` held its four baseline warnings. `make gate` PASS (206 s).
On the gate's Release build (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`), `--rows alpha-mode`
scored 12/12, exit 0, with stderr empty and no `Reelcut: ` line. F1 read 1
on `prores_4444` and 18 on `hevc_alpha` (2 pixels over 10), and F2 read 0 and
2, B92's figures.

## Issue batch B93 phase 3 — a timed page's backdrop goes under its words, a dim is one multiply, a backdrop's interior is written by vImage (`words_picture_probe.py` P10's backdrop pair scored, P19's `highlight-word0`, P20 and four mutants; `word_looks_proof.py`'s `dim-per-draw` re-anchored; #247, spec §11 W-17)

#247: a page with a backdrop AND a pause dim kept W-14's transparency layer,
and Karaoke's two-line page under `BackdropProps()` read 11.289 ms and
11.227 ms at 3840 × 2160 with the dim (6.359 ms and 6.341 ms without), over
P10's 8 ms budget; the backdrop's own whole-path fill was about 3 ms of that
3061 × 420 box. W-17 was recorded first. Now:
- `textBitmap` draws a TIMED page's (`reveal.word` and `word_style` set) words
  and pill first, and its backdrop UNDER them (`destinationOver`); every other
  page draws its backdrop first, as before.
- `drawWords`' dim is one `scaleBitmap` of the drawn page (every byte × the
  factor through `vImageMatrixMultiply_ARGB8888` in place, in 1/4096ths,
  rounded), in the existing `defer`, so the early return after `drawBase` is
  dimmed too. The transparency layer stays only for a context with no
  `data`, decided before drawing.
- `drawBackdrop` (`LayerRenderersBackdrop.swift`, new) flattens the rounded
  rect's fully covered cross — rows [⌈r⌉, ⌊H − r⌋) by every whole column, and
  every whole row by columns [⌈r⌉, ⌊W − r⌋) — with `vImageFlatten_RGBA8888`
  against `fullCoverageBytes(color)`, the bytes CoreGraphics writes for one

  the bitmap less the cross (an even-odd clip of the bitmap, both halves and
  their overlap).
