## The precision road map — PR0 to PR3 (`precision_proof.py`, `precision_encoder_probe.swift`, `preview_display_probe.py`; the preview probes' format reads and PF; `hevc_alpha_proof.py` R8, RH, KH, HA and four mutants; PR2's D2, R1, R2, C1 and two mutants; PR3's T1, T2, MA, the selftest and four mutants; spec §11 PR-1..PR-5)

The road map is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/precision.md`,
the phase records `archive/precision.md`, and its decisions
`designs/spec/11-decisions/precision.md`. PR1 makes the compositor 16-bit
float (`64RGBAHalf` buffers, `rgba16Float` targets) while sources stay
32BGRA, and decides per export row what its encoder is handed
(`ExportWriter.frameForm`, `ExportFrames`). PR2 decodes every video source
to `64RGBAHalf` (`Compositor.sourcePixelFormat`, spec §11 PR-2).

```
python3 tools/proof/preview_display_probe.py --rows spike          # V0–V2 (PR0's spike; exit 1 is its RECORDED outcome)
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py [--only C0,D1,D2,P1,H1,R1,R2,C1,T1,T2,S1,S2,S4,S5,S6,S7,V0,…,V6] [--control DIR]
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py reverse-cost                # precision-2 P2-2: the reverse's cost, no app
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py capture DIR                 # on the CONTROL tree, before any product edit
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py capture DIR --only S3c      # S3's scenes DIR lacks into an existing capture
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py compare DIR [--only K1,…,E2,S3]
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --measure capture|compare DIR   # M1, release-only
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --measure ab --mutant decode-8bit [--rounds N]   # MA, release-only
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --selftest                  # S1–S3, no app
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant h264-deep|hevc-deep compare DIR
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant output-8bit|hevc-no-profile|decode-8bit|no-source-clamp
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant hevc10-main|hevc10-unmapped|hevc10-eightbit|row-before-hevc-alpha
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant still-eightbit|still-deep-linear   # precision-2 P2-1: S1, S2 (+ S6, S7 for still-eightbit; S4 beside)
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant still-always-deep compare DIR      # precision-2 P2-1: S3
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant reverse-bgra|reverse-main|reverse-planar-drop   # precision-2 P2-2: V0 (V1, V2 beside reverse-bgra)
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant reverse-709-labels|reverse-no-attachments      # precision-2 P2-2: V2, V3 (V3 beside the second)
python3 tools/proof/precision_proof.py --mutant reverse-unversioned|reverse-odd-hevc           # precision-2 P2-2: V4; V5
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --rows straighten          # R0, K1, R8, RH, KH
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --measure hevc-alpha-deep   # HA, recorded
python3 tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py --mutant hevc-no-profile|bgra8-truncates|half-no-unpremultiply|half-no-fill
python3 tools/proof/preview_refresh_probe.py [--sources DIR]       # PF is section 7
```

**`preview_display_probe.py` exits 1 by design.** Its one mode is PR0's spike
(V0–V2): `CARenderer` draws an `AVPlayerLayer` in no window, and V1 — a
half-float frame tagged Linear, the control that must move — drew within 0.03
of the untagged one, so the instrument cannot be shown to see how the layer
READS a buffer. V1's failure is the recorded result, not a broken
instrument: leave the probe out of any sweep. PV was never built, and the
displayed picture's check is `docs/manual-checks.md`'s PRC-1.

**`precision_proof.py`** has `matte_proof.py`'s shape: its own instance
(`proof_app`; Debug unless `RC_PROOF_APP=release`), a scratch
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, everything under `work/precision/run/`, removed at the
start and at exit; DIR, a capture, is kept (PR0's is
`work/precision/ctl-pr0/`). The rows: **C0** two renders of K3 byte-equal;
**D1** an all-8-bit project renders an 8-bit PNG (PR-4); **P1** a 50 %
black→white gradient over black through `prores_422`, 1920 × 1080: the
middle row's luma against 0.5·g/255 at most 1.0 10-bit steps RMS (`--control
DIR` prints the 8-bit canvas's figure beside it); **H1** `hevc` is Main,
`yuv420p`. `compare DIR`: **K1–K6** (the spike's scenes) against PR0's
renders, K1 and K6 byte-identical and K2–K5 within ±2, each histogram
printed; **E1** — under the orchestrator's ruling after PR0, because E0's two
H.264 exports of one project differed by up to 124 levels (VideoToolbox's
H.264 encode does not repeat) — compares the h264 ENCODER'S INPUT, not a
file: K6's and K3's scenes are saved and read by
`precision_encoder_probe.swift`, built through `swift_build.build` over the
tree's `app/Sources` (a mutant copy's under `--mutant`), which resolves the
core's `h264` settings, builds the composition as an export does, reads one
frame through an `AVAssetReaderVideoCompositionOutput` in
`Compositor.outputPixelFormat`, and applies `ExportWriter.frameForm` and
`ExportFrames.convert` (or hands the reader's frame on when the form is
nil). The handed buffer must be 32BGRA, K6 byte-identical to DIR's render
and K3 within ±1 (the compositor's own ±1 on a blended scene). The probe
registers the app's bundled fonts, as `ATSApplicationFontsPath` does for the
bundle: without them K3's title drew in a fallback face, up to 194 levels
off. This tree's encoded h264 file is printed beside E0's digests, unscored.
**E2** (PR1's fix pass) is the same for the `hevc` (Main) encoder: fed the
half-float frame, `hevc` encoded the 10-bit ramp at 9.04 steps RMS against
PR0's 6.46 from 32BGRA (three exports each, every one the same figure), so
`frameForm` rounds `hevc`'s frame to 8 bits as it does `h264`'s.
**M1** (`--measure`, release-only, recorded): `prores_422` exports of a
typical and a heavy fixture at 1080p and 2160p, each on an instance of its
own launched with `-ReelcutCompositorTiming YES`: the timing log's average
and worst and the instance's lifetime `phys_footprint_peak`, beside the
control's, with the implied extra buffers and the frame-time stop (1080p
heavy average ≥ 8 ms). The memory is printed and recorded, not scored: the
owner accepted PR1's measured rise (heavy 4K +851.7 MB) and retired the
road map's +532 MB stop (spec §11 PR-1).

**PR2's rows and the compare's rules.** `capture` records the tree's
formats (`formats`: the `outputPixelFormat` and `sourcePixelFormat`
`Compositor.swift` names, read from `app/Sources`; a capture without them is
PR0's, both 32BGRA), and `compare` picks each K row's rule from the
control's formats against this tree's: K1 byte-identical always; K2–K5 (no
video) byte-identical when the output format is the control's (PR2 against
PR1's capture, `work/precision/ctl-pr1/`) and within ±2 across it (PR1
against PR0's); K6 (video) byte-identical when the source format is the
control's, and across it its histogram recorded and not scored (PR-2's ±1
on video), with an unscored line comparing both renders to ffmpeg's own
decode of the clip's frame 15 (BT.709, `accurate_rnd+full_chroma_int`).
Across a decode change E1's and E2's K6 bound is the largest |Δ| of this
tree's own K6 render against DIR's (the re-baseline rule's "within K6's
histogram"), and the handed frame must also be byte-identical to that render
(measured so: the 8-bit rounding is the render's own). The rows:
**D2** (a STOP, PR-4) D1's all-8-bit project still renders an 8-bit PNG with
every source decoded deep; **R1** `render_frame` of the 10-bit ramp on a
1920 × 1080 canvas is a 16-bit PNG whose middle row's green holds ≥ 850
distinct values (`--control DIR` holds the control's to ≤ 256); **R2** the
ramp through `prores_422`, the middle row's luma against x/1919 at most 1.0
10-bit steps RMS; **C1** the H.264 clip at `video.color.brightness` −0.4,
every colour channel within ±2 of max(0, its brightness-0 render − 102): a
deep-decoded frame arrives unclamped, and only `layerSample`'s `saturate`
keeps a value above 1.0 from reading above 0.6 at −0.4. The ramp is the
scoping spike's (every 10-bit code 64…940 across 1,920 px, ProRes 422 HQ,
1 s), made once by `precision_proof.py` into
`work/precision/media/ramp10_prores422hq.mov`; PRC-1 plays it, and this is
its recipe by hand:

```sh
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=black:size=1920x1080:rate=30:duration=1,format=yuv422p10le,geq=lum='64+X*876/1919':cb=512:cr=512" \
  -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -pix_fmt yuv422p10le -colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 ramp10.mov
```

**PR3's rows: the `hevc_10bit` row.** **T1** the 10-bit ramp exported
`hevc_10bit`: ffprobe's `hevc`, `Main 10`, `yuv420p10le`, and an MP4 (major
brand `mp42`; QuickTime's is `qt  `). **T2** the same ramp's middle-row luma
against x/1919, through `hevc_10bit` at most 2.0 10-bit steps RMS and at
most half of an `hevc` export of the same project in the same run, AND its
encoder was handed deep frames: the 8-bit staircase's tone
(`staircase_tone`: each column's mean 10-bit Y code over the frame's rows,
less a 31-column moving average, as an amplitude at 255 steps across the
width) at most 0.1 codes, where the `hevc` file's (8-bit, the control that
the instrument sees a staircase at all) is at least 0.3. The tone is the
claim that discriminates: Main 10 handed 8-bit frames (`hevc10-eightbit`)
measured 1.794 steps RMS against the tree's 1.459, inside both RMS halves,
but a tone of 0.536 against 0.014 (floor 0.010; `hevc` 0.758). **H1**
runs again. **MA** (`--measure ab --mutant decode-8bit`, release-only,
recorded; PR2's review asked for it): the heavy 2160p fixture alone,
exported on this tree's Release app and on a Release build of the
`decode-8bit` copy, alternated (ABBA…) `--rounds` times, so the deep
decode's frame-time share is read on one host load; each export's average,
the medians and their ratio are printed, and the row scores only that every
export measured. **The app driven decides the formats read** (PR2's review):
`app_tree` takes the sources from the tree whose `build/Build/Products` the
app sits in — this tree, or a mutant's copy — and an app outside any tree is
refused with exit 2 before any launch; `--selftest` (no app) holds S1 a
scratch tree's formats read through an app under its build folder, S2 an
app outside any tree (and one under a build folder with no `app/Sources`)
refused by `main`, S3 the default app this tree's. The mutants:
`hevc10-main` (Main 10 → Main: T1), `hevc10-unmapped` (`codecType(for:)`
drops `"hevc_10bit"`, so the export is refused: T1), `hevc10-eightbit`
(`frameForm`'s `isMain10` arm removed, so `.hevc` rounds the row to 8 bits:
T2), and the core `row-before-hevc-alpha` (the row moved before
`hevc_alpha` in `export_table.rs`; no app is built — row CT runs `cargo
test --release --no-fail-fast --test export --test export_hevc_10bit` in the
copy's own `core/`, made its own by `hevc_alpha_proof.own_core`, and must
fail naming `hevc_alpha_sits_directly_after_hevc` and
`it_sits_directly_after_hevc_alpha`).

**The preview probes read a buffer by its format.**
`preview_refresh_probe.py`, `preview_validity_probe.py` and
`media_less_playback_probe.swift` each take the grid mean from 32BGRA bytes
or from 64RGBAHalf halves × 255 (rounded), and leave no mean — failing every
row that reads one — for any other format. **PF**
(`preview_refresh_probe.py` section 7): at Full the displayed buffer is
`RGhA` and its 40 × 40 grid mean is within ±1 of `Exporter.renderFrame`'s at
the same tick. `--sources DIR` builds the probe from a copy's
`app/Sources` and shader in `work/preview-refresh/probe-sources/`, for
`precision_proof.py --mutant output-8bit`.

**`hevc_alpha_proof.py`'s precision rows** (the probe's `precision`):
**R8** `ExportStraightAlpha.eightBit(half:…)` rounds half(k/255) to k,
half((k+0.4)/255) to k and half((k+0.6)/255) to k+1, and writes RGBA as
BGRA; **RH** `straighten(half:…)` leaves |s·a − c| ≤ 2⁻¹⁰ and s ≤ 1 over a
grid of premultiplied pairs; **KH** over K1's seeded frames (the same draws)
and both lattices, every visible pixel opaque and coloured with a distinct
id, the half fill gives each transparent pixel the same source pixel as the
8-bit fill. **HA** (`--measure hevc-alpha-deep`, recorded, not used):
`hevc_alpha` fed 64RGBAHalf buffers directly. `label-premultiplied`'s first
anchor is now `ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`'s attachment line
(`STRAIGHT_HALF`); `hevc-no-profile` removes the `hevc` Main pin and hands
`hevc` the deep frame (from 32BGRA VideoToolbox writes Main with or without
the pin, so the pin alone is an equivalent mutant) and must fail B1.

**Re-baselined in PR1 (spec §11 PR-5).** `e1_proof.py`'s rows against the
frozen 1c3e92e build (the version-6 `wipe` and five cross-dissolve ticks)
compare decoded pixels within ±1 a channel (`within_one`); PR1's wipe moved
by 1 on 1,080 channels of its soft edge. `hevc_alpha_proof.py`'s B1 is
exact again: its re-baseline (PR1's centre red read 254 against 255, from
`hevc` fed 64RGBAHalf) was withdrawn when `hevc` went back to 8-bit frames,
which reproduce the baseline's digest. `word_looks_baseline.json`
is re-recorded by `word_looks_proof.py --record-baseline` once PR1 is
committed (it refuses an uncommitted tree): measured against PR0's Release,
40 of fixture B's 41 frames moved, every channel by at most 1.

**Mutants** (PR1, run once at the end on the final instrument):
`precision_proof.py`'s `h264-deep` (E1), `hevc-deep` (E2), `output-8bit`
(P1, and PF through `preview_refresh_probe.py --sources`) and
`hevc-no-profile` (H1), and PR2's `decode-8bit` (`sourcePixelFormat`
32BGRA: R1 and R2) and `no-source-clamp` (`layerSample`'s `saturate`
removed: C1);
`hevc_alpha_proof.py`'s probe-only `bgra8-truncates` (R8),
`half-no-unpremultiply` (RH) and `half-no-fill` (KH), its
`hevc-no-profile` (B1) and `label-premultiplied` on its new anchor, and the
four B93 probe mutants, since the fill they anchor in went generic.

**precision-2 P2-1 — deep stills (spec §11 PR-6; its record
`archive/precision-2.md`'s P2-1 section).** A still deeper than 8 bits a
component is drawn at 16-bit float (`LayerRenderers.renderImage`'s
`deepBitmap`, uploaded `rgba16Float`). The fixtures, made once into `work/precision/media/`:
`ramp16.png` (`rgb48be`) and `ramp16.tif` (`rgb48le`), 1920×1080, every
column X at X/1919 of full scale —
`ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=black:size=1920x1080:d=1,format=gbrp16le,geq=r='X*65535/(W-1)':g='X*65535/(W-1)':b='X*65535/(W-1)'" -frames:v 1 -pix_fmt rgb48be ramp16.png`
(PRC-4 imports it); `ramp8.png`, the same ramp written 8-bit and ROUNDED
(`format=gbrp,geq=…round(X*255/(W-1))…`, `rgb24`), so its steps fall where
Core Graphics' 8-bit draw puts them — ffmpeg's own `rgb48`→`rgb24`
truncates, which puts them near 256/(W−1) cycles a pixel, and
`staircase_tone` reads 255/(W−1) (P2-1's first control read 0.0301); and
two 640×360 8-bit `testsrc2` stills, `still8.png` and `still8a.png` (alpha
X·255/639); and `ramp10.heic`, `ramp16.png` drawn at 16-bit float and
written by ImageIO's HEIC writer (`heic10_writer.swift`, built through
`swift_build.build`; ffmpeg cannot mux HEIF, and both `sips` and the writer
fed the PNG's own 16-bit integer image write a Main 10 file holding about
256 levels), kept only when ffprobe reads HEVC Main 10 `yuv420p10le` with
≥ 800 distinct 10-bit Y codes on its middle row, and made only when S7
runs (not in the preflight): a writer that does not build or a file refused
is S7's FAIL, naming the reason. **S1** `ramp16.png` alone on a 1920×1080 canvas exported
`prores_422`: ≥ 800 distinct 10-bit Y codes on the middle row, luma RMS
against x/1919 under the in-run `ramp8.png` control's, staircase tone ≤ 0.1
where the control's is ≥ 0.3, and with `--control DIR` the control tree's
own distinct < 800; **S2** the same with `ramp16.tif`; **S4** both stills'
`render_frame` PNGs are 8-bit — a project whose only picture is a still,
deep or not, renders an 8-bit frame (spec §11 PR-4 as amended by PR-6,
accepted by the owner 2026-10-11); **S5** `ramp16.png` covering the H.264
clip renders an 8-bit frame, and **S6** covering the 10-bit ramp clip a
16-bit frame whose middle row's green (the still's) holds ≥ 850 distinct
values (PR-4 as amended: only a video source makes the frame deep, and a
deep frame keeps a deep still's depth); **S7** is S1 with `ramp10.heic`;
**Sc** (`capture`) records the three figures under `capture.json`'s
`stills` and renders S3's scenes into DIR; **S3** (`compare`) re-renders
`still8.png`, `still8a.png`, and `still8a.png` under brightness 0.1 and
contrast 0.5, from DIR's copies, each an 8-bit PNG byte-identical to DIR's.
The control is `work/precision/ctl-p21/`, captured on P2-0's product; its
`S3-color.png` was added by `capture DIR --only S3c` on P2-1's Release build
(the 8-bit draw's code unchanged; that run's opaque and alpha digests equal
the control's). S3c renders only the scenes DIR lacks: a scene `capture.json`
records whose PNG is in DIR at that digest is kept, PNG and fixture copy
untouched, so a later tree never replaces an older tree's reference. Mutants, once at the end on the final instrument:
`still-eightbit` (`let deep = false`: S1, S2, S6, S7), `still-deep-linear`
(the deep bitmap in `linearSRGB`: S1, S2), each running S4 beside in its
`also` (run and printed, not required to fail), and `still-always-deep`
(`let deep = true`, compare: S3, on the colour scene — the opaque and
alpha-ramp scenes alone left it equivalent, since only a non-identity step
after the un-premultiply carries the 8-bit draw's premultiplied rounding).

**precision-2 P2-2 — the 10-bit reverse (spec §11 PR-7; its record
`archive/precision-2.md`'s P2-2 section).** `ReverseRenderer` reads `x420`
(an odd size: `x422`) frames, copies every plane with the decoder's
attachments, and writes HEVC Main 10 (an odd size: ProRes 422) with no
colour properties; the reverse cache's digest carries
`ReverseCache.rendererVersion`. V0, V2 and
V5 run the REAL renderer through `reverse_probe.swift`
(`reverse_probe SOURCE DEST OUT_JSON`), compiled with every `app/Sources`
file but `main.swift` — a mutant copy's under `--mutant` — through
`swift_build.build`; a probe that does not build is those rows' FAIL. Its
stamp half is `source_mirror_probe.py` §3's. The fixtures, each made only
when a row needing it runs and refused (that row's FAIL, naming it) unless
ffprobe reads what it should: `ramp10_odd.mov` (the RAMP at 1919×1079,
`geq=lum='64+X*876/(W-1)'`, ProRes 422 HQ); `ramp10_hlg.mov` (the ramp,
`format=yuv420p10le,setparams=color_primaries=bt2020:color_trc=arib-std-b67:colorspace=bt2020nc`,
`-c:v hevc_videotoolbox -profile:v main10 -pix_fmt p010le -tag:v hvc1 -b:v 20M`
with the three `-color_*` flags); `chroma10_hlg.mov` (the same, with
`cb='112+X*800/1919':cr='912-X*800/1919'`: on the grey ramp a wrong matrix
or primaries label moves no code); `prores422_odd.mov` (`testsrc2`
1919×1079 2 s through `format=yuv444p10le` — left to negotiate 4:2:0,
ffmpeg wrote 1918×1078 — ProRes 422; `reverse-cost` only). **V0** the ramp
reversed: hevc Main 10 `yuv420p10le` 1920×1080, ≥ 800 distinct 10-bit Y
codes on the first frame's middle row at < 1.0 code RMS against
64 + x·876/1919, and the stamps (the frame count, the first at 0,
ascending, drift ≤ 1); **V1** (MCP) the ramp clip `set_reversed` and waited
for (the `cache/reversed/<media>-*.mov` with no `.partial` and no sheet,
≤ 300 s; on expiry `cancel_sheet` and a FAIL), exported `prores_422`: RMS ≤
the forward clip's + 0.5 and ≥ 800 codes; **V2** the HLG ramp reversed keeps
`arib-std-b67/bt2020/bt2020nc`, its middle row's Y, Cb, Cr within mean
|Δ| ≤ 2.0 codes of the source's; **V3** (MCP) the chroma ramp forward and
reversed rendered within mean |Δ| ≤ 0.25 8-bit levels (the old renderer
read 0.764: its picture was right and rounded to 8 bits, only its labels
were wrong, so the label mutants are what V3's chroma catches); **V4** (MCP)
a reverse planted under the pre-version name is not used and is pruned;
**V5** the 1919×1079 ramp reversed is ProRes 422 `yuv422p10le` at exactly
1919×1079; **V6** (MCP) the 8-bit H.264 clip alone, reversed, renders a
16-bit PNG and its reverse is hevc Main 10 (PR-4 as amended by PR-7, the
owner's "Accept 16-bit"; the old renderer FAILS it, 8-bit). On the old
renderer (a Debug copy with `ReverseRenderer.swift` from `HEAD`) every V row
FAILED. **`reverse-cost`** builds the probe `-O` and reverses
`prores422_1080`, `prores422_2160`, `prores422_odd` and the ramp three times
each, one process each, printing the median wall time, bytes, Mbps, peak
RSS, codec and size, and `pmset -g` and `vm.loadavg` before and after; exit
0 iff every reverse completed. Mutants, once at the end on the final
instrument: `reverse-bgra` (V0; V1, V2 beside), `reverse-main` (V0),
`reverse-709-labels` (V2, V3), `reverse-planar-drop` (V0),
`reverse-no-attachments` (V2; V3 beside), `reverse-unversioned` (V4) and
`reverse-odd-hevc` (V5).

## Road map grading — GR0, the grading spike (`grading_spike/`; #258)

The road map is closed: its condensed record is `designs/adr/grading.md`,
the phase records `archive/grading.md`, and its decisions
`designs/spec/11-decisions/grading.md`.

**What it answers.** What tone and a 3D LUT cost an ungraded and a graded
layer in the tree's own `Compositor.metal` under three routes — a uniform flag
(VF), function constants (VC), always on at neutral values (VA) — at 1920×1080
and 3840×2160, the route chosen by a rule written beforehand in
`archive/grading.md`; and for #258, whether a 10-bit biplanar source (`x420`,
`x422`) wins back what a `64RGBAHalf` source costs the layer stage. Nothing is
merged into `app/`. `grading_spike/README.md` has the variants, scenes, rows,
statistic and mutants.

```
python3 tools/proof/grading_spike/grading_spike.py --check                       # B0–B2, K1–K5 (10 frames, 1 run)
python3 tools/proof/grading_spike/grading_spike.py --check --mutant NAME         # anchor-missing | exposure-encoded | lut-axes-swapped | adjust-ignores-destination | biplanar-full-range | neutral-drift
perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/grading_spike/grading_spike.py --measure   # adds H0, C0, C1, F, T0–T2, P1, X0, X1, D1; recorded
```

**Its record** (2026-10-09, Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.5.1, `powermode 0`, AC
power, load `{ 7.68 8.94 9.76 }` before and `{ 6.88 8.61 9.61 }` after, seed
20261009): `--check` exit 0 (B0–B2 and 44 K rows); `--measure` exit 0. C0 noise
0.001 ms at 1080p and 0.000 ms at 4K; one ungraded full-bleed layer, V0 0.125
/ 0.481 ms (1080p / 4K); S1 overhead over V0 for the TL variants: VF-TL 0.000 /
0.001, VC-TL −0.003 / −0.000, VA-TL 0.022 / 0.083 ms. **T1: route VF** (VA-TL
misses bound + noise at both sizes). A graded layer over its own S1, tone and
a 33³ look at 0.8: VF 0.057 / 0.226, VC 0.037 / 0.149, VA 0.001 / 0.003 ms; one
adjustment pass 0.045–0.047 / 0.169–0.174 ms; the linear-light step 0.011 /
0.040 ms. P1: two stacked adjustment passes keep 256 of 256 levels through
`rgba16Float` (CONTROL through `bgra8Unorm`: 189). #258 (SH, four video
layers, 4K): B8 0.765, H16 0.900, X420 0.769, X422 0.792 ms, C1 noise 0.002;
G 0.135, W 0.131 ms, so **X1: #258 stays open for the owner's choice**. D1
(fps into 32BGRA / 64RGBAHalf / x420 / x422): ProRes 422 10-bit 198.6 / 313.3
/ 196.4 / 450.8, HEVC Main 10 198.5 / 277.3 / 341.0 / 315.9. Mutants: all six
killed (`anchor-missing` by B0, `exposure-encoded` by K2 and K4,
`lut-axes-swapped` by K3, `adjust-ignores-destination` by K4,
`biplanar-full-range` by K5, `neutral-drift` by K1). The full tables are
`archive/grading.md`'s GR0 record.

## Road map grading — GR2, tone end to end over MCP (`tone_proof.py` N0–N2, E1, E2, W1, K1, F1, O1, A1, R1, X1, U1, M1, B1, P1–P4, Z1 and seven mutants; `tone_probe.swift`; `core/tests/tone.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v15.rs`; spec §11 GR-2, GR-9; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** That `set_video {patch: {color: {…}}}`'s nine tone keys
reach the compositor's step 4c and do what spec §11 GR-2 says, in
`render_frame`'s bytes: exposure ±1 as a doubling and a halving of LINEAR
light on a grey-128 card, temperature and tint as linear-light gains, whites
and blacks held at their ends and fade lifting black to 26 and white to 242 on
a 0–255 ramp, tone after the obscure regions' own re-sample, an action
interpolating from neutral, the range refusals, undo and redo, a luma matte
clip toned into a wider window, and `render_frame` against a `prores_422`
export's frame. N0 holds six neutral frames byte-identical (16 bits a channel)
to a control captured on the UNTOUCHED tree's Release build before any product
edit; N2 reads the saved `project.json`; P1–P4 are `tone_probe.swift`, built
by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` (a failed build is a scored FAILURE):
a Light row's write over two clips carries only its own key, the flag is set by
a negative value, the block is 464 bytes with `exposure` at 416, and the Color
sub-tab's `◆N`. The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/tone_proof.py                                   # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release; N0 not run
python3 tools/proof/tone_proof.py --only E1,A1                      # run and score only these rows
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/tone_proof.py capture DIR  # the neutral control, on the untouched tree
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/tone_proof.py compare DIR  # every row, and N0 (scored on Release only)
python3 tools/proof/tone_proof.py --mutant NAME                     # one of the seven below
cd core && cargo test --release --test tone --test schema_v15
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/tone/home`), writes its fixtures (a 640×360 grey-128 PNG,
a 1920×360 ramp PNG, a 2 s `testsrc2` H.264 movie) into its work folder,
performs no menu item, closes every project it opens, and removes its work
folder at the start and at exit (the control folder is not under it).
`--mutant` builds a tree copy (`tree_copy.make_copy`, `own_core` for a
`core/` edit with the tree's `core/tests` linked in), applies its edits (each
anchor asserted to occur once), builds the probe over the copy's
`app/Sources`, and reports MUTANT PASS only when every named row failed and no
other scored row did; a core mutant also runs `cargo test --release
--no-fail-fast --test tone --test schema_v15` in the copy's core (row CT).

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `exposure-encoded` | exposure multiplies the ENCODED value (white balance stays linear) | E1 E2 |
| `tone-before-obscure` | step 4c moved before 4b | O1 |
| `flag-ignores-negative` | `apply(tone:)` raises `toneEnabled` only for a positive key | E2 P2 |
| `range-check-dropped` | `check_video`'s exposure range check removed | R1 CT |
| `tone-always-written` | `is_zero` answers false, so every tone key is serialised | N2 CT |
| `lerp-base-unfilled` | `evaluate_clip`'s base state through `to_json`, not `video_json` | A1 CT |
| `light-writes-group` | a Light row writes the whole colour group | P1 |

GR2 also pinned the GR0 spike's shader to `4d742cc` (`grading_spike.py`'s
`SHADER_COMMIT`) and made both spikes' benches hand their shader the first 104
floats of `LayerUniforms`, since the tree's block grew a tone group.

**Its record**: `archive/grading.md`'s GR2 section.

## Road map grading — GR3, seeing the grade (`seeing_proof.py` U1–U4, W1, V1–V4, P1–P7, G1, H1, H2, Z1 and seven mutants; `waveform_probe.swift`; `core/tests/ungraded.rs`; spec §11 GR-4, GR-5; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** That the recipe's `ungraded` option draws the picture
as if no clip were graded and nothing else, and reaches only what asks for it;
and that the luma waveform counts what the person sees. U1 holds
`render_frame {ungraded}` of a graded stack (two tracks, a nested clip, a
luma-matte clip) to the bytes of the same stack before any grade; U2 and U3
turn View ▸ Show Ungraded on in the window and find `render_frame` and a
`prores_422` export still graded; U4 is the refusal of a non-boolean. W1 holds
`render_frame {waveform}`'s counts on a 1920-column ramp to the rendered
values bin by bin; V1 and V2 hold the shown panel's readouts (read through
`snapshot_ui`) to `render_frame {waveform}`'s, graded and then ungraded; V3 the
panel's 248 pt and the canvas beside it; V4 the "Ungraded" tag. P1–P7 are
`waveform_probe.swift`, built by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` with
the tree's own `Waveform.metal` compiled from source (a failed build is a
scored FAILURE): the ramp, grey, the Rec. 709 weights, the rounding at both
ends and the saturation, the marks at 0.5 %, the two commands moving no
`UserDefaults` key and setting `ungraded` on the document's key only, and the
tap's latest-wins slot. G1 records the pass's GPU time. H1 and H2 are the
harness's fifteenth argument, `seeing=scopes,ungraded,ramp` (`waveform` before
grading-2's G2-1 renamed View ▸ Waveform to View ▸ Scopes), light and dark.
The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/seeing_proof.py                  # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
python3 tools/proof/seeing_proof.py --only U1,V1     # run and score only these rows
python3 tools/proof/seeing_proof.py --mutant NAME    # one of the seven below
cd core && cargo test --release --test ungraded
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/seeing/home`), writes its fixtures (a 640×360 grey-128 PNG,
a 1920×360 ramp PNG, a 2 s `testsrc2` H.264 movie) into its work folder,
performs only View ▸ Show Ungraded and View ▸ Scopes (which persist nothing,
and are turned off again), closes every project it opens, and removes its work
folder at the start and at exit. `--mutant` builds a tree copy as `tone_proof`
does, builds the probe over the copy's `app/Sources` and shader, skips H1–H2
(the harness builds the tree's own sources), and reports MUTANT PASS only when
every named row failed and no other scored row did; a core mutant also runs
`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test ungraded` in the copy's core (row
CT).

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `ungraded-ignored` | the option never reaches `layer` | U1 U3 V2 CT |
| `ungraded-tone-only` | the option strips Light's nine and keeps Color's four | U1 CT |
| `view-key-leaks` | a key with no options of its own reads another key's | U2 U3 |
| `luma-weights-swapped` | the kernel weighs blue as red | P3 |
| `level-floors` | the kernel floors Y′·255 instead of rounding it | P1 P2 P4 W1 V1 |
| `no-paused-refresh` | the two commands do not compose the paused frame again | V1 V2 |
| `pending-dropped` | a frame offered while a pass is in flight is dropped, not kept | P7 |

**Its record**: `archive/grading.md`'s GR3 section.

## Road map grading — GR4a and GR4b, adjustment clips and their chrome (`adjustment_proof.py` N1, G1, U1, G2, F1, O1, O2, M1, Q1, M2, E1–E8, C1, A1, R1–R7, I1–I4, S1–S4, Z1 and thirteen mutants; `core/tests/adjustment.rs`; spec §11 GR-6; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** That an adjustment clip (`add_adjustment_clip`) grades
everything drawn behind it and nothing in front, by its colour, its point
filters and its opacity, through the eighth pipeline, and that every rule GR-6
refuses answers in its own sentence. On a four-track stack (a grey and a blue
rectangle behind the clip, a red square in front, a dark background showing
between): N1 a neutral clip changes no byte; G1 brightness +0.2 lifts every
sample behind it by 0.2 and leaves the front square's bytes alone; U1
`render_frame {ungraded}` is N1's frame; G2 exposure +1 is the linear-light
doubling; F1 invert is 255 − v; O1 opacity 0.5 lands halfway and O2 an opacity
action is halfway at its midpoint; M1 an alpha matte window in front of the
clip grades only inside it, and Q1 is M1 as a `prores_422` export at
[320, 180] (the Preview Quality path); M2 the clip's own track made a matte
leaves the frame as if it were not there; E1–E5 are the opaque export rows and
E6–E8 the alpha rows (over a transparent canvas, `hevc_alpha` skipped by name
where the encoder is missing), each decoded middle frame within ±8 of
`render_frame` and its alpha within ±2; C1 a split, a trim to 20 s and a paste
grade the same; A1 reads the ALPHA channel over a transparent canvas (alpha
unchanged, the premultiplied colour graded), which is the one row a blending
pipeline fails; R1–R7 are GR-6's seven sentences, the transition sentence from
all three transition ops, with the project and the last undo step unchanged.

GR4b's rows drive the chrome. I1–I4 perform Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip
(`perform_menu_item`) over a back shape [0, 4 s) and a front shape
[3 s, 4 s): I1 a 0.5–2.5 s range lands one clip on the front track, selected,
the inspector on Clip ▸ Color of `[color, clip]`, one undo step "Add
Adjustment Clip"; I2 the selection's span overlaps the front shape, so a new
front "Adjustment" track takes it and one undo removes both; I3 a matte front
track is never used; I4 the item is disabled ("is disabled here") inside a
nest and on an empty project with no range, and a range there is the
CONTROL. S1–S4 read the inspector's `snapshot_ui` layout dump over an image
clip and an adjustment clip at opacity 0.75: S1 the adjustment clip alone gets
`[color, clip]` and Strength "75%" in an Adjustment section above Light and
Color (a section is named by a row of its own, because a header draws its
title); S2 with the image too, Color has Light and no Strength; S3 the image
alone keeps Picture (CONTROL); S4 the adjustment clip on a matte track shows
"An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." The module docstring
lists every row and its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/adjustment_proof.py                  # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
python3 tools/proof/adjustment_proof.py --only G1,M1     # run and score only these rows (and Z1)
python3 tools/proof/adjustment_proof.py --mutant NAME    # one of the thirteen below
cd core && cargo test --release --test adjustment
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/adjustment/home`), builds every fixture over MCP (shapes
only, and one PNG it renders itself; no media file), performs only Insert ▸
Adjustment Clip (which persists nothing), closes every project it opens, and
removes its work folder at the start and at exit. It launches with three
argument-domain section pins (`video.adjustment` open, `video.light` and
`video.color` closed), which S1 relies on. `--mutant` builds a tree
copy as `tone_proof` does (a core mutant owns the copy's `core/` through
`hevc_alpha_proof.own_core`) and reports MUTANT PASS only when every named row
failed and no other scored row did.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `blending-on` | the adjust pipeline built with fixed-function blending on | A1 |
| `ignores-matte` | the pass's weight drops the matte coverage | M1 Q1 |
| `ignores-opacity` | the pass's weight drops the opacity | O1 O2 |
| `front-graded` | adjustment layers drawn after every other layer | G1 |
| `matte-track-not-inert` | the recipe keeps an adjustment clip on a matte track | M2 |
| `nest-allowed` | `nest` takes an adjustment clip | R1 |
| `overlap-allowed` | the overlap rule's adjustment clause gone | R5 |
| `span-ignores-range` | the In/Out range ignored by the span (the validator shares it) | I1 I4 |
| `matte-front-taken` | a matte front track takes the clip | I3 |
| `enabled-in-nest` | the item enabled with a nest open | I4 |
| `picture-for-adjustment` | Picture offered with an adjustment clip | I1 S1 S2 |
| `strength-in-mixed` | Strength shown for a mixed selection | S2 |
| `adjustment-note-gone` | the adjustment matte note gone | S4 |

**Its record**: `archive/grading.md`'s GR4a and GR4b sections.

## Road map grading — GR5a and GR5b, looks end to end over MCP and in the chrome (`look_proof.py` N0, R1, K1, D1, P1, A0, M1, U2, U1, J1, A1, O1, X1, L1–L5 (GR5a); G1, G2, S1, S2, LM1–LM3, G3, B1–B4 (GR5b); Z1; fourteen mutants; `look_probe.swift`; `core/tests/look.rs`, `core/tests/ungraded.rs`; spec §11 GR-7; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** That `set_video {patch: {look: {kind, amount}}}` reaches
the compositor's step 4d through the recipe's `look` — the core's definition,
baked on the GPU into a 33³ lattice at `texture(2)` — and does what spec §11
GR-7 says, in `render_frame`'s bytes. On a CHART (a grey ramp over six
saturated patches): R1 the amount's range sentence and an unknown kind's,
naming the eight; K1 those eight are the `set_video` catalog clause's, in
order; D1 every look differs from none and from each other by more than 3
levels; P1 a save writes `video.look` only when there is one, as the group's
last key; A0 amount 0 is the neutral bytes; M1 amount 0.5 is the midpoint ±1;
U2 a new kind keeps the amount, and undo and redo; U1 `render_frame
{ungraded}` removes a clip's look and an adjustment clip's; J1 `look: null`
removes it, and an adjustment clip with `vivid` over the chart is the clip's
own `vivid` ±1; A1 an action from amount 0 to 1 is strictly between at
mid-span and the full look at its end. On a grey card O1 holds the order
(tone, then the look): temperature +0.5 under `black_white` stays grey. X1 is
`render_frame` against a `prores_422` export's frame. N0 holds four neutral
frames byte-identical (16 bits a channel) to a control captured on the
UNTOUCHED tree's Release build before any product edit. L1–L5 are
`look_probe.swift`, built by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` (a failed
build is a scored FAILURE) with the tree's `Compositor.metal` compiled by
`makeLibrary(source:)` beside three probe kernels: the 2³ placeholder and a
neutral 33³ bake return all 16,777,216 8-bit colours through `gradeLook`, the
neutral bake's texels are their coordinates, `apply(look:)` and the pair's
offsets 456 / 460 of 464, the eight bakes' milliseconds (a record), and
`teal_orange`'s lattice (its definition read off the core's recipe) is bluer
than red at grey 0.2 and redder than blue at 0.8. The module docstring lists
every row and its fixture.

GR5b's rows are the Color sub-tab's Look section and Clip ▸ Look ▸, on project
MG (MOVIE `{warm, 0.5}` and a grey card IM on one track, a text clip TX, an
adjustment clip AJ). The instance is launched with argument-domain pins —
`video.look` open, `video.light` and `video.color` closed — and
`-RCDevLookGalleryDump`, so each completed thumbnail generation lands in the
work folder as nine PNGs and a manifest. G1 holds each tile's PNG BYTE-identical
to the click's own `set_video` followed by `render_frame {t, max_width: 256}`,
and the nine distinct; G2 that nothing renders while nothing changes, and that
the thumbnail time follows the playhead inside the clip and falls back to its
start outside; S1 that `select_inspector_tab {section: video.look}` shows the
nine names in reading order inside the captured inspector with no layout
problem, and refuses an unknown section naming the held ones; S2 that the
Amount row appears only when every selected clip has a look; LM1–LM3 Clip ▸
Look ▸ over MCP (`perform_menu_item`): a kind keeps each clip's amount, None
removes, undo "Look", disabled for a text clip and enabled for an adjustment
clip (the spec's M1–M3, renamed because GR5a has an M1); G3 a second instance
with the section pinned closed renders nothing. B1–B4 are `look_probe.swift`'s:
the menu's items, tags and place; the validator's checkmarks and dashes; the
model's pure answers; and the section in a headless `ClipPane`, a tile driven
by `sendAction`.

```
python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py                                   # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release; N0 not run
python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py --only D1,M1                      # run and score only these rows
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py capture DIR  # the neutral control, on the untouched tree
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py compare DIR  # every row, and N0 (scored on Release only)
python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py --only G1,G2,G3,S1,S2,LM1,LM2,LM3,B1,B2,B3,B4  # GR5b's rows
python3 tools/proof/look_proof.py --mutant NAME                     # one of the fourteen below
cd core && cargo test --release --test look --test ungraded
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/look/home`), writes its fixtures (the 640×360 chart PNG, a
640×360 grey-128 PNG, a 2 s `testsrc2` H.264 movie) into its work folder,
performs only Clip ▸ Look ▸ items (which persist nothing), closes every project
it opens, and removes its work folder at the start and at exit (the control
folder is not under it).
`--mutant` builds a tree copy as `tone_proof` does, the probe over the copy's
`app/Sources` and its shader, and reports MUTANT PASS only when every named
row failed and no other scored row did; a core mutant also runs `cargo test
--release --no-fail-fast --test look --test ungraded` in the copy's core (row
CT).

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `look-before-tone` | step 4d moved before 4c | O1 |
| `amount-ignored` | `apply(look:)` writes `lookAmount` 1 | M1 A1 U2 L3 |
| `ungraded-keeps-look` | the `ungraded` option keeps the look | U1 CT |
| `adjustment-ignores-look` | `reelcut_adjust_fragment` has no step 4d | J1 |

GR5a's seven are not re-run for GR5b: none of their anchors moved.

GR6a moved one anchor: `kindless-look-kept` now names `evaluate_clip`'s guard
as it calls `lut.rs`'s `evaluates_as_look`. K1 expects the eight and `lut`
(GR-8), and `look_probe.swift`'s B1/B2 and L4 walk `LookKind.builtIns`.

**Its record**: `archive/grading.md`'s GR5a and GR5b sections.

## Road map grading — GR6a and GR6b, `.cube` LUTs end to end over MCP (`lut_proof.py` T0, I1, R1, R2, N1, S1, A1, F1, K1, O1, X1, U1, J1, M1, C1, D1, P1, LG1, LG2, LM4, P2, T1, T2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, Z1 and seventeen mutants; `lut_probe.swift`; `core/tests/cube.rs`, `core/tests/lut.rs`; spec §11 GR-8; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** That a `.cube` file imported over MCP becomes media of
kind `lut` read by the core's parser, and that `set_video {patch: {look:
{kind: "lut", media, amount}}}` draws its table at step 4d, in `render_frame`'s
bytes. T0 (a record, run first on the untouched build) is the log/HDR check of
spec §11 GR-8: one 10-bit ProRes 422 chart re-tagged by stream copy as BT.709,
BT.2020 with the BT.709 transfer, HLG, PQ and untagged — in the ProRes headers
alone and again with the container's `colr` atom — each rendered against the
BT.709 movie tagged the same way. On the CHART: I1 the import's answer and its
note, and a bare `add_media {path, kind: lut}`; R1 every refusal file (size
200, 1D, a domain, an input range, an unknown keyword, a keyword after the
table, a short table, a word, `nan`, a two-number row, no size, a second size,
a short DOMAIN_MAX, binary bytes, 32 MiB + 1) answered as `“NAME.cube” is not a
LUT Reelcut reads: <the core's sentence>.`; R2 the accepted variants; N1 an
identity of 2, 33 and 65 is the neutral bytes; S1 a channel swap of each size
is every sample's (g, b, r) exactly; A1 half of it is the midpoint ±1; F1 three
smooth LUTs (17, 33, 65) within ±2 of ffmpeg's trilinear `lut3d` on the same
PNG (`--lut PATH` adds an owner's file, for GR7's T4); K1 a built-in kind
replacing a LUT and the four look-rule sentences; O1 `add_clip` refused; X1 an
end from LUT A to LUT B at adjacent ids switching at the end, A at 75 %; U1
`ungraded`; J1 an adjustment clip with a LUT; M1 a deleted file draws
ungraded and a relink brings the look back (deleted, not renamed: the
bookmark follows a rename); C1 `consolidate_media`; D1 `remove_media`'s
refusal, `with_clips` and undo; P1 a paste into another project remapping the
base look and an end by path. P2, T1, T2 and P3 are `lut_probe.swift`, built
by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` (a failed build is a scored
FAILURE): the clipboard's media ids, a size-2 asymmetric file through
`LutTextures` read back red fastest, nil for a missing or refused file, and
`RecipeSource.lookURLs(for:)` answering the URLs published under an
instruction's key after it was built.

GR6b adds project LG (the CHART with `{warm, 0.5}`, saved first as LG0 for the
probe) on an instance launched with `look_proof.pins(closed=False,
dump=WORK/dump)`: LG1 each Imported tile's dumped thumbnail is BYTE-identical to
`set_video {look: {kind: lut, media}}` then `render_frame {t, max_width: 256}`;
LG2 the Look section's layout before the import (Import LUT…, no Imported) and
after it (Imported under the nine, swap-33 and invert on one row, Import LUT…
under them, no layout problem); LM4 Clip ▸ Look ▸'s titles before and after,
the listing's checkmarks, performing a LUT item and its undo. P4–P7 are the
probe's: `LookGallery`'s LUT answers, `LookMenuFiller` and the LUT items'
validation and `setLook:`, a headless pane's Imported tiles, outline, summary
and Import LUT… enabling, and `importLUT(from:into:clips:)` as one undo
step that reuses a listed file. The section's summary is drawn by its header,
not a view, so P6 reads it, not LG2. The module docstring lists every row and
its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/lut_proof.py                        # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
python3 tools/proof/lut_proof.py --only S1,X1           # run and score only these rows
python3 tools/proof/lut_proof.py --lut ~/LUTs/Film.cube # F1 with an owner's file too (T4)
python3 tools/proof/lut_proof.py --mutant NAME          # one of the seventeen below
cd core && cargo test --release --test cube --test lut
```

(`tools/proof/work/lut/home`), writes every `.cube` file and its fixtures into

start and at exit. `--mutant` builds a tree copy as `look_proof` does and
reports MUTANT PASS only when every named row failed and no other scored row
did; a core mutant also runs `cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test cube
--test lut` in the copy's core (row CT).

## Road map grading — GR7a, the verdict's figures (`grading_verdict.py` L1–L4, H0, M1, G0, E1, E2, F4, T4, T4c, Z1 and four mutants; `grading_spike.py --tree`, `tree_bench.swift`, KT, TC and one mutant; the `grading` branch)

**What it answers.** Every cap in `archive/grading.md`'s "What it may cost",
measured for the branch against main at the branch point `f407f87` (`BASE`),
and T4's script half — the figures the owner's trial reads. It writes no
verdict: a RECORD row prints `cap held` or `cap missed by X` and never changes
the exit status; a scored row is about the instrument (it read, it built, it
timed, the fixture is what it says).

- **`sizes`** (git only, no app; `work/gr7/sizes.json`): **L1** `git diff
  --numstat BASE HEAD` over `PRODUCT` (`app/Sources`, `core/src`,
  `app/Resources/Shaders`), scored that every root contributes and
  `Compositor.metal` is listed; per root, in total, and per first-parent commit
  in `BASE..HEAD` against its first parent, as a record only (no feature has a
  size budget, root CLAUDE.md); `core/include`'s net printed beside the total.
  **L2** each frozen file's lines at BASE and HEAD and its net against ~50.
  **L3** every changed `.swift`/`.rs` under `app/Sources` or `core/src` that is
  new and over 400 lines, or over 600, with BASE → HEAD; "unpaid" when it grew
  outside `EXEMPT` (`edit.rs`, `ReelOps.swift`) and outside the frozen five
  (listed "frozen: see L2"). **L4** `ClipSubTab`'s cases and each case's
  `…Section(` calls in `ClipPane.makeSections()`, read with `git show` at both
  commits: the sub-tabs added, Color's section count against 4, Picture's
  sections lost and gained.
- **`main-tree make` / `main-tree remove`**: main's comparison build comes only
  from a throwaway `git worktree add --detach work/gr7/main f407f87` and a cold
  `make app` there (bounded at 1500 s, run in the background and waited on
  once); it is removed through `tree_copy.remove_tree` (lsregister `-u`) and
  `git worktree prune`, in a command of its own.
- **`measure`** (release-only kind; `RC_PROOF_APP=release`): every instance a
  fresh `mcp.launch` with `-ReelcutCompositorTiming YES` as a launch argument
  under the scratch `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` `work/gr7/run/home`, stopped by its own
  pid; no menu item is performed. Main's build (`--main`, default the
  worktree's Release binary) is resolved, freshness-checked and launched only
  when M1, E1 or E2 is selected, so `--only H0,F4,T4,Z1` and `--only T4 --lut
  PATH` need no main build. The movie is `work/gr7/media/testsrc2_1080_10s.mp4`
  (ffmpeg `testsrc2` 1920×1080, 30 fps, 10 s, libx264 yuv420p CRF 18, BT.709
  tags); the LUT `work/gr7/luts/gr7-camera-33.cube` is written from textbook
  maths only (33³, red fastest: a smoothstep S-curve mixed at 0.5, gains 1.06 /
  1.0 / 0.92, saturation 1.2 about the Rec. 709 luma, a clamp). Fixtures
  (1920×1080, 30 fps, black): **U** the movie `seconds/10` times on track 1 and
  again on track 2 at scale 0.5, (480, −270); **G** U with every clip at GR0's
  ST tone and `teal_orange` 0.8 and a front adjustment clip over the whole at
  exposure 0.2, vibrance 0.2; **F** 20 s, four full-frame tracks (warm, cool,
  teal_orange, vivid at 0.8 over ST) and a front adjustment clip at exposure
  0.2; **T** the movie at 0. **H0** the host gate (`grading_spike.host_gate`;
  shut → every row a named SKIP, exit 2). **M1** `perform_menu_item {}` with no
  project on main's instance and the branch's: the branch must hold View ▸
  Show Ungraded, View ▸ Scopes, Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip and Clip ▸ Look ▸
  Warm; the leaves added and removed, grouped by their first two path parts,
  against the cap's four. **G0** `render_frame` at 0.5 s of G differs from U by
  more than 8 levels and G holds one adjustment clip. **E1/E2** an h264
  `size: document` export per fresh instance, timed by monotonic wall clock,
  rounds alternating (mU, bU, bG) then (bG, bU, mU) (`run_ab`'s alternation):
  E1 `median(bU)/median(mU) − 1` against 2 %, E2 `median(bG)/median(bU) − 1`
  against 10 %, each series' runs and spread printed, `vm.loadavg` before and
  after each export. **F4** fixture F exported `--rounds` times on the branch,
  the compositor log's 120-frame windows averaged per run (precision's
  `m1_export`), the median average against 8 ms; scored only when 3 exports
  are timed (fewer, as under `--rounds 1`, is a named SKIP and a record). **T4** project T's frame at
  0.5 s through the LUT at amount 1 (`render_frame`) against `ffmpeg -vf
  lut3d=file=…:interp=trilinear` on the neutral frame, decoded to `rgb24`,
  within ±2 at every pixel and channel; **T4c** (CONTROL, scored) the neutral
  frame against ffmpeg's is more than 2 away; `--lut PATH` (expanded and
  resolved, refused unless a file) adds the owner's file as a recorded line,
  ffmpeg reading a safe-named copy so no `:` or `'` in its path reaches the
  filter graph. **Z1** every project closes and no log holds `Reelcut: `.
- **`grading_spike.py --tree`** (`grading_spike/README.md`): V0 main's
  `Compositor.metal` at `f407f87`, VT the tree's own; KT (VT:S1 = V0:S1 within
  1/1023, both sizes) and, with `--measure`, C0, F, T0 and the RECORD **TC**
  (T0 ≤ +0.02 ms at 1080p and +0.06 ms at 4K, plus C0).

```
python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py sizes                               # L1–L4
python3 tools/proof/grading_spike/grading_spike.py --check --tree          # B0–B2, KT
perl -e 'alarm 1500; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py main-tree make   # background; cold build
perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/grading_spike/grading_spike.py --measure --tree
RC_PROOF_APP=release perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py measure --only H0,M1,G0,E1,E2,Z1
RC_PROOF_APP=release perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py measure --only H0,F4,T4,Z1
python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py main-tree remove
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/grading_verdict.py measure --only T4 --lut PATH   # the owner's LUT; no main build
```

**Mutants** (each edits the driver's own behaviour): `sizes --mutant
shader-not-counted` (the shader root dropped from `PRODUCT`) must fail L1;
`measure --mutant lut-not-applied` (the look skipped) T4; `measure --mutant
graded-fixture-ungraded` (every clip's grade and the adjustment clip's colour
dropped, the clip kept) G0; `measure --mutant menus-same-app` (the branch
listing read from main's instance) M1; `grading_spike.py --check --tree
--mutant tree-graded` KT. Each prints `mutant NAME: killed by …` or `SURVIVED`.

**Its record** is `archive/grading.md`'s "GR7a" section, with every figure's
command, host, power and load.

## Road map grading-2 — G2-1, the scopes (`scopes_proof.py` S1–S10, T1, T2, M1–M4, H1–H3, Z1 and eleven mutants; `scopes_probe.swift`; spec §11 GR-10)

**What it answers.** That the parade, the vectorscope and the histogram count
what the person sees, by GR-10's arithmetic and its counting rule, in time;
that the tap and `render_frame` read the same counts; and that the panel's
two slots lay out by the shrink-to-fit rule and persist nothing. S1–S10 are
`scopes_probe.swift`, built by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` with the
tree's own `Waveform.metal` compiled from source (a failed build is a scored
FAILURE of every probe row): S1 the six 75 % cards each in the ONE vectorscope
bin this script computes from the BT.709 matrix, the JSON's targets and the
123.3° skin line; S2 the centring (a grey card, a grey ramp and a
(128, 129, 128)/255 card in bin (128, 128)); S3 a red ramp's parade, at 256
wide (counted globally) and at 1920, 1999 (a last group 7 px across) and 3840
wide (counted per band); S4 a grey
ramp's flat histogram; S5 the histogram's Y′ against the waveform's column
sums and the parade's marks; S6 every kind's counts totalling the pixels at
sizes the threadgroup does not divide; S7 latest-wins with two kinds shown;
S8 the tap's reading of a 64RGBAHalf buffer against `analyze(image:kinds:)`;
S9 the panel's picks, defaults and 360 pt floor in an `EditorViewController`;
S10 `layout(picks:paneHeight:)` for every pick pair. T1 times each scope at
1080p and 4K on GR-10's five fixtures through an IOSurface 64RGBAHalf wrap
(the tap's), each pass alone after a burst of sixteen that brings the GPU's
clock up, median of 10 after 2 warm-ups, and scores the worst 4K figure of
the parade, the vectorscope and the histogram against 1.1 ms, recording the
waveform, the waveform + vectorscope pair and `pmset -g`. T2 (G2-5) builds a
second library from the same shader with its one `bool banded = ` line forced
to `false` and times the tree's parade and that forced-global one back to back
on the five 4K fixtures, as T1 times them; on the fixture where the
forced-global parade is slowest (flat on the M2 Max) it scores the banded time
against 0.75 × the global one, which says the banded path is the one running
(the global parade sits about 1.1 ms, so T1 alone cannot), and a shader with
no such line, or more than one, is a FAILURE. M1–M4 are over MCP
on a 75 % bars PNG: the four sentences and JSON files of `render_frame` with
all four booleans and the vectorscope's bins against this script's from the
PNG's pixels; the top slot's readouts against the waveform JSON; the refusal
of a non-boolean; the panel's layout through `snapshot_ui` (the pickers are
parts, `scopes.<top|bottom>.picker`). H1–H3 are the harness's fifteenth
argument, `seeing=scopes,ramp,top=<kind>,bottom=<kind>`: four pick pairs light
and dark, each byte-identical twice; trace pixels in every body; and the slot
rects the harness prints (`seeing panel …`, `seeing slot …`) at panes of about
460, 755 and 305 pt. The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
python3 tools/proof/scopes_proof.py                  # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
python3 tools/proof/scopes_proof.py --only S1,M1     # run and score only these rows
python3 tools/proof/scopes_proof.py --mutant NAME    # one of the eleven below
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/scopes/home`), writes its fixture (a 640×360 75 % bars
PNG with a white and a black quarter) into its work folder, performs only View
▸ Scopes (which persists nothing, and is turned off again), closes the
project it opens, and removes its work folder at the start and at exit.
`--mutant` builds a tree copy as `seeing_proof` does, builds the probe over the
copy's `app/Sources` and shader, skips H1–H3 (the harness builds the tree's
own sources), and reports MUTANT PASS only when every named row failed and no
other scored row did, but a row the mutant tolerates (`TOLERATED`), which the
MUTANT line names when it failed.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `cb-cr-swapped` | the kernel puts Cr on the Cb axis | S1 M1 |
| `bt601` | the vectorscope's matrix is BT.601's | S1 M1 |
| `bins-edged` | the chroma bins floor instead of round | S1 S2 |
| `vectorscope-global` | every vectorscope pixel adds globally | T1 |
| `histogram-global` | every histogram pixel adds globally | T1 |
| `histogram-luma-601` | the histogram's Y′ takes BT.601's weights | S5 |
| `pick-persisted` | a slot's pick is written to `UserDefaults` | S9 |
| `tap-first-kind-only` | the tap measures only the first shown kind | S7 S8 |
| `slots-not-shrunk` | the slot bodies stay at their preferred heights | S10 |
| `parade-band-misplaced` | the parade's merge puts both bands in the group's first column | S3 |
| `parade-global` | every parade group adds globally (`bool banded = false;`) | T2; T1 tolerated (the forced-global parade measured 1.15 ms at 4K on flat in G2-5, 1.019–1.042 in G2-1, at or over T1's 1.1 ms) |

**Its record**: `archive/grading-2.md`'s G2-1 and G2-5 sections.

## Road map grading-2 — G2-2, the wheels (`wheels_proof.py` N0–N2, L1, G1, Y1, C1, O1, A1, J1, X1, U1, V1, P0, R1, P1–P7, Z1 and twelve mutants; `wheels_probe.swift`; `core/tests/wheels.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v16.rs`; spec §11 GR-11)

**What it answers.** That `video.wheels` changes nothing until set (N0: six
wheel-less frames — the card, the card at exposure +1, an adjustment clip at
exposure +1 over it, the ramp, the ramp under Warm, the movie — byte-identical
at 16 bits to `capture DIR`'s from the untouched tree's Release build); that
each wheel follows GR-11's formula on measured bytes (L1 lift, G1 gain, Y1
gamma along a grey ramp, ±1, the held ends exact); that a push at the rim keeps
a GREY pixel's Y′ (C1, ±1, ±2 for gamma, the only pixel GR-11 claims it for);
that step 4c.1 runs after tone (O1), in an adjustment clip's pass as on a clip
(J1), lerps in an action (A1), reaches an export as `render_frame` draws it
(X1), undoes (U1), leaves under `ungraded` (V1) and pastes (P0); and that the
two refusals speak in their sentences (R1). P1–P7 are `wheels_probe.swift`,
built by `swift_build.build` over `app/Sources` (a failed build is a scored
FAILURE of all seven), on a project of two cards at lift masters 0.2 / −0.2:
P1 a puck drag through `ColorWheelControl.press` / `drag` / `release` in a
headless `ClipPane` wired to a `ProjectDocument`'s live trio is one undo step
"Lift" whose every update sends exactly `{wheels: {lift: {x, y}}}` to both
clips (the masters kept), and the Color sections run Color, Wheels, (Curves since G2-3,) Look; P2
`apply(wheels:)`'s flag; P3 the 512-byte block with `liftX` at 464 and
`wheelsEnabled` at 500; P4 the `◆N` badge; P5 ⌥ at a tenth for the puck and
the strip (no jump on the strip's ⌥ press, and none on a press on its
knob, so a double-click there is the reset alone), and since #272, on a fresh
`ProjectDocument` per case, a double-click OFF the Lift strip's knob is one
undo step back to 0.2 / −0.2, a reset after an edit between the clicks is its
own step, and an identity jump amends no older step (its clicks run 0.1 s apart,
so P5 fails loudly on a host whose double-click interval is under about 0.2 s,
and the detail prints the interval; the strip's other guard, amending only
within that interval of the release, is unmeasured and has no mutant, as the
probe has no clock to age a release); P6 a double-click resets x and y only,
one step "Lift"; P7 10,000 drags past the rim land with
x² + y² ≤ 1 + 1e-9. The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
make app                                                                   # the untouched tree, before any product edit
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/wheels_proof.py capture tools/proof/work/wheels-control
python3 tools/proof/wheels_proof.py                                        # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/wheels_proof.py compare tools/proof/work/wheels-control
python3 tools/proof/wheels_proof.py --mutant NAME                          # one of the twelve below
cd core && cargo test --release --test wheels --test schema_v16
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/wheels/home`), writes its fixtures (`tone_proof.py`'s card,
ramp and `testsrc2` movie) into its work folder, performs no menu item, closes
every project it opens, and removes its work folder at the start and at exit.
`--mutant` builds a tree copy as `tone_proof` does; a core mutant also runs
`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test wheels --test schema_v16 --test
ungraded` in the copy's core (row CT). MUTANT PASS only when every named row
failed and no other scored row did.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `wheels-before-tone` | step 4c.1's block moved before 4c in the layer stage | O1 |
| `gamma-sign` | gamma's exponent `exp2(-gamma)` → `exp2(gamma)` | Y1 C1 (the gamma push lowers its hue's channels) |
| `push-not-luma-neutral` | `wheelOffset` pushes the full hue, not `lookHueChroma` | C1 |
| `flag-ignores-negative` | `wheelsEnabled` only for a positive value | G1 C1 P2 (C1's 240° push is all negative) |
| `circle-check-dropped` | `grade_check.rs`'s circle test never refuses | R1 CT |
| `rim-tolerance-dropped` | the circle test exact, no `WHEEL_RIM_TOLERANCE` | CT (`wheels.rs`'s rim and split cases) |
| `ungraded-misses-wheels` | `ungraded` keeps the wheels | V1 CT |

| `puck-writes-group` | a puck write sends the wheel's master too | P1 |
| `strip-reset-not-amending` | a strip's double-click always applies its reset as its own step (#272) | P5 (case a) |
| `amend-ignores-step` | `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` undoes whatever is last, an edit between the clicks included | P5 (case b) |
| `amend-without-step` | a strip's release keeps its handle even when the gesture made no step | P5 (case c) |

Also moved by G2-2 (the block's 464 → 512): `tone_probe.swift` P3,
`look_probe.swift` L3 (and B4's section list), `clip_inspector2_probe.swift`

## Road map grading-2 — G2-3, the curves (`curves_proof.py` N0–N2, K1, K3, C1, M1, O1, A1–A3, J1, X1, U1, V1, P0, R1, P1–P11, Z1 and ten mutants; `curves_probe.swift`; `core/tests/curves.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v17.rs`; spec §11 GR-12)

**What it answers.** That `video.curves` changes nothing until set (N0: seven
curve-less frames — the card, the card at exposure +1, at lift master 0.5, an
adjustment clip at exposure +1 over it, the ramp, the ramp under Warm, the
movie — byte-identical at 16 bits to `capture DIR`'s from the untouched tree's
Release build), that an identity curve is no curve (N1) and a save writes
only what is not the identity, at the header's format (N2); that a curve hits
its points on a grey ramp (K1: ±1 at 8 bits and within one 10-bit level at 16
bits — the ramp sits over a black 10-bit ProRes clip it covers, so its
`render_frame` is a 16-bit PNG, spec §11 PR-4) and never falls along it (K3,
the overshoot a Catmull–Rom tangent makes); that a red curve moves only red
(C1: R follows the script's own Fritsch–Carlson ±1, G and B within one
half-float step of the uncurved frame at 16 bits), that master runs before a
channel (M1) and after the wheels (O1); that an action lerps per point (A1),
animates from no curve through the identity aligned to the end's x's (A2)
and back to neutral from an end of `[[0,0],[1,1]]` that keeps its key (A3);
that the adjustment pass curves as a clip does (J1), an export matches
`render_frame` (X1), undo works (U1), `ungraded` removes it (V1), it pastes
(P0) and the three refusals speak in their sentences while 0 and 1 pass (R1).
P1–P11 are `curves_probe.swift`, built by `swift_build.build` over
`app/Sources` (a failed build is a scored FAILURE of all eleven), on a project
of two cards with master middles 0.6 and 0.4, the plot driven through
`CurveEditorView.press` / `drag` / `release` / `key` in a headless
`ClipPane` wired to a `ProjectDocument`'s live trio: P1 a press adds one
point on the curve, one live gesture "Curves" sending the whole master list
to both clips, the Color sections running Color, Wheels, Curves, Look; P2 a
drag is one step, held 0.001 inside its neighbour and in 0…1; P3 ⌫ and a
double-click delete, one step each, nothing at two points; P4 the arrows
±0.01 and ⇧ ±0.1, one step each; P5 `apply(curves:)`'s flag (0 for a 3-point
diagonal); P6 `CurveTable.value` against the proof's own Fritsch–Carlson on
200 seeded curves (1e-9) and inside each segment's y span; P7 the strip
`rgba32Float` 1024×1 reading back `CurveTable.strip`, the 2×1 placeholder; P8
the `◆N` badge; P9 the Delete item dead while the plot holds a point (an
editor window of its own); P10 where a write lands inside an action and what
Reset writes there (the identity curve, never `null`); P11 on an identity
channel a click writes nothing, the point waits on y = x bit for bit, and ↑
writes it. The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
make app                                                                   # the untouched tree, before any product edit
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/curves_proof.py capture tools/proof/work/curves-control
python3 tools/proof/curves_proof.py                                        # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/curves_proof.py compare tools/proof/work/curves-control
python3 tools/proof/curves_proof.py --mutant NAME                          # one of the ten below
cd core && cargo test --release --test curves --test schema_v17
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/curves/home`), writes its fixtures (`wheels_proof.py`'s
card, ramp and `testsrc2` movie, and the 10-bit black clip) into its work
folder, performs no menu item, closes every project it opens, and removes its
work folder at the start and at exit. `--mutant` builds a tree copy as
`wheels_proof` does; a core mutant also runs `cargo test --release
--no-fail-fast --test curves --test ungraded` in the copy's core (row CT).
MUTANT PASS only when every named row failed and no other scored row did.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `catmull-rom` | interior tangents the Catmull–Rom chord, no Fritsch–Carlson limit | K3 P6 |
| `master-channel-swapped` | the strip holds master(channel(v)) | M1 |
| `strip-without-half-texel` | the strip sampled at v, not v·(n−1)/n + 0.5/n | C1 |
| `strip-rgba16` | the strip uploaded as `rgba16Float` | P7 |
| `rising-check-dropped` | `check_curves`' rising-x refusal gone | R1 CT |
| `curves-before-wheels` | step 4c.2's block moved before 4c.1 in the layer stage | O1 |
| `ungraded-misses-curves` | `ungraded` keeps the curves | V1 CT |
| `adjust-without-curves` | the adjustment pass has no step 4c.2 | J1 |
| `identity-kept` | `set_video` stores an identity curve | N1 CT |
| `identity-not-aligned` | no identity alignment before an action's lerp | A2 A3 CT |

Also moved by G2-3: `wheels_proof.py` N2 (the header's format version, not
16), `wheels_probe.swift` P1's, `look_probe.swift` B4's and
`clip_inspector2_probe.swift`'s Color section lists, and `grading_spike/tree_bench.swift`, which binds an identity
strip at `texture(3)` (`--tree-base b2fd1f9`).

**Its record**: `archive/grading-2.md`'s G2-3 section.

## Road map grading-2 — G2-4, the qualifier (`qualifier_proof.py` N0–N2, H1, W1, G1, S1, S1b, S2, L1, I1, M1, D1, E1, V1, B1, F1, A1, A2, R1, P0, U1, V2, K1–K8, Z1 and thirteen mutants; `qualifier_probe.swift`; `core/tests/qualifier.rs`, `core/tests/selection.rs`, `core/tests/schema_v18.rs`; spec §11 GR-13)

**What it answers.** That `video.qualifier` changes nothing until set (N0:
six unqualified frames — the card, an adjustment clip at exposure +1 over it,
the same under an alpha matte window, the grey ramp, the hue card graded by an
adjustment clip at saturation −1, the movie — byte-identical at 16 bits to
`capture DIR`'s from the untouched tree's Release build), that an all-null
qualifier is an identity (N1) and a save writes only the ranges set, at the
header's format (N2). The rest read GR-13's ranges off script-written cards
whose every reading the script computes itself from the bytes it wrote (HSV
hue, C = max − min, S = C / max, V, Rec. 709 Y′; Z1 holds the rendered
picture equal to those bytes): HUE (column x hue 360·x/1440, row y saturation
1 − y/359, V 1), HUE50 (the same at V 0.5) and DARK (saturation 1, row y V =
y/359), and the grey ramp. `render_frame {selection}` is the instrument: H1 a
40° hue band selected exactly (255 at d ≤ 20°, 0 at d ≥ 40°, monotone
between) and the graded frame B outside it and graded inside; W1 the wrap at
0 and 350; G1 no grey picked by hue (the chroma guard, on HUE's low rows and
the ramp); S1 a saturation band by row; S1b the same band at V 0.5, which a
chroma reading would put at S 0.8–1; S2 the near-black guard on DARK; L1 a
luma band on the ramp; I1 Invert; M1 a matte window across the band (the
weight is the product); D1 the reading taken before the grade (a hue +120
grade); E1 Show Selection never reaching `render_frame` or an export; V1 the
menu state and tag, off after reopening; B1 black outside the clip's span and
a shape in front left out; F1 `selection` refused by name; A1, A2 actions
(A2 the short way round, 350 → 10 through 0, read at frame 9: a time between
frames renders the frame it snaps to); R1 the three sentences and every bound
accepted; P0 Paste Attributes' rule; U1 undo; V2 `ungraded` keeping the
qualifier. K1–K8 are `qualifier_probe.swift`, built by `swift_build.build`
over `app/Sources` beside a `default.metallib` of the tree's shader and
`Blank.mp4` (K3 renders a frame, and a probe has no app bundle; a failed
build is a scored FAILURE of all eight), on a project of HUE, two adjustment
clips and a red rectangle in front: K1 `QualifierSample` against the script's
readings (1e-9), K2 `ColorQualifier.picked` (widths kept, a grey turning hue
off, pure red's saturation shifted to 0.7–1, luma re-centred inside 0–1, 500
picks every level range inside 0–1 holding the pixel), K3 `QualifierPick.sample`
answering the picture BEHIND the clip, K4 the Color sections, K5 the Hue
checkbox, a strip drag and Reset with their undo names, K6 Show Selection's
key, defaults and rebind, K7 `QualifierUniforms` against the shader's struct,
K8 the `◆N` badge. The module docstring lists every row and its fixture.

```
make app                                                                      # the untouched tree, before any product edit
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/qualifier_proof.py capture tools/proof/work/qualifier-control --app <a copy of the bundle>
python3 tools/proof/qualifier_proof.py                                        # Debug unless RC_PROOF_APP=release
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/qualifier_proof.py compare tools/proof/work/qualifier-control
python3 tools/proof/qualifier_proof.py --mutant NAME                          # one of the thirteen below
cd core && cargo test --release --test qualifier --test selection --test schema_v18
```

It launches its own instance on a scratch socket in a scratch home
(`tools/proof/work/qualifier/home`), writes its fixtures into its work folder,
performs only View ▸ Show Selection (which persists nothing), closes every
project it opens, and removes its work folder at the start and at exit.
`--mutant` builds a tree copy as `curves_proof` does; a core mutant also runs
`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test qualifier --test selection` in the
copy's core (row CT). MUTANT PASS only when every named row failed and no
other scored row did; each names every row it was measured to fail.

| Mutant | Edit | Must fail |
|---|---|---|
| `hue-wrap-broken` | the hue distance without the wrap at 360 | W1 G1 |
| `softness-inside` | the fall-off inside each edge, not outside | H1 S1 S1b L1 W1 D1 |
| `chroma-guard-removed` | no `smoothstep(0.02, 0.06, C)` on the hue range | G1 |
| `saturation-reads-chroma` | the saturation range reads C, not C / max | S1b S2 |
| `near-black-guard-removed` | no `smoothstep(0.03, 0.10, V)` on the saturation | S2 |
| `hue-long-way` | no `align_hue_center` before an action's lerp | A2 CT |
| `q-from-graded` | the weight's `q` read from the graded colour | D1 H1 |
| `matte-not-multiplied` | a qualified pass weighs by `q` instead of `q` × coverage | M1 |
| `selection-reaches-export` | a key with no options reads another key's `selection` | E1 |
| `qualifier-on-any-clip` | `check_qualifier_clip` always passes | R1 CT |
| `paste-keeps-qualifier` | Paste Attributes copies a qualifier onto a picture clip | P0 CT |
