## Road map grading-3 — T3-1, honest sources and step 0 (`hdr_proof.py` H1, H1m, H1a, H1s, H1w, H2–H7, R0, TI, P1–P4, Z1 and twelve mutants; `hdr_probe.swift`, `hdr_pick_probe.swift`, `applelog_writer.swift`; spec §11 GR-15 as amended)

`hdr_proof.py` is curves_proof.py's shape (`capture DIR` | `compare DIR [--only …]` |
`--measure` | `--mutant NAME [--control DIR]`); its header has every row. The control
(`capture tools/proof/work/t3-1/ctl`) was taken on 716720c's Release build before any product
edit; H1's fixtures are copied into `DIR/media/` so every later run draws the same bytes (a
VideoToolbox encode is not repeatable). Fixtures are made once under
`tools/proof/work/hdr/media/`, each kept only when ffprobe reads its tags: the road map's
1024×128 10-bit ramp (grey row 32, chroma row 96) re-tagged by `prores_metadata` + `+write_colr`
(BT.709, untagged, HLG, PQ, BT.2020/BT.709, P3/BT.709), the same through `hevc_videotoolbox` Main
10 (HLG, sRGB, BT.2020/BT.2020-10, P3/sRGB), `testsrc2` H.264, HEVC 8-bit, ProRes 4444, an 8-bit
PNG and a VP9 WebM, `applelog.mov` (`applelog_writer.swift`: a passthrough rewrite with Apple
Log's format-description label, read back), and TI's 4K twins. ffmpeg 9 writes an H.264 colour
tag only with `setparams`; the untagged ProRes keeps the road map's bsf `unknown`, which ffprobe
reads as `gbr/reserved/reserved`.

- **The two probes.** `hdr_pick_probe.swift` is the chroma eyedropper without a window
  (`CanvasEyedropperSession.suppression`, `Exporter.renderFrame`, `color(at:in:canvas:)`), with
  an optional `"png"` written by `FrameWriter.write` and a `"plain"` path (an
  `AVAssetImageGenerator` over the file itself: Apple's reading of its own labels). It uses
  existing API only, so it is built twice: over the tree (or a mutant copy's `app/Sources`) and
  over 716720c's `app/Sources` and `app/Resources` (`git archive` into
  `tools/proof/work/hdr/base-716720c/`, made once), both linking the tree's unchanged core.
  `hdr_probe.swift` (P1–P4) drives `InputConversion` through both readers, `toBT709`, and an
  `InputStage` built from the tree's `Compositor.metal` by `makeLibrary(source:)` on half-rounded
  inputs against the script's oracle.
- **The oracle** (`convert`): the codes ffmpeg reads back from a fixture through the matrix its
  tags name (limited range), then GR-15's formula with its numbers, the matrices derived from
  the published chromaticities and D65. H4 and H5 hold the chroma rows to its envelope — the
  oracle at the fixture's Y′, Cb and Cr codes each moved by −1, 0, +1 (27 evaluations), widened
  by 1 level — because the decoder's chroma reconstruction differs from the sited sample by up
  to one code, which the 1/2.4 encode amplifies near black.
- **The STOP rows.** H1 (12 single-source SDR scenes against the control's PNG bytes and picks)
  and H1m (two mixed projects, tree probe against base probe) stop the phase on any difference;
  neither is ever re-baselined. H1s, H1w and H6 carry their own CONTROL: the base-tree probe must
  fail them.
- **R0** reads only the colour labels of the newest `Screen Recording *.mov` in
  `~/Movies/Reelcut Recordings/`; nothing here records the screen.
- **TI** (`--measure`, Release) launches with `-ReelcutCompositorTiming YES` on an instance per
  twin and reads the timing line's `, N input passes` suffix.

**Its record**: `archive/grading-3.md`'s T3-1 section.

T3-3 (the close) measured two of GR-15's open claims with two more rows, and the product was
not edited for them. **H1a** puts prores4444 | hlg | hevc_alpha | webm on one 640×360 track and
holds the tree probe's PNG bytes and picks at each non-HLG clip to the base tree's (716720c, a
version-18 `base_copy`, as H1m does). Its CONTROL is that the HLG clip's PNGs differ.
`hevc_alpha.mov` is `hevc_videotoolbox` from `bgra`, tagged by `setparams`, because the `-color_*`
flags alone do not stick. **H7** takes `pq_plain.mov` and `pq_hdr10.mov`, libx265 lossless
twins of the ramp, the second with `master-display` and `max-cll` naming a 4,000 cd/m² peak
(not the conversion's own 1,000, so equal renders mean the metadata is ignored, not followed).
Its CONTROL is ffprobe's first-frame side data and that peak, each peak line matched whole. It
holds each grey row to the PQ oracle ±1 and the two renders' PNG bytes equal. Neither row runs
under `capture`, `--measure` or a mutant's default selection. **TI** now also prints each
export's wall time (`time.monotonic()` around `export`), recorded and not scored. Its record:
`archive/grading-3.md`'s T3-3 section.

## Road map grading-3 — T3-2, camera log at step 0 (`log_proof.py` LP1–LP4, L1–L9, Z1 and ten mutants; `log_probe.swift`; `applelog_writer.swift`'s `log2`; spec §11 GR-16)

`log_proof.py` is hdr_proof.py's shape (`capture DIR` | `compare DIR [--only …]` | `--mutant
NAME [--control DIR]`) and imports its decoding helpers; its header has every row. The control
(`capture tools/proof/work/t3-2/ctl`) was taken on e76d827's Release build before any product
edit: L9's references (each fixture alone at 0.5 s) and their media in `DIR/media/`, with
LP1–LP4 and L1–L8 failing there. Fixtures are made once under `tools/proof/work/log/media/`,
written by the script as raw `yuv422p10le` (each curve's encode of a scene-linear ramp on rows
0–63, the makers' 0/18/90 % codes as three patches on rows 64–127, chroma 512) and encoded
`prores_ks` HQ, then re-tagged by stream copy — except the untagged `vlog.mov`, kept as encoded
(the bsf's `unknown` writes 0, which ffprobe reads as `gbr/reserved/reserved`). S-Log3 and V-Log
store the maker's code itself; Apple Log stores P in video range (`64 + 876·P`), GR-16's code
domains. `applelog.mov` and `applelog2.mov` are relabelled by `applelog_writer.swift` (`log2`:
the Apple Log 2 label, primaries removed, as the SDK header asks), the label read back. The two
`.cube` files are channel-distinct (out = 0.7r + 0.2g + 0.1b², g², 0.5b + 0.3r), 17³ and 33³.

- **The oracle** (`log_convert`): the codes ffmpeg reads back, the decoded signal ROUNDED TO
  HALF (step 0 reads an `rgba16Float` source; next to black one half-ulp is a level), then
  GR-16's formula with the makers' constants and Reelcut's display transform, the gamut matrices
  derived from the published chromaticities.
- **L6** compares a reversed clip to the media's conversion of the reverse intermediate's OWN
  codes (Y ±1, widened by 1 — H4's envelope), and to the forward render ±2 only where the
  intermediate's code is the file's within 1: the HEVC Main 10 intermediate moved the ramp's
  first column from 95 to 98 (S-Log3) and 196 to 199 (Apple Log), seven levels through the toe.
- **L9** is the STOP row beside hdr_proof.py's H1 and H1m, which must hold too. hdr_proof's
  `Doc.place` sets an Apple-Log-detected media to None after import, and its base-tree probe
  reads a version-18 copy of each package (`base_copy`, for H1m and H6); a package whose media
  carry `color` is a FAIL.
- **Mutants** build a tree copy (`tree_copy.make_copy`); a core mutant replaces the copy's
  `core` symlink with a copy of the tree's core (no `target/`), so the copy's own make builds it.

**Its record**: `archive/grading-3.md`'s T3-2 section.
